item.title: Saudi Arabia to kick off 2027 Asian Cup against Palestine in Riyadh
item.description: Saudi Arabia will kick off next year's Asian Cup against Palestine in Riyadh on January 7, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) said on Monday after confirming the tournament schedule and venues.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia will kick off next year's Asian Cup against Palestine in Riyadh on January 7, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) said on Monday after confirming the tournament schedule and venues. The 24-team continental championship will run from January 7 to February 5, with the opening match and final both scheduled at Riyadh's King Fahd Sports City Stadium. The tournament remains under scrutiny amid regional [USN:L6N4600NM TEXT:"security concerns"]. AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa earlier said that [USN:L1N4600SG TEXT:"postponement to 2028"] remained a possibility if required. The tournament will feature 51 matches across eight stadiums in three cities: Riyadh (five venues), Jeddah (two) and Al Khobar (one). Defending champions Qatar begin their title defence against Thailand on January 11, while Japan open their campaign against Indonesia the same day. South Korea face Yemen, Australia take on Singapore and Iran meet China in their opening matches. The group stage concludes on January 20, with the knockout rounds beginning on January 22. Saudi Arabia will host the Asian Cup for the first time, seven years before it stages the 2034 World Cup.

item.title: Winless Bucks aren't panicking ahead of matchup with Pacers
item.description: The Milwaukee Bucks will be looking to avoid their first 0-4 start to a season in a half-century when they host the Indiana Pacers on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Milwaukee Bucks will be looking to avoid their first 0-4 start to a season in a half-century when they host the Indiana Pacers on Monday. The last time Milwaukee started a season with four straight defeats was in 1976-77, when the Bucks went on to lose their first five before Larry Costello quit as coach after 18 games (3-15) and was replaced by Don Nelson. Fifty years later, Milwaukee stands on the precipice of unwanted history after slumping to 0-3 with a 127-116 loss to the Philadelphia 76ers on Saturday, but the Bucks aren't panicking just yet. "We won the transition battle, we won the paint battle, we just didn't come up in a couple clutch moments," Milwaukee coach Taylor Jenkins said after losing to the Sixers. "Obviously, our turnovers definitely hurt us, but, man, the competitive spirit was awesome. Obviously, the record is the record, but we're making progress in how we want to play night-in, night-out. "I know the result's going to sting -- we're motivated," Jenkins added. "We want to get our first win. We want to get multiple wins. But we're making progress." Jaime Jaquez Jr. led the Bucks with 21 points in Philadelphia, while Kel'el Ware added 19 points and 13 rebounds off the bench. "You've just got to stay the course," Jaquez said, echoing Jenkins' sentiments. "It's frustrating to drop your first three, but you've still got to balance that with knowing that there's 79 more games. Hopefully, you just take these (losses) and continue to grow. I think we've been growing from the first game even to now, and now it's just got to translate to wins." Indiana can relate to Milwaukee's current plight. Coming off a loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder in Game 7 of the NBA Finals in June 2025, the Pacers started last season with five straight defeats and never recovered. The signs are better this time around. Indiana improved to 2-1 by beating the Brooklyn Nets 136-109 in New York on Sunday, led by Tyrese Haliburton's 24 points and 10 assists. Haliburton, Andrew Nembhard and Obi Toppin hit four 3-pointers each to lead a long-range assault from the Pacers, who went 21 of 43 from distance. But the victory came at a cost, with center Ivica Zubac leaving the arena on crutches after spraining his left ankle in the first quarter. "He's got some swelling," Indiana coach Rick Carlisle said. "It's pretty unlikely he'll play (Monday), but we'll see. Hopefully, it will be a day-to-day thing ... maybe he'll feel a lot better in the morning. It's hard to say. You never know, but it's probably unlikely. I talked to him after the game and he said, 'I'll be all right.' " With guards Ben Sheppard (left meniscus tear) and T.J. McConnell (right hamstring strain) both sidelined and Johnny Furphy still recovering from an ACL tear, the Pacers would be down to 10 healthy standard-contract players if Zubac is out. "With Sheppard being not available right now and T.J. still not back yet, we need everybody," Carlisle said. "Our game isn't going to look exactly the way it's looked in recent months and years. But the important thing is to find a way to hang in and compete and give ourselves a chance." The Bucks have won seven of their past eight meetings against the Pacers, including all four last season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Cavaliers look to sort out finishing issues against trending Wolves
item.description: Building large leads hasn't been a problem for the Cleveland Cavaliers in their first two games. Keeping them, however, is another story.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Building large leads hasn't been a problem for the Cleveland Cavaliers in their first two games. Keeping them, however, is another story. Cleveland hosts the unbeaten Minnesota Timberwolves on Monday, giving it an opportunity to make a better impression on their understandably unnerved fans. Donovan Mitchell scored 22 points as the Cavaliers went up by 22 before holding on for a 125-121 win over the Brooklyn Nets on Saturday. Cleveland didn't trail after the first quarter in its home opener, but allowed the Nets to pull within two in the closing seconds. Two nights earlier, the Cavaliers blew a 29-point lead in a 114-106 season-opening loss at the Philadelphia 76ers in the home debuts of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. "No disrespect to Brooklyn, but it's not Philly, you know what I mean?" Mitchell said. "There are certain things that we were able to get away with because they're young and they're still figuring themselves out. "It sucks that's the way it's been the first two games, but it's something to clean up, something to work on. ... It builds character, too. You find out what you're made of." Mitchell, forward Evan Mobley and center Jarrett Allen have shined thus far, combining to average 63.5 points, 24.0 rebounds and 4.5 blocked shots. They're also shooting a blistering 58.4% from the field. It hasn't been as smooth of a start for Cleveland guard James Harden, who has only made 6 of his 20 field-goal attempts, or forward Peyton Watson. The latter was acquired in an offseason sign-and-trade deal with the Denver Nuggets and is shooting 33.3% from the floor and 22.2% from 3-point range. "Part of this is we're not in elite condition right now, which is kind of normal," Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson said. "It's the second game. Getting in a rhythm, we're not there." Like Philadelphia, the Timberwolves are a legitimate NBA title contender with Anthony Edwards, Rudy Gobert and longtime Charlotte Hornets point guard LaMelo Ball in the fold. They have opened the season with three straight wins for the first time in seven years. Minnesota arrived in Cleveland after winning its 11th consecutive home opener, 117-94 over the Toronto Raptors on Sunday night. Edwards scored a game-high 26 points, and Gobert had eight points and led all players with 13 rebounds. "We're pretty much just being us, following the game plan. The coaches make it easy and we just follow them," said Ball, who is averaging 16.5 points and 5.5 assists on the young season. Foul trouble limited Ball to 15 points and eight assists in 17 minutes Sunday, so he should be fresh for the second half of the Timberwolves' first back-to-back of the season. Minnesota outscored Toronto by 33 points with him on the court. "I just love being here and love doing what I do, playing basketball," Ball said. "Minnesota is amazing, so we're going to keep going." Gobert and Jaden McDaniels were the lone Timberwolves to play more than 28 minutes against Toronto at 31 apiece. Minnesota blew the game open with a 35-15 third quarter, taking advantage of the Raptors being without star Kawhi Leonard, who was sidelined with knee swelling. The Timberwolves were tremendous defensively, keeping Toronto's Scottie Barnes scoreless on 0-of-12 field-goal attempts in 28 minutes. Gobert held starting center Jakob Poeltl to zero points and one rebound. "Our ball contain continues to be strong and our fly-around is really good," Minnesota coach Chris Finch said. "We're kind of stuffing up the paint a little bit, and we did a good job getting out and contesting (3-pointers)." --Field Level Media

item.title: Mindful of the markets, UK's Healey is set to deliver a careful budget
item.description: British finance minister John Healey looks set to announce a cautious first budget this week, prioritising stability in the bond market over the kind of big spending moves that Andy Burnham talked about when he became prime minister.
item.dc:creator: William Schomberg
item.content:encoded: British finance minister John Healey looks set to announce a cautious first budget this week, prioritising stability in the bond market over the kind of big spending moves that Andy Burnham talked about when he became prime minister. When Healey stands up in parliament on Wednesday, he is likely to offer some help to households facing another rise in energy bills and he has hinted that businesses will get "breathing space" from rising costs. But against a backdrop of the US-Israeli war on Iran , which has driven up inflation and taken government bond yields worldwide to multi-decade highs, the [USN:L8N44P1EA TEXT:"former trade union official"] knows he cannot repeat the big spending and tax-raising budgets of his predecessor Rachel Reeves. "If they decide to ramp up spending more than what we're taking in, in a really fiscally tenuous situation, that would be what the market doesn't want to hear," Bryn Jones, head of fixed income at wealth manager Rathbones, said. INVESTORS' FOCUS IS ELSEWHERE Investors have recently been less alarmed by the state of Britain's public finances than they are by those of [USN:L6N45R10C TEXT:"France"], Italy and the US. But four years after a bond market meltdown under former Prime Minister Liz Truss, British gilt yields are still the highest among the Group of Seven rich industrialised nations. Burnham once spoke of his frustration at "being in hock to the bond market" and he promised change when he moved into Downing Street in July. But since then he has told [USN:L8N45I08M TEXT:"investors"] that he understands the reality of the public finances. "Some might say that Burnham is very much in hock to the bond market at the moment," Allan Monks, a senior economist at J.P.Morgan, said. The new prime minister's big ambitions - including an increase in public housebuilding, taking defence spending to 3% of economic output and greater state ownership of public services - will probably be delayed. Analysts also expect a decision on whether to increase spending to offset the [USN:L8N45V18B TEXT:"impact of higher inflation"] on government departments to be postponed. Still, Healey's [USN:L1N4610D3 TEXT:"margin for error"] in hitting his fiscal targets will be narrow. Britain's public debt [USN:L8N46708T TEXT:"hit £3 trillion"] ($4 trillion) for the first time in September and the cost of servicing it has risen. Healey - who earlier this year quit as former Prime Minister Keir Starmer's defence minister in a row over funding - may try to cover a near-term shortfall in Britain's spending plans for the armed forces. The main tax-raising measure in the budget is expected to be an increase in a levy on [USN:L8N4610PT TEXT:"the profits of banks"]. The Treasury has already announced some other measures, including more than [USN:L6N46A01K TEXT:"£20 billion extra"] in support for investment in artificial intelligence, defence and green energy over a roughly five-year period. It has said [USN:L8N4691W8 TEXT:"mayors in England"] will be given new funding and powers under a push for more devolution, while around £600 million [USN:L8N4691RM TEXT:"will be allocated"] to defend against health and security threats from artificial intelligence. Analysts expect the big decisions of the Burnham government will have to wait for an official spending review next year by which time the conflict in the Gulf may have eased, bringing down borrowing costs. A reset of [USN:L2N46B01B TEXT:"Britain post-Brexit ties"] with the European Union following a UK-EU summit in November might also have improved the outlook by then. "This budget will largely be a stopgap that will tide the government over before a more significant policy overhaul in 2027," Alexander Harvey, UK economist at Oxford Economics, said. ($1 = 0.7478 pounds)

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS L'Europe vue sur un rebond, résultats et banques centrales au menu de la semaine
item.description: Les principales Bourses européennes sont attendues sur un rebond lundi à l'ouverture, la baisse des cours du pétrole offrant un certain répit au début d'une semaine chargée avec une nouvelle vague de résultats d'entreprises et les décisions de politique monétaire des principales banques centrales.
item.dc:creator: Diana Mandia
item.content:encoded: Les principales Bourses européennes sont attendues sur un rebond lundi à l'ouverture, la baisse des cours du pétrole offrant un certain répit au début d'une semaine chargée avec une nouvelle vague de résultats d'entreprises et les décisions de politique monétaire des principales banques centrales. D'après les premières indications disponibles, le CAC 40 parisien (.FCHI) pourrait gagner 0,39% à l'ouverture. Les contrats à terme signalent une hausse de 0,25% pour le Dax à Francfort (.GDAXI) , de 0,36% pour le FTSE à Londres (.FTSE) et de 0,22% pour le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) . Les cours du brut reculent légèrement après avoir progressé de plus de 6% la semaine dernière et atteint leur plus haut niveau depuis le 29 avril dernier, alors que les attaques des Houthis du Yémen en Arabie saoudite ont ravivé les craintes de nouvelles perturbations de l'approvisionnement Les rebelles yéménites, alliés de l'Iran, ont déclaré lundi avoir ciblé les stations de pompage de l'oléoduc Est-Ouest saoudien ainsi que l'aéroport de Ryad, mais les informations selon lesquelles des médiateurs qataris se trouvaient dimanche à Téhéran ont apaisé dans une certaine mesure la pression. Des hauts responsables des pays signataires de l'"accord de La Mecque" – l'Arabie saoudite, la Turquie et le Pakistan – doivent par ailleurs rencontrer lundi dans la capitale iranienne des responsables du régime pour discuter de la coordination régionale, [USN:L5N46C04R TEXT:"ont indiqué"] deux sources proches du dossier. L'inflation provoquée par le conflit est plus que jamais présente dans l'esprit des investisseurs en cette semaine de décisions de politique monétaire des banques centrales, notamment celle de la Réserve fédérale américaine (Fed) mercredi et celle de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE) jeudi. Ces deux institutions devraient maintenir leurs taux inchangés cette fois-ci, mais les marchés anticipent de nouvelles hausses en décembre, les prix restant bien au-dessus de leurs objectifs. "Le message principal que font passer les banques centrales mondiales, confrontées aux surprises macroéconomiques de cette année, est qu'un cycle de hausse des taux relativement modéré est en cours", déclare Bruce Kasman, économiste chez JPMorgan. Également au programme de la semaine, les banques centrales du Canada et de Nouvelle-Zélande devraient en revanche annoncer un relèvement de leurs taux respectifs, tandis que la Banque du Japon (BoJ) est attendue sur un statu quo. Les investissements dans l'intelligence artificielle (IA) devraient en outre continuer à occuper les investisseurs, avec la publication cette semaine des résultats trimestriels d'Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , de Microsoft (MSFT.O) et d'Amazon (AMZN.O) , alors que les doutes quant à la pérennité du rallye qui a connu le secteur refont surface. Le calendrier des résultats est également très chargé en Europe, avec, par exemple, TotalEnergies (TTEF.PA) , Danone (DANO.PA) ou Renault (RENA.PA) au programme, sans parler des banques françaises BNP Paribas <BNPP. PA>, Société Générale (SOGN.PA) et Crédit Agricole (CAGR.PA) , qui viennent de traverser une semaine difficile en Bourse dans un contexte de prudence vis-à-vis des actifs de la deuxième économie de la zone euro, dont les rendements souverains ont récemment atteint de nouveaux sommets. L'agence de notation Moody's [USN:L8N46923J TEXT:"a toutefois"] décidé vendredi de maintenir la note de crédit de la France à "Aa3", assortie d'une perspective négative, alors que la plupart des analystes s'attendaient à une dégradation à "A1". LES VALEURS A SUIVRE : [USN:L8N4691Y8] A WALL STREET La Bourse de New York a fini en baisse vendredi, au terme d'une semaine mouvementée pour le secteur de l'IA, alors que les investisseurs ont désormais les yeux rivés sur de nouveaux résultats d'entreprises et la décision prochaine de la Fed. L'indice Dow Jones (.DJI) a cédé 1,23%, le S&P-500 (.SPX) , plus large, a perdu 0,51%, et le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) , riche en valeurs technologiques, a reculé 0,20%. EN ASIE L'indice Nikkei (.N225) à Tokyo a fini en baisse de 0,8%, les valeurs du secteur des semi-conducteurs ayant reculé dans le sillage de Wall Street vendredi. Les Bourses chinoises sont également dans le rouge, affectées par les pertes du secteur technologique et alors que le cinquième plénum du Comité central du parti communiste s'ouvre ce lundi à Pékin. Le marché chinois est désormais en baisse depuis 11 semaines consécutives, sur fond d'inquiétudes concernant la demande intérieure, alors même que les exportations restent solides. L'indice CSI 300 (.CSI300) des grandes capitalisations cède 0,27% et le SSE Composite (.SSEC) de Shanghaï perd 0,01%. La Bourse de Hong Kong (.HSI) gagne en revanche 0,55%. TAUX / CHANGES Le rendement des Treasuries à dix ans perd 2 points de base à 4,9677%, tandis que celui du titre à deux ans abandonne 1,5 point de base à 4,6666%. Jeudi, l'obligation de référence a connu sa plus forte hausse quotidienne depuis près de quatre ans, en lien avec les inquiétudes concernant le caractère durable du redressement des actions liées à l'IA, qui ont attiré les investisseurs vers les actifs refuge. Sur le marché des changes, le dollar perd 0,12% face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) , tandis que l'euro gagne 0,12% à 1,1216 dollar . PÉTROLE Le Brent perd 1,65% à 114,79 dollars le baril et le brut léger américain (West Texas Intermediate, WTI) perd 2,04% à 101,16 dollars. Le directeur de l'Agence internationale de l'énergie a par ailleurs déclaré lundi qu'il ne s'attendait pas à ce que les marchés de l'énergie reviennent en 2027 à la situation qui prévalait avant la guerre en Iran, qui a débuté fin février. item.title: Spain's Moeve 'fully focused' on transformation strategy after Galp talks collapse
item.description: The CEO of Spanish energy firm Moeve said on Monday the company was "fully focused" on its strategic transformation towards low-carbon businesses after talks with Portugal's Galp over a potential combination of downstream businesses collapsed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The CEO of Spanish energy firm Moeve said on Monday the company was "fully focused" on its strategic transformation towards low-carbon businesses after talks with Portugal's Galp (GALP.LS) over a potential combination of downstream businesses collapsed. The strategy "has always been a standalone strategy. The potential downstream combination with Galp represented an opportunity to accelerate value creation, but it was never a condition for its delivery," Maarten Wetselaar said in a statement. "We remain fully focused on executing our transformation," the chief executive added. Moeve, owned by Abu Dhabi fund Mubadala and US-based private equity firm the Carlyle Group (CG.O) , was formerly known as Cepsa. It rebranded in 2024 to reflect its shift towards low-carbon businesses under an €8 billion ($8.98 billion) plan. It has sold most of its oil production assets since 2022, including operations in Abu Dhabi and South America. ($1 = 0.8911 euros)

item.title: CITAS Líderes mundiales felicitan al presidente de Brasil, Lula, por su reelección
item.description: Líderes mundiales celebraron la victoria del presidente de Brasil, el izquierdista Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, en la segunda vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales del domingo, en la que derrotó al senador derechista Flávio Bolsonaro y obtuvo un cuarto mandato no consecutivo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Líderes mundiales celebraron la victoria del presidente de Brasil, el izquierdista Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, en la segunda vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales del domingo, en la que derrotó al senador derechista Flávio Bolsonaro y obtuvo un cuarto mandato no consecutivo. Estas son algunas de las reacciones: PRESIDENTA DE LA COMISIÓN EUROPEA, URSULA VON DER LEYEN: "Felicitaciones a mi amigo (Lula) por su victoria electoral. La democracia y el multilateralismo han triunfado en Brasil". "La alianza entre Europa y Brasil está floreciendo. Seguiremos a su lado en los próximos años". "Juntos seguiremos trabajando estrechamente por un comercio libre y abierto. Por un orden mundial basado en reglas. Y por objetivos ambiciosos en materia climática". PRESIDENTE DEL CONSEJO EUROPEO, ANTÓNIO COSTA: "El pueblo brasileño ha hablado. ¡Felicitaciones por su reelección, presidente (Lula)!" "La Unión Europea y Brasil son socios sólidos". "Anoche hablé por teléfono con el presidente Lula para felicitarlo por su reelección. Seguiremos trabajando juntos para estrechar nuestros lazos, afrontar los desafíos globales y construir un mundo más pacífico y próspero". PRIMER MINISTRO DE CANADÁ, MARK CARNEY: "La relación entre Canadá y Brasil ha florecido gracias a nuestra colaboración". "Aprovechemos esta oportunidad para fortalecerla aún más, juntos, para crear nuevas e importantes oportunidades comerciales, proteger el medioambiente y generar mayor prosperidad para nuestros dos pueblos". PRESIDENTA DE PERÚ, KEIKO FUJIMORI: "Felicito al presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva por su reelección y saludo al pueblo brasileño por esta jornada democrática". PRESIDENTE DE ECUADOR, DANIEL NOBOA: "Nuestra región tiene enemigos comunes, desafíos compartidos y mucho por ganar cuando trabajamos juntos". PRESIDENTE DE CHILE, JOSÉ ANTONIO KAST: "Acabo de conversar con el Presidente de Brasil, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva y lo he felicitado por el resultado de la elección". "Chile y Brasil tienen mucho futuro en común y seguiremos trabajando por una agenda que potencie las relaciones entre nuestros países en integración económica y combate al crimen organizado en la región". PRESIDENTA DE MÉXICO, CLAUDIA SHEINBAUM: "Viva la democracia, ganó el pueblo de Brasil. ¡Felicidades presidente Lula!" PRESIDENTE DE PARAGUAY, SANTIAGO PEÑA: "Saludo al pueblo brasileño por esta gran jornada democrática". "El Paraguay y Brasil comparten una agenda común de integración y desarrollo. Seguiremos trabajando juntos por el bienestar de nuestra gente". PRESIDENTE DE URUGUAY, YAMANDÚ ORSI: "Acabo de comunicarme con el presidente electo de Brasil, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, un amigo". "Lo felicité por el triunfo y por la fiesta democrática que representa un proceso electoral". PRESIDENTE DE BOLIVIA, RODRIGO PAZ: "Bolivia y Brasil somos países vecinos y hermanos, unidos por una historia y desafíos comunes". "Seguiremos trabajando juntos para fortalecer nuestra relación y generar más oportunidades para nuestras naciones". PRESIDENTE DE CUBA, MIGUEL DÍAZ-CANEL: "Estimado hermano (Lula), te felicito en nombre del gobierno y pueblo cubanos por esta victoria histórica que garantiza la continuidad del camino de paz, soberanía y justicia social emprendido por el pueblo brasileño bajo tu liderazgo". PRESIDENTE DE PANAMÁ, JOSÉ RAÚL MULINO: "Felicito al pueblo brasileño por esta jornada democrática y especialmente al Presidente (Lula) por la victoria! Seguiremos trabajando juntos por nuestros países".

item.title: Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi acquitted in defamation case, TV channels report
item.description: Rahul Gandhi, the leader of India's main opposition Congress party, was acquitted in a defamation case by a local court on Monday, TV channels said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rahul Gandhi, the leader of India's main opposition Congress party, was acquitted in a defamation case by a local court on Monday, TV channels said. The acquittal comes at a time when Gandhi is leading a [USN:L4N45X03I TEXT:"united opposition campaign"] against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Chief Election Commissioner over a [USN:L4N45K0E7 TEXT:"controversial revision"] of voter lists Gandhi, 56, the scion of the Nehru-Gandhi political dynasty and top leader of Congress, which has mostly ruled India since it gained independence from the British, was in court in the northern town of Sultanpur when the verdict was pronounced His supporters burst crackers, beat drums and waved party flags as he left the court after the acquittal, images on TV showed Gandhi was accused of calling India's powerful Home Minister Amit Shah, who was then head of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), a "murder accused", during a state election campaign speech in 2018 The case was filed in Sultanpur town of Uttar Pradesh state by a BJP member and the verdict was announced on Monday A court in Modi's home state of Gujarat had convicted Gandhi in 2023 in a separate defamation case over a "Modi surname" remark, which [USN:P8N38K0ED TEXT:"briefly cost him his seat"] in parliament

item.title: Los países del Pacto de La Meca se reunirán con dirigentes iraníes en Teherán el lunes
item.description: Altos cargos de los países del Pacto de La Meca —Arabia Saudita, Turquía y Pakistán— se reunirán el lunes en Teherán con los dirigentes iraníes, en lo que supondrá su primer contacto de alto nivel desde que el reino se convirtiera en un punto de presión en el conflicto más amplio con Irán.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Mills, Ariba Shahid
item.content:encoded: Altos cargos de los países del Pacto de La Meca —Arabia Saudita, Turquía y Pakistán— se reunirán el lunes en Teherán con los dirigentes iraníes, en lo que supondrá su primer contacto de alto nivel desde que el reino se convirtiera en un punto de presión en el conflicto más amplio con Irán. Arabia Saudita estará representada por el ministro de Defensa, el príncipe Khalid bin Salman; Pakistán, por el jefe del Ejército, el mariscal de campo Asim Munir; y Turquía, por el jefe de los servicios de inteligencia, Ibrahim Kalin, informaron fuentes oficiales sauditas e iraníes. Las conversaciones se producen en un momento en que los ataques de los hutíes yemeníes, alineados con Irán, se han intensificado en las últimas semanas y la retórica entre Washington y Teherán se ha vuelto más acalorada. Ambos países también han elaborado planes para reanudar la guerra a gran escala, posiblemente tras las elecciones de mitad de mandato de EEUU del 3 de noviembre. Las conversaciones previstas para el lunes supondrían el primer contacto de alto nivel entre Irán y todos los miembros del bloque de tres naciones desde que Arabia Saudita se vio más profundamente involucrada en el conflicto. En virtud del Acuerdo Conjunto de Defensa de La Meca, firmado en agosto, un ataque armado contra uno de los miembros se considera un ataque contra todos. Los mediadores qataríes se reunieron el domingo en Teherán con representantes iraníes en un intento por rebajar las tensiones regionales, informó Reuters. Qatar lleva meses desempeñando un papel mediador clave entre Teherán y Washington. Un alto cargo iraní dijo que la reunión fue impulsada por Pakistán durante la visita de Munir a Teherán la semana pasada, en la que se reunió con el presidente iraní, Masud Pezeshkian, y otros altos cargos. Según medios de comunicación iraníes, durante la visita los dirigentes iraníes le comunicaron que no habría conversaciones con Washington hasta que se cumplieran las exigencias de Teherán. Anteriores esfuerzos de mediación en los que participaron tanto Pakistán como Qatar contribuyeron a alcanzar un acuerdo de paz provisional en junio, pero el acuerdo se desmoronó rápidamente al reanudarse los combates entre Irán y Estados Unidos semanas más tarde. El subsecretario del máximo órgano de seguridad de Irán, Ali Baqeri-Kani, declaró a la televisión estatal que el ministro de Defensa saudita, el príncipe Khalid, el pakistaní Munir y el jefe de los servicios de inteligencia turcos, Ibrahim Kalin, visitarían Teherán para mantener consultas con el Consejo Supremo de Seguridad Nacional de Irán sobre la seguridad regional. El viceministro saudita de Diplomacia Pública, Rayed Krimly, afirmó que la reunión forma parte de los esfuerzos continuos de los países del Pacto de La Meca para rebajar la tensión de la crisis actual, promover soluciones diplomáticas y apoyar los esfuerzos de mediación liderados por Qatar y Pakistán. "La visita también subraya el papel fundamental de los Estados del Pacto de La Meca a la hora de fomentar la seguridad y la estabilidad regionales, así como su compromiso de colaborar con todas las naciones de la región para alcanzar este objetivo", publicó Krimly en la red social X. El departamento de comunicación del ejército pakistaní y el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Turquía no respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. AUMENTAN LAS TENSIONES Arabia Saudita interceptó el domingo otra oleada de misiles y drones, mientras los combates con los hutíes continuaban sin tregua. Los ministros de los países del Pacto de La Meca celebraron una reunión de emergencia en Riad a principios de este mes y acordaron garantizar el "rápido despliegue" de fuerzas y capacidades militares en Arabia Saudita. Los ataques hutíes se han convertido en un elemento cada vez más desestabilizador en la ofensiva estadounidense-israelí contra Irán, lo que ha convertido a Arabia Saudita, aliada de EEUU, en un punto de presión en el contexto más amplio de la guerra. Las tensiones entre Washington y Teherán se han agudizado en los últimos días. El presidente Donald Trump dijo el viernes que EEUU podría llevar a cabo otra operación militar contra Irán, y los líderes iraníes han declarado que una nueva campaña militar estadounidense recibiría una respuesta más contundente que antes. Autoridades de seguridad iraníes han declarado a Reuters que Teherán ha elaborado planes detallados para atacar los cables submarinos del golfo Pérsico si Estados Unidos e Israel vuelven a atacar. Un informe de los servicios de inteligencia estadounidenses de esta semana advertía de que los complots iraníes contra personal estadounidense habían alcanzado "fases avanzadas". La guerra, que ya dura casi ocho meses, ha lastrado los índices de popularidad del presidente Donald Trump de cara a las elecciones de mitad de mandato. El primer artículo del acuerdo de La Meca establece que las partes utilizarán "todos los medios necesarios" para eliminar las amenazas a la integridad territorial, la soberanía o las fronteras internacionalmente reconocidas de cada una de ellas, según un texto al que tuvo acceso Reuters. Los trámites del Parlamento turco para ratificar el acuerdo comenzaron la semana pasada y aún están en curso, mientras que Pakistán aprobó el pacto la semana pasada.

item.title: La AIE no espera que el precio de la energía vuelva a los niveles anteriores a la guerra en 2027
item.description: El director de la Agencia Internacional de la Energía dijo el lunes que no espera que los mercados energéticos vuelvan en 2027 a la situación en la que se encontraban antes de la guerra de Irán, que comenzó a finales de febrero.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El director de la Agencia Internacional de la Energía dijo el lunes que no espera que los mercados energéticos vuelvan en 2027 a la situación en la que se encontraban antes de la guerra de Irán, que comenzó a finales de febrero. El conflicto ha provocado una fuerte contracción en un mercado para el que se había previsto un excedente este año, lo que ha alterado significativamente los flujos energéticos mundiales y ha impulsado al alza los precios de referencia del petróleo y de los productos refinados. "Me temo que no veo ninguna vía creíble para que los mercados vuelvan el año que viene a la situación en la que nos encontrábamos antes de que comenzara esta guerra", dijo el director ejecutivo de la AIE, Fatih Birol, en la conferencia de la Semana Internacional de la Energía de Singapur. "Por lo tanto, todos debemos prepararnos, dando prioridad absoluta a la seguridad energética en nuestros gobiernos y en el mundo empresarial, pero sin olvidar cuál será el próximo capítulo para los países y las empresas que hoy se encuentran aquí", añadió. Los nuevos ataques hutíes en Arabia Saudita hicieron que los futuros del crudo Brent alcanzaran el viernes los 117 dólares por barril, el nivel más alto en casi seis meses. El contrato se moderó el lunes, pero seguía cotizando un 59% por encima de su nivel anterior a la guerra. "Los precios del petróleo rondan los 120 dólares por barril y los de los productos derivados son incluso mucho más elevados", dijo Birol en una rueda de prensa. Se negó a ofrecer una previsión sobre los precios del petróleo, pero añadió: "Puedo decirles que el precio actual del petróleo, para algunos países, por ejemplo en Europa, quizá no sea tan elevado y resulte asequible. Pero en muchas partes del mundo, tener precios del petróleo de casi 120 dólares está teniendo un impacto importante en los déficits comerciales". PREOCUPACIONES INVERNALES Birol también expresó su preocupación por la demanda invernal de algunos combustibles, especialmente el diésel, que se utiliza en algunas zonas de Occidente para la calefacción. "Además, me preocupan los productos refinados porque estamos entrando en… la temporada de invierno. En algunas partes del mundo, donde la demanda de diésel suele ser elevada, varias refinerías se encuentran en periodo de mantenimiento". "En Europa nos enfrentamos a un invierno difícil, ya que los países europeos han decidido recortar las importaciones de gas de Rusia y, sumado al problema adicional que surge ahora de la guerra de Irán —es decir, que Qatar y Emiratos Árabes Unidos no pueden exportar gas como antes—, esto ejercerá una presión significativa sobre los mercados del gas". Birol prevé un "fuerte repunte" del sector nuclear como consecuencia de la crisis actual. La reciente encuesta de la AIE reveló que hay 90 gigavatios de centrales nucleares en construcción, lo que supone la cifra más alta de las últimas cuatro décadas, añadió.

item.title: Brazil heads back to the future as Flavio Bolsonaro refuses to recognize Lula win
item.description: Right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has followed his imprisoned father's lead by refusing to concede defeat to leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who won a historic fourth term in Sunday's presidential election.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Griffin, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
item.content:encoded: Brazilian right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has followed his imprisoned father's lead by refusing to concede defeat to leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who won a historic fourth term in [USN:L2N46B01X TEXT:"Sunday's presidential election."] Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, called into question a late-Sunday decision by a Lula-appointed Supreme Court justice that extended voting by two hours over alleged voter transport irregularities. He said he would ask for the result to be annulled. "It is impossible to recognize the election results, given the circumstances under which things unfolded," Bolsonaro told journalists. Yet the scale of the loss, with Bolsonaro trailing Lula by over 4 million votes, makes it unlikely his efforts to annul the vote will succeed, analysts said. His petition is also undermined by the fact that his campaign also sought a voting extension due to heavy rains in the conservative-leaning south. Still, Bolsonaro's refusal to concede could spark a wave of protests in a country where faith in the electoral system, and in judicial independence, has been strained in recent years, observers say. Jair Bolsonaro plunged Brazil into a deep democratic crisis after the election in 2022, when his supporters stormed government buildings in protest against the result. He later received a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup. LULA DEFIES EXPECTATIONS Lula's victory defied polls, precedent and global anti-incumbent sentiment to put the brakes on a wave of right-wing election victories across Latin America. The result will disappoint the administration of US President Donald Trump, whose State Department [USN:L1N4650X8 TEXT:"led a campaign"] to return the Bolsonaros to power. Financial markets also expressed initial concerns at the shock result. A Tokyo-listed exchange-traded fund tracking Brazil's Bovespa index (1325.T) dived nearly 15% in Asia trade on news of Lula's victory, while analysts expected the Brazilian real to fall against the US dollar. Lula had trailed Bolsonaro in the first round, but managed to convince voters to come out for him in the runoff. Speaking at a hotel in São Paulo late on Sunday, he took a conciliatory tone. "I won’t speak of national unity, because that doesn’t always fit the reality of this country. No one is obliged to like the elected president, but he was put in place to govern for everyone," Lula said. 'COUNTLESS' CHALLENGES During the campaign, Lula pointed to his track record of cutting poverty and inequality while also highlighting record low unemployment, illiteracy and deforestation, but his fourth term may prove challenging. He will have to work alongside a Congress packed full of Bolsonaro allies after a surge of right-wing voting recast Brazil's legislature in favor of the president's enemies. “The challenges are countless,” said Carlos Melo, a political science professor at Insper in São Paulo.

item.title: Vietnam's first chip plant unlikely to meet 2027 target, sources say no deal yet with ASML
item.description: Vietnam is unlikely to meet a 2027 target for its first semiconductor plant to embark on a trial production run, with people saying that a deal to buy chipmaking equipment from ASML has yet to be reached.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Guarascio, Khanh Vu, Toby Sterling
item.content:encoded: Vietnam is unlikely to meet a 2027 target for its first semiconductor plant to embark on a trial production run, with people saying that a deal to buy chipmaking equipment from ASML (ASML.AS) has yet to be reached. The site of the plant on the outskirts of Hanoi remains covered in wild vegetation, a Reuters visit there last week showed. Satellite images taken in January by Planet Labs PBC and by Airbus in October also confirm that no buildings have been constructed. A person with direct knowledge of the project said the 2027 target would probably not be achieved due to delays stemming from developer Viettel's lack of experience in building chip factories and administrative hurdles in quickly securing government funding. The government-mandated project is ongoing but the timeline is unclear, said the person, who was not authorised to speak to media and declined to be identified. The project's lack of progress and Viettel's talks with the Dutch equipment maker are being reported here for the first time. Viettel, a military-run telecoms and defence group, said in a statement to Reuters that the project was "progressing in line with the established plan and schedule." "Project activities are being carried out in phases, in accordance with the project's technical and implementation requirements. We will provide further updates at an appropriate time," it said. Vietnam's finance ministry did not respond to requests for comment. A representative for ASML declined to comment on the talks with Viettel. The project is part of the ruling Communist Party's plans for Vietnam to move up the semiconductor value chain. It wants the country to become a high-income economy by 2045, with growth of at least 10% through 2030. TALKS WITH ASML SAID TO BE UNDERWAY FOR MONTHS Viettel, which [USN:L1N3YH04J TEXT:"broke ground"] on the site in January, said at the time it wanted the plant to be fully operational by 2030 and that it intended to supply its chips to the aerospace, telecom and auto sectors. Talks with ASML have been underway for months, said three separate people familiar with the matter, who declined to be identified because the discussions were private. The talks have covered the purchase of a deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography machine, needed to print circuitry patterns onto silicon wafers, two of the people said. Reuters was not able to learn why no agreement has been reached or which type of DUV machine was under discussion, which would indicate whether the sale could be subject to Dutch export controls and would help in understanding potential costs. Authorities have estimated the cost of the plant at about $1.3 billion. ASML said this month it may [USN:L6N4610HN TEXT:"not fully meet demand"] for its most advanced machines over the next two years because of the AI boom. Supply constraints for older-generation equipment are expected to be less severe. It holds a monopoly on the most sophisticated extreme ultraviolet (EUV) machines, and is the biggest provider of immersion DUV systems, a market where it competes with Nikon (7731.T) of Japan. SETTING SIGHTS HIGH Viettel said in a January presentation that it planned to produce semiconductors using 32-nanometre technology, an ambitious starting point for a newcomer to chip manufacturing. By comparison, [USN:L1N41T07H TEXT:"Tata Electronics has said"] its $11 billion project in Gujarat, developed with Taiwan's PSMC (6770.TW) , will begin with 55- and 90-nanometre processes before adding more advanced 28-nanometre production. The reference to 32-nanometre was subsequently removed from Viettel's website. Viettel has also not disclosed if it is partnering up with an established chip manufacturer to provide technology and expertise. Efforts by Vietnam's government to attract foreign investors to build a chip manufacturing facility in Vietnam have been unsuccessful, according to industry sources. The country is, however, a fast-growing hub for the less capital-intensive sector of semiconductor assembling, testing and packaging (ATP). Intel (INTC.O) , Amkor Technology (AMKR.O) and Hana Micron (067310.KQ) operate large ATP factories in Vietnam, while Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) is [USN:L6N41X0BE TEXT:"planning a chip-testing facility."] ASML suppliers also have operations in Vietnam, including Coherent and VDL Enabling Technologies Group, though their local factories primarily serve customers other than ASML.

item.title: Eurazeo nomme Christophe Bavière président du directoire
item.description: Eurazeo a annoncé lundi la nomination de Christophe Bavière comme président unique du directoire du groupe d'investissement français, dans la perspective de l’échéance des mandats en cours, le 5 février 2027.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Eurazeo (EURA.PA) a annoncé lundi la nomination de Christophe Bavière comme président unique du directoire du groupe d'investissement français, dans la perspective de l’échéance des mandats en cours, le 5 février 2027. "Je tiens (...) à remercier le directoire actuel de la société pour le travail accompli à la réussite d’Eurazeo et à saluer particulièrement la contribution de M. William Kadouch-Chassaing depuis 2023", a souligné Jean-Charles Decaux, président du conseil de surveillance, cité dans un communiqué du groupe. Le Conseil de Surveillance arrêtera la composition du futur Directoire à l’issue des mandats en cours, précise le communiqué d'Eurazeo.

item.title: Vucic reconoce su derrota ante el movimiento estudiantil en unas elecciones históricas en Serbia
item.description: El serbio Aleksandar Vucic reconoció su derrota ante un movimiento de protesta liderado por estudiantes en unas elecciones históricas celebradas el domingo, que ponen fin a su prolongado dominio del poder y anuncian una nueva era política en el país balcánico.
item.dc:creator: Ivana Sekularac, Edward Mcallister, Aleksandar Vasovic
item.content:encoded: El serbio Aleksandar Vucic reconoció su derrota ante un movimiento de protesta liderado por estudiantes en unas elecciones históricas celebradas el domingo, que ponen fin a su prolongado dominio del poder y anuncian una nueva era política en el país balcánico. Vucic, populista y nacionalista, ha dominado la política serbia como primer ministro o presidente desde 2014. Sin embargo, convocó elecciones anticipadas en septiembre, tras casi dos años de manifestaciones encabezadas por estudiantes contra lo que consideran corrupción y un autoritarismo creciente. Las protestas se desencadenaron por la muerte de 16 personas al desplomarse la marquesina de una estación ferroviaria en la ciudad de Novi Sad en 2024. "Está claro que hemos perdido estas elecciones, la Lista Estudiantil ha ganado", dijo Vucic en un discurso televisado. Instantes después de su anuncio, estallaron las celebraciones en las calles de Belgrado. Decenas de miles de personas abarrotaron los principales bulevares de la ciudad, entre bocinazos de automóviles, gente que bailaba y estudiantes que gritaban "victoria" y "se acabó para él". El triunfo de los estudiantes marca un profundo cambio político en este país de unos seis millones de habitantes y recuerda a la derrota del húngaro Viktor Orban en abril. También podría servir de modelo para otros movimientos estudiantiles de Europa, que en las últimas semanas han salido a las calles para protestar, en algunos casos de forma violenta, contra la baja calidad de la educación y la falta de perspectivas. Vucic dijo que los estudiantes obtendrían entre 135 y 140 escaños en el Parlamento de 250 miembros, mientras que su Partido Progresista Serbio (SNS) conseguiría 105, según los resultados preliminares. "Querida Serbia, esta noche se está escuchando la voz del pueblo", dijo Radomir Sajcic, profesor de la Universidad de Belgrado, en nombre de los estudiantes desde su sede. "Esta noche celebramos la victoria, mañana construimos el futuro". Dirigentes y funcionarios europeos felicitaron a la Lista Estudiantil por su victoria, entre ellos la presidenta de la Comisión Europea, Ursula von der Leyen, y la comisaria europea de Ampliación, Marta Kos. "Estamos dispuestos a (...) trabajar juntos para impulsar el futuro de Serbia en la Unión Europea", escribió Von der Leyen en X. El primer ministro húngaro, Peter Magyar, aseguró a los estudiantes que contarían con el apoyo de su país. UNA PARTICIPACIÓN RÉCORD IMPULSA A LOS ESTUDIANTES A LA VICTORIA Durante la jornada se formaron largas filas que serpenteaban desde los centros de votación en ciudades y localidades de todo el país, e incluso Vucic esperó casi dos horas para votar en Belgrado. Las empresas de sondeos y la comisión electoral situaron la participación cerca del 70%, la más alta desde la desintegración de Yugoslavia en 1992. "(La participación) no me sorprendió porque a lo largo de los últimos dos años se ha formado un movimiento numeroso y fuerte", dijo la votante Katarina Petrovic. Vucic, que renunció a su segundo mandato presidencial para volver a aspirar al cargo de primer ministro, partía de una sólida posición en el poder y pocos en el movimiento de protesta estudiantil se atrevían a creer que reconocería la derrota tan pronto. Sus partidarios le atribuyen la modernización de la economía serbia y la construcción de nuevas autopistas, ferrocarriles, escuelas y hospitales. "Algunos empresarios, algunas personas nos abandonarán, pero nuestra estructura es sólida, estamos muy unidos, somos muy fuertes, estamos acostumbrados a estar en la oposición", dijo Vucic. INCERTIDUMBRE SOBRE LOS CANDIDATOS APOYADOS POR LOS ESTUDIANTES Persisten muchas incógnitas sobre cómo se desempeñarán los candidatos respaldados por los estudiantes. Su lista de 250 candidatos, en su mayoría desconocidos, incluye profesores universitarios, actores y agricultores, y está encabezada por el cardiólogo Ilija Srdanovic, que lloraba tras el anuncio de Vucic. Sin embargo, no está claro quién será el primer ministro que llevará adelante el programa de política interna de los estudiantes, cuyo objetivo es erradicar la corrupción y mejorar la educación. Los analistas políticos prevén algún tipo de purga de aliados de Vucic en la policía, los servicios de seguridad y los ministerios. Los estudiantes, en cambio, han sido más reservados sobre sus aspiraciones internacionales. Como hizo Vucic durante años, tendrán que mantener un equilibrio en las relaciones con China, un importante inversionista; Rusia, aliada tradicional de Serbia y su principal proveedor de gas natural; y la Unión Europea, su mayor socio comercial. "La mayor incertidumbre es (...) quién encabezará el Gobierno, quiénes serán los ministros clave y cómo actuarán para cumplir sus promesas de combatir la corrupción, restablecer el Estado de derecho y también restablecer la posición de Serbia en política exterior", dijo Radivoje Grujic, consultor electoral radicado en Varsovia.

item.title: Los hutíes aseguran haber atacado infraestructuras petroleras sauditas y el aeropuerto de Riad
item.description: Los hutíes de Yemen, alineados con Irán, afirmaron el lunes que habían atacado las estaciones de bombeo de crudo este-oeste de Arabia Saudita y el aeropuerto de Riad, en un momento en que el recrudecimiento de las hostilidades está obstaculizando el suministro de petróleo y amenaza con desembocar en un conflicto de mayor envergadura.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los hutíes de Yemen, alineados con Irán, afirmaron el lunes que habían atacado las estaciones de bombeo de crudo este-oeste de Arabia Saudita y el aeropuerto de Riad, en un momento en que el recrudecimiento de las hostilidades está obstaculizando el suministro de petróleo y amenaza con desembocar en un conflicto de mayor envergadura. La coalición liderada por Arabia Saudita en Yemen había dicho anteriormente que había destruido dos lanzadores de misiles balísticos en la capital, Saná, incluido uno utilizado para disparar un misil hacia Riad que, según la coalición, había sido interceptado. No hubo confirmación inmediata por parte de Arabia Saudita sobre los ataques hutíes. Los hutíes han estado lanzando misiles balísticos y drones contra aeropuertos, puertos e instalaciones petroleras sauditas, convirtiendo a Arabia Saudita, aliada de EEUU, en un punto de presión en la extensión de esta guerra. Los hutíes también dijeron haber atacado el Aeropuerto Internacional Rey Jalid de Riad, que reanudó sus operaciones en dos terminales el domingo tras un ataque reivindicado por el grupo [USN:L6N45Y0QF TEXT:"este mes"] en el que murieron 13 personas, el más mortífero en el reino en más de una década. Altos cargos de los países del Pacto de La Meca —Arabia Saudita, Turquía y Pakistán— tienen previsto reunirse con funcionarios iraníes en Teherán el lunes para debatir la coordinación regional, según dos personas con conocimiento del asunto. Las conversaciones previstas supondrían el primer contacto de alto nivel entre Irán y todos los miembros del bloque de tres países desde que Arabia Saudita se viera sometida a ataques cada vez más intensos por parte de los hutíes yemeníes, alineados con Irán. ATAQUES EN YEMEN Arabia Saudita cerró temporalmente en septiembre su oleoducto este-oeste, de 1.200 kilómetros, como medida de precaución tras un ataque con drones que, según Riad y Bagdad, se originó en Irak. El oleoducto ha servido como ruta clave para las exportaciones de petróleo de Oriente Medio, mientras que el estrecho de Ormuz ha quedado prácticamente cerrado por la guerra. Los hutíes también dijeron el sábado que habían atacado el oleoducto este-oeste, estaciones de bombeo de crudo, una instalación de Aramco en Yanbu y la refinería de Rabigh. Arabia Saudita no ha confirmado estas afirmaciones. La coalición saudita dijo el lunes que también había llevado a cabo una operación militar contra objetivos hutíes en Yemen, destruyendo cinco túneles utilizados para almacenar misiles balísticos, cuatro lanzadores de misiles balísticos y una instalación de almacenamiento de misiles. La operación también se centró en las líneas de suministro, los combatientes y el equipamiento militar de los hutíes a lo largo de las líneas del frente en el interior de Yemen, según el portavoz de la coalición, Turki al-Maliki, quien se comprometió a continuar con "medidas operativas disuasorias" para proteger a la población civil. Arabia Saudita ha intensificado sus ataques a los hutíes desde que el grupo se apoderó el mes pasado de zonas estratégicas a lo largo de la costa yemení del mar Rojo, avanzando hacia el estrecho de Bab el-Mandeb, una ruta marítima clave a nivel mundial para los productores de petróleo del golfo Pérsico, situada al otro lado de la península arábiga con respecto al estrecho de Ormuz. Los últimos combates han puesto fin de hecho a una tregua negociada por la ONU, que se había mantenido en gran medida desde 2022. Arabia Saudita lideró una coalición que intervino en la guerra civil de Yemen en 2015 para respaldar al Gobierno reconocido internacionalmente, un año después de que los hutíes tomaran la capital, Saná.

item.title: Chinese beauty brands, flush with success at home, start to vie for global shelf space
item.description: China's beauty brands are stepping out into the global market, armed with intricately carved lipsticks, freeze-dried face masks activated with purified water as well as creams infused with ingredients from traditional Chinese medicine.
item.dc:creator: Casey Hall, Dominique Patton
item.content:encoded: China's beauty brands are stepping out into the global market, armed with intricately carved lipsticks, freeze-dried face masks activated with purified water as well as creams infused with ingredients from traditional Chinese medicine. Proya Cosmetics (603605.SS) , the largest C-beauty brand by revenue, is among the most aggressive. Its Advanced Firming and Original Repair skincare lines will be sold in 400 Ulta stores as well as on Ulta.com across the United States from November, and it opened a Paris research and development centre this month. Other brands had their start in online sales and are now expanding to physical stores abroad. They include Florasis, whose lipsticks and other ornate cosmetics draw on traditional Chinese aesthetics. It opened its first overseas flagship shop in Tokyo's posh Ginza district last year. Joocyee, which produces skincare-infused makeup, and Judydoll, known for inventive products such as its metal-wand mascara, opened shops in Singapore last year. Both brands, owned by China's Joy Group, are also now stocked at Skin Cupid, a British retailer specialising in Asian beauty products. C-beauty brands have grown rapidly within China over the past decade and industry executives today speak of a growing confidence that Chinese products will find favour with consumers worldwide. Gone are the days when China was associated with cheap and low-quality goods, as Chinese innovations — across many industries but particularly in [USN:L6N42A0LN TEXT:"electric vehicles"] — have produced a halo effect, they say. "The shift can be seen in everything from cars and smartphones to AI models," said David Huang, CEO of New York-listed Yatsen Group (YSG.N) , which owns the Perfect Diary makeup brand. The efforts by the C-beauty firms are part of a broader push abroad by [USN:L8N3WQ005 TEXT:"Chinese brands"] — from fashion and electronics to [USN:L6N3XM0L4 TEXT:"bubble tea"] — keen to seek new revenue amid a years-long slump in domestic consumer spending. BRAND AWARENESS CHALLENGES AHEAD Some Chinese brands are very ambitious. Proya, for example, wants to become a top 10 brand globally and is among C-beauty companies [USN:L5N3S10CC TEXT:"exploring acquisitions"] of smaller foreign brands to expand their portfolios. Its 51%-owned colour cosmetics brand Flower Knows, known for fairytale-inspired packaging, also launched with British pharmacy and beauty retailer Boots in March and began a limited run in Ulta stores in September. While awareness of Chinese beauty brands is growing in many international markets, Proya says it has a long way to go. "I would say that Proya's brand awareness in both Europe and the US is currently zero," founder and CEO Hou Juncheng said at the opening of the company's R&D centre in Paris. "We hope that through collaboration with our partners, we can earn consumer trust and encourage them to purchase our products." Rivals believe Proya, founded only 20 years ago, has a bright future, with Marc-Antoine Jamet, president of French industry association Cosmetic Valley, describing Hou as an "incredible competitor". "He moved from the mass market to the mid-market, and then from the mid-market to the premium segment. You can be sure he’ll move into the luxury sector — whether in six weeks, six months, or six years. That’s a near certainty," said Jamet. CONQUERING AT HOME AND INSPIRED BY K-BEAUTY C-beauty brands overtook international names in 2022 and accounted for 57.4% of China's $159 billion cosmetics market last year, according to the China Association of Fragrance, Flavor and Cosmetic Industries. They can also draw inspiration from the success of their Korean counterparts, which have become a significant force in the global cosmetics industry. Exports for the K-beauty sector, known for 10-step routines to produce luminous "glass skin", surged 50% over five years to hit $11.4 billion in 2025. South Korea also overtook France in 2024 to become the top source of cosmetics imports in the tough-to-crack American market, US International Trade Commission data showed. K-beauty has helped pave the way by bringing "this Asian cultural awareness to the market," said Jing An, an attorney at Altman & An, a New York law firm that helps foreign firms with US intellectual property and e-commerce operations. An says her Chinese clients are usually apparel firms, luggage brands and online platforms but in the past year she has taken on two Chinese beauty clients looking to enter the US market. One advantage that Chinese brands might have is their mid-market price points. Global consumers have become "really fed up of paying premium prices for topical skincare," said Elisa Harca, co-founder of marketing firm Red Ant Asia, which has advised global retailers on which C-beauty products to stock. In the US, Chinese brands must also navigate persistent trade and geopolitical tensions between Beijing and Washington. Gabby Chen, president of global markets at Florasis, said that last year, China-US tensions led the brand to shift its international expansion away from the US. Chen is more optimistic today, saying her focus is on building a sustainable, long-term global business regardless of the geopolitical backdrop. People who choose to buy Florasis are likely to be more international and open-minded, she added. "It doesn't have to be political. It's like Feng Shui, you can choose to believe it or not, but we are here to share with you the essence of our culture and the essence of our brand."

item.title: Philippines defends bounty for fugitive senator wanted by ICC
item.description: The Philippine presidential palace defended on Monday a 50 million peso ($786,646) bounty for information leading to the arrest of Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, saying it was part of a legitimate operation by the Interior Department and the Philippine National Police.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Philippine presidential palace defended on Monday a 50 million peso ($786,646) bounty for information leading to the arrest of Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, saying it was part of a legitimate operation by the Interior Department and the Philippine National Police. Presidential Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro said in an interview with state-run Radyo Pilipinas that the bounty was an operational strategy of the Interior Minister and the Philippine National Police, when asked whether it had been ordered or approved by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr Castro said confidential and intelligence funds allocated to the interior department and police could be used for such operations, provided authorities could substantiate the operation and show results Dela Rosa is wanted by the International Criminal Court for alleged crimes against humanity during the "war on drugs" he helped oversee as national police chief under Rodrigo Duterte, who served as president from 2016 to 2022 He has denied any involvement in illegal killings He was last seen in May when he took refuge at the Senate for several days following six months spent in hiding Amid claims that his [USN:L6N41O0SP TEXT:"arrest"] was imminent, he appealed for help from his supporters and [USN:L6N41S0NA TEXT:"slipped away"] from the Senate in the early hours of May 14 following hours of [USN:L6N41Q0RF TEXT:"chaos that included gunfire"] Police have given Dela Rosa one week from Friday to surrender, but Castro said the deadline did not mean operations would stop if he failed to turn himself in In a Facebook post on Monday, Dela Rosa's lawyer, Israelito Torreon, questioned the legal basis for the bounty, arguing that authorities should produce an arrest warrant issued by a Philippine court ($1 = 63.5610 Philippine pesos)

item.title: Nice earnings forecasts you have. Shame if something happened to them
item.description: The bull case for equities rests on sky-high earnings forecasts. History suggests forecasts typically fail most spectacularly when markets are priced for exceptional future profit growth. That’s exactly where we are right now.
item.dc:creator: Joachim Klement
item.content:encoded: The bull case for equities rests on sky-high earnings forecasts. History suggests forecasts typically fail most spectacularly when markets are priced for exceptional future profit growth. That’s exactly where we are right now. Equity analysts are a chronically overoptimistic bunch, and their track record for earnings forecasts is never great, but that’s especially true at the end of major bull markets. Since 1992, average annual earnings per share (EPS) growth in the S&P 500 (.SPX) was 9.5%. The average EPS growth predicted by analysts was 22.3%, more than double the actual rate. Unsurprisingly, the gap between forecast and realised EPS growth becomes especially large when realised EPS declines. The largest misses in recent decades came after the 1990–91 recession and during the dotcom bust of 2000–02, the global financial crisis of 2007–09, the 2015–16 earnings recession and the COVID-19 shock in 2020. In the months when S&P 500 EPS growth turned negative, the rolling 12-month growth rate averaged minus 4.5%. Yet, at the start of those periods, Bloomberg consensus estimates projected EPS growth of 18.8%. CALLING MY SHOT A few weeks ago, [USN:FWN45R0CB TEXT:"my forecast"] that the S&P 500 could fall to 5,000 points by the end of 2027 made waves. I, like everyone, cannot definitively time the end of the current bull market, but I believe that within the next two years, we will enter a major bear market as the AI investment boom ends. My intention with this end-of-2027 forecast is to warn investors to prepare for such an event today, even if it may not come until 2028. Strategists at other more bullish banks were quick to reject my call, arguing that investors underestimate future earnings growth and that earnings will “grow into” today’s seemingly high valuations. To which, I can only respond, “Nice earnings forecasts you have. Shame if something happened to them.” FORWARD VS TRAILING P/E RATIOS Analysts today are extremely optimistic about future EPS growth. That means price-to-earnings (P/E) ratios based on 12-month forward EPS estimates can appear more attractive than trailing valuation measures suggest. The current 12-month forward P/E ratio of the S&P 500 is 18.9x, roughly in line with its 10-year average. But that holds only if we believe EPS will grow by 38.6% over the next 12 months. Meanwhile, the 12-month trailing P/E ratio is 26.2x, about 14% above its 10-year average, indicating a somewhat expensive market. Backtests suggest trailing valuation measures are a far better indicator of future stock market performance than forward P/E ratios. And the longer a bull market lasts, the more unreliable earnings forecasts typically become. GROWTH FORECAST OVERREACH The most dangerous forecasts, though, are the long-term ones, where scrutiny is weakest. I started my career in the late 1990s at the height of the last technology boom. One thing we learned once the bubble burst was that analysts often sought to justify extremely high share prices by ramping up their earnings growth expectations. However, as the bubble continued, that became increasingly difficult since even the most gullible investor wouldn't believe that a large-cap stock with billions in revenue can grow its earnings by 100% or 200% every year. In these types of situations, analysts will sometimes try to shift excessive EPS growth into the outer years, where there is less scrutiny of their assumptions. Research by Allaudeen Hameed, Massimo Massa, and Zhenghui Ni finds that companies in the decile with the highest long-term EPS forecasts usually underperform the rest by a wide margin over the following year. Why is this? Probably because it simply becomes challenging for companies to meet these excessively optimistic forecasts. The resulting disappointment, together with large downward earnings revisions, weighs heavily on these firms’ share prices. So where do we stand today? The long-term EPS growth forecast for the S&P 500 is currently 16.7%, placing it in the top 10% for this century. S&P 500 constituents with particularly high long-term EPS growth expectations include Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) , Intel (INTC.O) , Broadcom (AVGO.O) , Palantir and Micron (MU.O) . That leaves their shares more exposed if growth falls short of consensus. None of us has a crystal ball, and bull runs can keep going longer than logic would deem reasonable. But investors should be warned. (The views expressed here are those of Joachim Klement , an investment strategist for Panmure Liberum.) Enjoying this column? item.title: Large fire breaks out on island off Hong Kong
