item.content:encoded: A fire broke out at a waste management facility on an artificial island off Hong Kong's southwestern coast on Monday, sending large plumes of thick, black smoke billowing into the air, the city's fire department said. The fire occurred on the island that houses an incinerator and waste management facilities off the south coast of Lantau island. Firefighters were deployed to battle the blaze, the department said. No casualties have been reported so far.

item.title: Trump evoca el 11S para oponerse al candidato musulmán de Míchigan al Senado
item.description: El presidente Donald Trump, intensificó su campaña en un mitin al vincular al candidato al Senado de EEUU Abdul El-Sayed con extremistas musulmanes, comparándolo con los autores de los ataques del 11S y afirmando que los demócratas permitirían la entrada en Estados Unidos de terroristas violentos y antiestadounidenses.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: El presidente Donald Trump, intensificó su campaña en un mitin al vincular al candidato al Senado de EEUU Abdul El-Sayed con extremistas musulmanes, comparándolo con los autores de los ataques del 11S y afirmando que los demócratas permitirían la entrada en Estados Unidos de terroristas violentos y antiestadounidenses. "Estoy aquí para impedir que un yihadista, miembro de los Hermanos Musulmanes, se convierta en senador de Estados Unidos", dijo el domingo el presidente ante un público receptivo en Port Huron, una localidad de Míchigan donde el 66% de los votos fueron para Trump en las elecciones presidenciales de 2024. Si El-Sayed ganara, sería el primer musulmán elegido para el Senado de EEUU. Trump ha intentado presentarlo como un musulmán radical antiestadounidense y, el domingo, llevó su retórica a un nuevo nivel al comparar a El-Sayed con los atacantes que secuestraron el vuelo 93 de United Airlines durante los atentados del 11 de septiembre de 2001. Míchigan acoge una de las contiendas por el Senado de EEUU más reñidas del país de cara a las elecciones de mitad de mandato del 3 de noviembre, en las que el exdiputado republicano Mike Rogers y El-Sayed compiten por un escaño vacante que ayudará a decidir el control de la cámara. El domingo, el presidente comparó votar en contra de El-Sayed con las acciones de Todd Beamer, natural de Míchigan, y de otras personas que se enfrentaron a los secuestradores del vuelo 93. "Veinticinco años después, Míchigan tiene que plantar cara y luchar, igual que hizo Todd, para impedir que un yihadista entre en el Capitolio", afirmó Trump. Si El-Sayed gana, "sería el único senador que tendría que pasar por un detector de metales antes de que se le permitiera entrar en el Senado", señaló Trump. El-Sayed ha desestimado las acusaciones en su contra y, en un acto celebrado el domingo por la noche, sugirió que el hecho de que Trump insista tanto en su nombre denota cierta hipocresía. "Entiendo que el presidente de Estados Unidos se tome como una ofensa personal mi nombre de pila", declaró El-Sayed ante el público en Grand Rapids, Míchigan. "No le molesta tanto cuando se trata de un nombre común entre los sauditas que financian el fondo de capital riesgo de su yerno, ni parece importarle tanto cuando son los cataríes quienes le regalan un avión privado de 400 millones de dólares". Según se ha informado, Affinity Partners, el fondo de inversión de Jared Kushner, yerno de Trump, ha recibido miles de millones de una entidad del Gobierno saudita. Qatar regaló a Trump un avión Boeing 747. EL-SAYED DICE QUE CUESTIONAR SU LEALTAD ES "VERGONZOSO" El público, en su mayoría blanco, que asistió al mitin del domingo aplaudió los comentarios de Trump sobre El-Sayed. Algunos asistentes gritaron "traidor" y otros "depórtenlo", aunque El-Sayed nació en Míchigan. Terrance Camburn, un veterano del Ejército discapacitado de 52 años de Sandusky, en Míchigan, afirmó que apoyaba las críticas de Trump debido a las "convicciones políticas" de El-Sayed. "He estado en Dearborn y he visto muchas de las cosas con las que él está de acuerdo", dijo Camburn cuando se le preguntó por los comentarios de Trump sobre el 11S. Dearborn, situada en Míchigan, tiene la mayor concentración per cápita de musulmanes de todas las ciudades de EEUU. Al salir del recinto tras el mitin, Rogers, el candidato republicano, no respondió a las preguntas de Reuters sobre la referencia de Trump al 11S. Sin embargo, ese mismo domingo, había declarado en un programa de la NBC que no estaba de acuerdo con la idea de que El-Sayed fuera un terrorista violento. "Nunca le he llamado terrorista", declaró Rogers a la NBC. Rogers ha alegado, sin aportar pruebas, que El-Sayed tiene vínculos con los Hermanos Musulmanes, uno de los grupos islamistas más antiguos e influyentes del mundo árabe. El-Sayed ha negado cualquier afiliación con los Hermanos Musulmanes y ha calificado de "vergonzoso" que Rogers cuestione su lealtad a Estados Unidos. Rogers declaró en el programa de la NBC que El-Sayed no había respondido de forma satisfactoria a las preguntas sobre las acusaciones. "Es un candidato alineado con el Partido Demócrata Socialista de Estados Unidos que cuenta con grupos de apoyo bastante radicales a los que no les gusta Estados Unidos", dijo. El discurso de Trump en el este de Míchigan el domingo se produjo un día después de que el expresidente Barack Obama hiciera campaña a favor de los demócratas en el estado, lo que subraya su importancia en las elecciones de la próxima semana. En un mitin celebrado el sábado en Detroit, Obama calificó los ataques de los oponentes de El-Sayed como un intento de hacerle parecer "menos estadounidense que ellos". El expresidente comparó esta situación con su propia experiencia como blanco de afirmaciones falsas de que había nacido en Kenia. "Esas cosas no me hicieron mella", dijo Obama. "Ni en Míchigan. Tampoco le van a hacer mella a Abdul". Los demócratas solo necesitan ganar unos pocos escaños tanto en el Senado como en la Cámara de Representantes de EEUU para revertir las estrechas mayorías republicanas de 53-47 y 218-214.

item.title: Inversionistas prevén ventas y cautela en el mercado brasileño tras el triunfo de Lula
item.description: El presidente brasileño, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, ganó la reelección el domingo, derrotando al senador de derecha Flávio Bolsonaro y planteando una prueba para los inversionistas, que esperan que las recientes apuestas por un cambio de Gobierno se reviertan en una semana previsiblemente volátil.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Campos, Marcela Ayres
item.content:encoded: El presidente brasileño, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, [USN:L2N46C00P TEXT:"ganó "][USN:L2N46C00P TEXT:"la reelección"] el domingo, derrotando al senador de derecha Flávio Bolsonaro y planteando una prueba para los inversionistas, que esperan que las recientes apuestas por un cambio de Gobierno se reviertan en una semana previsiblemente volátil. Los mercados se habían movido con fuerza ante la expectativa de un giro hacia la derecha desde que Bolsonaro, hijo del expresidente condenado Jair Bolsonaro, quedara inesperadamente en primer lugar en la primera vuelta hace tres semanas. La bolsa brasileña (.BVSP) cerró el viernes casi un 7% por encima de su nivel al inicio de la primera vuelta, mientras que el real se había apreciado casi un 5% frente al dólar estadounidense. Los futuros sobre las tasas de interés habían indicado que se esperaba que el endurecimiento de las finanzas públicas permitiera una bajada de los costos de financiación. "Esperamos una fuerte reacción del mercado el lunes, con una reevaluación agresiva, una ola de ventas de activos y unos futuros sobre tasas de interés que probablemente alcancen su límite superior poco después de la apertura", dijo Luis Felipe Vital, director de estrategia macroeconómica de Warren Investimentos. Durante los próximos cuatro años, Lula deberá frenar el crecimiento de la deuda brasileña al tiempo que protege los programas sociales y la inversión. Para los inversionistas, la cuestión es si su enfoque gradual para sanear las finanzas públicas podrá reducir los costos de financiación. Sin la confianza de que pueda cumplir sus promesas, los prestamistas podrían exigir tasas de interés más altas, lo que aumentaría la deuda del Gobierno y encarecería el crédito para las empresas y los hogares. "Los inversionistas quieren un compromiso claro y creíble con la disciplina fiscal", dijo Alejo Czerwonko, director de inversiones para mercados emergentes de UBS Global Wealth Management. "Prevemos que el repunte que siguió a la primera vuelta ya esté en gran medida descontado en los precios, y que el ánimo se mantenga débil hasta que surja un plan fiscal claro". Czerwonko señaló que los inversionistas esperan que se ponga fin al gasto que acompañó a la campaña y que se trace una vía creíble para estabilizar la deuda pública. "Esto también implica una relación de trabajo con un Congreso de tendencia opositora, ya que ningún plan fiscal se aprueba sin él", añadió. El equipo de Lula se propone alcanzar un superávit presupuestario primario de alrededor del 1,3% del producto interno bruto para 2030. Eso dejaría fondos para cubrir parte de los intereses, reduciendo la necesidad de nuevos préstamos. Sin embargo, la deuda pública ya supera el 82% del PIB, mientras que las pensiones y otros gastos obligatorios por ley limitan las fuentes de ahorro. "Las políticas de Lula han hablado de recortes de gasto, pero no ha entrado en detalles sobre cómo se concretarán", señaló Divya Singaravelu, directora de investigación de Meridian 1305 Capital. Afirmó que la elección del próximo ministro de Finanzas sería una primera señal para los mercados, y añadió: "Queremos ver cómo serán el presupuesto y el límite de gasto para 2027". Quien ocupe el cargo tendrá que explicar cómo encajan los compromisos de campaña dentro de esos límites fiscales. "La clave es que, aunque prevalezca el pesimismo a corto plazo, los inversionistas tendrán que estar atentos a cómo avanza la agenda económica del Gobierno a medio plazo", señaló Gustavo Sung, economista jefe de Suno Research. "Lo más importante ahora es observar cómo se organiza el Gobierno de cara a 2027."

item.title: Drone attack on Russia's Voronezh region kills two men, governor says
item.description: A drone attack in Russia's Voronezh region killed two men and injured 17 people, including a child, regional governor Alexander Gusev said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A drone attack in Russia's Voronezh region killed two men and injured 17 people, including a child, regional governor Alexander Gusev said on Monday. Air defence systems had destroyed 113 drones over the region, Gusev wrote on the MAX messaging app. Fires also broke out at several industrial sites, Gusev said. A passenger train bound to Moscow from Anapa in Russia's Krasnodar region, popular among Russian vacationers, was also damaged and five passengers injured, Russian Railways said. Train services through Voronezh have been suspended. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

item.title: El ex primer ministro japonés Yasuo Fukuda muere a los 90 años, según el Nikkei
item.description: El ex primer ministro japonés Yasuo Fukuda, quien aprovechó su breve mandato para estrechar los lazos con los países vecinos de Asia, especialmente con China, ha fallecido a los 90 años, informó el lunes el diario económico Nikkei.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El ex primer ministro japonés Yasuo Fukuda, quien aprovechó su breve mandato para estrechar los lazos con los países vecinos de Asia, especialmente con China, ha fallecido a los 90 años, informó el lunes el diario económico Nikkei. El político japonés, el primer hijo de un primer ministro que también llegó a ocupar el cargo, murió el jueves a causa de una insuficiencia cardíaca, según Nikkei. Fukuda asumió como primer ministro tras la repentina dimisión de Shinzo Abe en 2007 y permaneció en el cargo menos de un año, un mandato aún más breve que el de dos años de su padre, Takeo. Licenciado en Economía por la prestigiosa Universidad de Waseda, en Tokio, Fukuda pasó casi dos décadas ascendiendo en una empresa petrolera —con una estancia de dos años en Estados Unidos— antes de renunciar para convertirse en secretario político de su padre cuando este asumió como primer ministro en 1976. Elegido en 1990 para la Cámara Baja del Parlamento japonés, la de mayor poder, Fukuda fue secretario jefe del Gabinete entre 2000 y 2004. Dimitió tras ser uno de varios ministros que admitieron no haber cotizado al sistema de pensiones. Conocido por su carácter irritable, Fukuda, que llevaba gafas, fue blanco de críticas en 2003 por unos comentarios que hizo bajo condición de que no se publicaran, en los que sugirió que las mujeres que vestían de forma provocativa buscaban que las violaran. Cuando sucedió a Abe, Fukuda bromeó con que quizá le había tocado la peor parte al asumir el cargo, dada la división del Parlamento y la capacidad de los partidos de oposición para retrasar la aprobación de leyes. Frustrado por el bloqueo del proceso legislativo, Fukuda dimitió en 2008 y fue el segundo de seis primeros ministros que renunciaron tras apenas un año aproximadamente en el cargo. Conocido por su talante conciliador en política exterior, Fukuda visitó China en varias ocasiones después de dejar el cargo, en un esfuerzo por mejorar unas relaciones a menudo tensas. Fukuda deja un hijo, Tatsuo, que también es diputado y ha sido considerado como un posible futuro primer ministro.

item.title: Kampf gegen Wohnungsnot - Regierung bringt einfachen Baustandard auf den Weg

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Angesichts der Wohnungsnot in Deutschland hat die Bundesregierung einen Gesetzentwurf für einfacheres und günstigeres Bauen vorgelegt. Durch eine Änderung des Bauvertragsrechts soll unter Verzicht auf bestimmte Komfortstandards so auch schneller gebaut werden können, wie aus einem Entwurf des Justizministeriums (BMJV) zum sogenannten Gebäudetyp E hervorgeht, der Reuters am Montagmorgen vorlag. Erfahrungen aus Pilotprojekten zufolge können die Baukosten dadurch um zehn bis 15 Prozent gesenkt werden. Die Neuregelung sieht eine freiwillige Option vor. Nur wenn die Parteien eines Bauprojekts den neuen "Gebäudetyp E-Basisstandard" ausdrücklich vereinbaren, gelten die vereinfachten Regeln. Andernfalls bleibt es bei den bisherigen, höheren Standards. An zwingenden staatlichen Vorgaben etwa zu Brandschutz, Statik oder Belichtung ändert das Gesetz nichts. "Bauen in Deutschland muss einfacher und günstiger werden. Denn wir brauchen mehr bezahlbaren Wohnraum", erklärte Bundesjustizministerin Stefanie Hubig (SPD). "Mit dem Gebäudetyp-E-Gesetz ebnen wir dafür den Weg." Bauministerin Verena Hubertz (SPD) sagte: "Jeder Euro, den wir nicht in überflüssige Standards stecken, ist ein Euro für mehr bezahlbaren Wohnraum. So wird Bauen günstiger und bleibt rechtssicher." Dem Entwurf waren monatelange Abstimmungen innerhalb der Regierung vorausgegangen. Ursprünglich hatten Justiz- und Bauministerium bereits im November 2025 ein gemeinsames Eckpunktepapier vorgelegt. Die Verbände der Bau- und Immobilienwirtschaft sowie mehrere Bundesländer hatten die Regierung zuletzt wiederholt zu mehr Tempo bei dem Vorhaben gedrängt. Bislang scheitert das Bauen nach einem günstigeren Standard oft an rechtlichen Unsicherheiten, da Bauunternehmen bei Abweichungen von etablierten Normen Rechtsstreitigkeiten fürchten. Der Gesetzentwurf wird nun an die Länder und Verbände versandt, die bis zum 13. November 2026 Stellung nehmen können.

item.content:encoded: Die Bundesregierung bringt die Umsetzung von EU-Vorgaben zur stärkeren Bekämpfung von Geldwäsche auf den Weg. Die EU-Pläne sollen dabei eins zu eins umgesetzt werden, wie aus einem der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters am Montag vorliegenden Referentenentwurf des Finanzministeriums hervorgeht. Dieser wird derzeit regierungsintern beraten. Die Maßnahmen ergänzen den bereits vorgestellten [USN:L8N43I18N TEXT:"Aktionsplan"] der Bundesregierung gegen Steuer- und Finanzkriminalität. Das Bundeskriminalamt beziffert den für 2025 durch Geldwäsche verursachten Schaden auf 1,5 Milliarden Euro. Die tatsächliche Summe dürfte allerdings deutlich höher liegen. In der Regierung heißt es, es gebe den Trend, dass Geldwäsche immer professioneller und digitaler werde, was die ohnehin komplexen und oft internationalen Ermittlungen erschwere. Das SPD-geführte Finanzministerium will das bestehende Geldwäschegesetz aus dem Jahr 2017 zum 10. Juli 2027 aufheben. Es soll dann durch ein neues Gesetz zur Bekämpfung von Geldwäsche und Terrorismusfinanzierung ersetzt werden. Außerdem werden noch Anpassungen des Kreditwesengesetzes und des Bundeskriminalamtgesetzes vorgenommen. Konkret geplant ist, eine zentrale Koordinierungsstelle für die Geldwäscheaufsicht bei der Bonner BaFin einzurichten. Außerdem soll die Zentralstelle für Finanztransaktionsuntersuchungen (FIU) mehr Befugnisse bekommen. Vorgesehen ist auch mehr Transparenz, wer hinter Firmen, Organisationen oder Stiftungen steht. Ab Juli 2029 soll dann eine zentrale Zugangsstelle für Immobilieninformationen stehen. Sie soll auch zu mehr Transparenz führen, insbesondere für Strafverfolgungsbehörden. Ferner werden Abrufverfahren zu Bankkonten europaweit besser vernetzt. Hintergrund des Gesetzentwurfes ist das EU-Paket zur Geldwäschebekämpfung von Ende Mai 2024. Es ist die bisher weitreichendste Reform im Bereich der Geldwäscheprävention und umfasst zwei Richtlinien sowie zwei Verordnungen. Es muss in den 27 EU-Staaten ab dem 10. Juli 2027 angewendet werden. Es regelt unter anderem, welche Unternehmen Präventionsmaßnahmen gegen Geldwäsche ergreifen müssen, etwa durch Prüfung der Identität eines Kunden oder die Meldung von Verdachtsfällen. Außerdem wird eine EU-weite Obergrenze für Bargeldzahlungen von 10.000 Euro im gewerblichen Bereich eingeführt. Diese gilt jedoch nicht für Geschäfte zwischen Privatpersonen. Durch das von der Bundesregierung geplante Gesetz entstehen im Bundeshaushalt in den Jahren 2027 bis 2030 zusätzliche Ausgaben in Höhe von insgesamt rund 157 Millionen Euro. Bei der Finanzaufsichtsbehöre BaFin sollen 32 zusätzliche Vollzeitstellen geschaffen werden, um die neuen Aufgaben zu erfüllen. Insidern zufolge soll das Kabinett noch in diesem Jahr grünes Licht für das Gesetz geben.

item.title: Australia's CSL names interim CEO Gordon Naylor as new chair
item.description: Australia's CSL on Monday named interim chief Gordon Naylor as chair from March next year, the latest leadership shake-up days after naming GSK executive Deborah Waterhourse as its first female CEO.
item.dc:creator: Sherin Sunny, Nikita Jino
item.content:encoded: Australia's CSL (CSL.AX) on Monday named interim chief Gordon Naylor as chair from March next year, the latest leadership shake-up days after naming GSK (GSK.L) executive Deborah Waterhourse as its first female CEO. Naylor has led CSL on an interim basis since February, following the surprise exit of former CEO Paul McKenzie amid investor concerns over the biotechnology giant's falling shares. Once Australia's most valuable listed company and a market favourite, CSL suffered a series of earnings and revenue downgrades and announced plans to cut 3,000 jobs, triggering selloffs that wiped billions of dollars from its market value over the past year. "CSL's leadership picture is finally coming into focus, and Gordon Naylor's elevation to chair provides continuity at a critical juncture," said Marc Jocum, senior ETF strategist at Global X ETFs. Naylor's role in CSL's strategic reset and his knowledge of the company should help [USN:L4N4670C7 TEXT:"incoming CEO Deborah Waterhouse"] tackle its challenges, combining new executive leadership with an experienced chair, he added. Current chair Brian McNamee will retire from CSL's board on March 31, 2027, after more than eight years in the role. He previously served as CEO and managing director from 1990 to 2013. CSL shares closed 0.8% lower at A$195.14, broadly in line with a 0.5% decline in the healthcare sub-index (.AXHJ) .

item.title: Ukraine-Des frappes russes visent plusieurs régions, des blessés
item.description: Des frappes russes menées dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi ont fait six blessés dans le sud-est et le nord de l'Ukraine, ont dit un responsable et les services d'urgence ukrainiens.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des frappes russes menées dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi ont fait six blessés dans le sud-est et le nord de l'Ukraine, ont dit un responsable et les services d'urgence ukrainiens. Quatre personnes ont été blessées dans la ville de Zaporijjia, a dit lundi le gouverneur de cette région du sud-est, Mykhaïlo Semikine, sur Telegram. Les services d'urgence ukrainiens ont par ailleurs indiqué que deux personnes avaient été blessées dans la région de Tchernihiv, dans le nord du pays. Le ministère russe de la Défense a de son côté annoncé avoir frappé une centrale électrique à Kharkiv, la deuxième ville d'Ukraine, et une autre dans la région de Khmelnitskiy, dans l'ouest du pays. Des infrastructures portuaires à Tchornomorsk et un navire cargo qui faisait route vers Odessa utilisé à des fins militaires, ont également été pris pour cible, a dit le ministère.

item.title: Revolut launches personal loans in UK, taking on major banks
item.description: Digital bank Revolut has begun offering unsecured personal loans in Britain, its UK chief executive Francesca Carlesi told Reuters, taking Europe's most valuable startup into a lucrative consumer lending market dominated by the country's biggest banks.
item.dc:creator: Lawrence White, Tommy Wilkes
item.content:encoded: Digital bank Revolut has begun offering unsecured personal loans in Britain, its UK chief executive Francesca Carlesi told Reuters, taking Europe's most valuable startup into a lucrative consumer lending market dominated by the country's biggest banks. The move pushes Revolut beyond its core payments and subscription products and into a riskier business as it seeks to compete more directly with lenders including NatWest (NWG.L) , Lloyds (LLOY.L) , Barclays (BARC.L) , Santander's (SAN.MC) UK business and HSBC (HSBA.L) . "We want to transition from being a very successful everyday spending app and disrupting the market, to become effectively the primary bank of choice for everybody in the UK," Carlesi said. Revolut will also launch a credit card product in the near future, Carlesi said, part of a broader effort to increase the income it generates from each customer, a metric by which it lags traditional banks. Since its creation in 2015 by CEO Nik Storonsky and Vlad Yatsenko, London-based Revolut has grown worldwide to serve more than 80 million customers and commands a private valuation of $115 billion, bigger than listed rivals like Barclays and NatWest. Yet the bank still [USN:L6N45R0BS TEXT:"faces questions over whether it can sustain its breakneck growth"] with per-customer revenue well below rivals along with the proportion of its customers using Revolut for their primary bank account and paying salaries in. Revolut's rapid growth has also drawn regulatory and operational scrutiny. In 2025, Lithuania's central bank imposed a record €3.5 million fine over shortcomings in transaction-monitoring controls, while this month it was among financial firms hit by an hours-long [USN:L6N4660L6 TEXT:"Google Cloud outage"]. OFFLOADING THE RISK While Revolut already offers unsecured loans in some other countries, Britain is one of its biggest markets. Carlesi said Revolut will initially take a cautious approach, offering loans to a selected group of customers and expanding to its 14 million customers in Britain over the coming months. The loans will range from £2,000 to £25,000, with rates of 6.9% to 29.3%, a Revolut spokesperson said. Without the decades of customer spending and repayment data held by traditional banks, Revolut has supplemented its underwriting with information purchased from external providers, Carlesi said, adding that the company was confident about its credit analysis. Revolut will expand lending gradually and does not have a target for its overall lending in Britain, Carlesi said. The bank will eventually look to offload much of its risk via securitisation, aiming to keep its loan-to-deposit ratio close to 6%, far lower than other banks, she said. Carlesi said Revolut also eventually plans to enter the highly competitive market for mortgages in Britain. Revolut's lending push comes amid persistent cost-of-living challenges in Britain worsened by a [USN:L8N46608R TEXT:"soft labour market"] and rising inflation, which could weigh on borrowers' ability to repay debt.

item.title: Who are the leading candidates in Israel's election?
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has long looked on course to lose power in Israel's election, but the race has narrowed as the vote approaches and his rivals have no clear path to power.
item.dc:creator: Maayan Lubell
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has long looked on course to lose power in Israel's election, but the race has narrowed as the vote approaches and his rivals have no clear path to power. Votes will be cast on Tuesday for parties, and seats in parliament will be allocated to individuals on party lists according to proportional representation. Here are details of some of the leading candidates in Israel's first parliamentary election since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023 that plunged the Middle East into turmoil, with Israel going to war in Lebanon and Gaza and launching airstrikes against Iran. BENJAMIN NETANYAHU In power for much of the time since 2009, after a first stint as prime minister in the 1990s, Netanyahu has become the face of Israel abroad and a polarising figure at home. Supporters hail Netanyahu as "King Bibi" and see him as the strong leader Israel needs to defend itself in a hostile region. But, wanted by the International Criminal Court over alleged war crimes in Gaza which he rejects and on trial in Israel on corruption charges which he denies, he is fighting for his political life. Opinion polls have pointed to a sharp drop for his Likud party since the October 7 attack, which shattered Netanyahu's security credentials. His government's policies on matters of religion and state have also been unpopular among many Israelis. But Netanyahu, 77, is a consummate political survivor. He has said he wants to form a "broad national" government after the election, if he wins. In the event of a stalemate, he could remain a caretaker prime minister for many months. NETANYAHU'S TOP RIVALS * Former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, who lost a son in Gaza combat. Eisenkot, 66, has projected an image as a political outsider, soldier and security hawk whose humble background and family sacrifices stand in vivid contrast to Netanyahu's decades in high office and lingering corruption cases. He heads a new centrist party called Yashar, Hebrew for "straight" or "honest". * Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, 54, a right-wing former commando, former Netanyahu aide and high-tech millionaire who has joined forces with centrist former premier Yair Lapid. Their new party is called Together and its messages have focused on healing a traumatised nation and getting the country back on track. Their alliance, despite being on opposite ends of the political spectrum, ousted Netanyahu in a 2021 election. * Former Defence Minister Avigdor Lieberman, 68, was once a close ally of Netanyahu. Even more hawkish than his former boss, Lieberman quit Netanyahu's government in 2018, accusing the prime minister of being too soft on Palestinian militants in Gaza, and has become one of Netanyahu's sharpest critics. His party, Israel Our Home, draws much of its support from the country's ex-Soviet immigrant community. * Former general Yair Golan, 64, hailed for his rescue of people from one of the Hamas October 7 attack sites, leads the Democrats, founded on the moribund remnants of Israel's historical Labour party and smaller left-wing Meretz. CANDIDATES ON NETANYAHU'S SIDE Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, 46, and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, 50, have both drawn intense international scrutiny for their far-right policies toward the Palestinians. Smotrich has spearheaded Israel's rapid expansion of West Bank settlements, voicing his hope that it would 'bury' the idea of a Palestinian state. Ben-Gvir, who was convicted in 2007 of racist incitement against Arabs, has promoted capital punishment for convicted Palestinian militants, toughened prison conditions for jailed Palestinians and easier gun ownership for Israelis. Both men have advocated for the expulsion of Palestinians from the Gaza Strip and Israel resettling the enclave. ULTRA-ORTHODOX ALLIES Netanyahu has relied on two ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties, United Torah Judaism and Shas, for his political survival for years. Their demands for their community to be mostly exempt from compulsory military service, along with their low participation in the work force and reliance on state benefits, have angered many Israelis, all the more so at a time of war. POTENTIAL KEY PLAYERS Parties which are not clearly aligned with either side could tip the balance in favour of Netanyahu or his rivals. They include Raam and the Joint List, the two parties that represent Israel's 20% Arab minority. Along with them are a new right-wing party called People of Israel and a centre-right party called The Reservists, both of which have been wavering in opinion polls.

item.title: China says no secondary disasters, casualties from Tibet earthquake
item.description: China said on Monday there had been no secondary geological disasters and no further casualties from a magnitude-7 earthquake that struck China's southwestern region of Tibet last Friday, killing 16 people and injuring 76.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China said on Monday there had been no secondary geological disasters and no further casualties from a magnitude-7 [USN:L6N4690I3 TEXT:"earthquake"] that struck China's southwestern region of Tibet last Friday, killing 16 people and injuring 76. The country's Ministry of Natural Resources said in a statement that the "impact of this earthquake on glacier lakes and glaciers within the affected area was generally minimal" Since the earthquake there have been a total of 2,054 aftershocks, including two of at least 5.0 magnitude Authorities completed inspections of secondary geological disasters within a 50 km (31 miles) radius of the epicentre The [USN:L1N4680UK TEXT:"quake"] struck Nagqu, a high-altitude city in northern Tibet, a sparsely populated region of China, and was the strongest to hit the country since January 2024 Authorities inspected 157 geological disaster hazard points, including 122 existing hazards and 35 new hazard points, the ministry said. Experts analysed 80 glacial lakes and 145 glaciers within a 50-km radius of the earthquake, they said

item.title: Gold gains on softer oil prices; Fed decision in focus
item.description: Gold edged higher on Monday as softer oil prices tempered inflation concerns, while investors awaited the Federal Reserve's policy decision later this week.
item.dc:creator: Sukanya Mitra
item.content:encoded: Gold edged higher on Monday as softer oil prices tempered inflation concerns, while investors awaited the Federal Reserve's policy decision later this week. Spot gold rose 0.4% to $4,010.51 per ounce by 0544 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since mid-July in the previous session. Bullion posted a 4% weekly fall on Friday, its steepest weekly decline since June. US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.4% to $4,024.00. "The jump that we've seen is mostly symptomatic of the kind of relief provided by a lower oil price, but one that could easily be capped as markets position for the FOMC decision in a couple of days' time," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com. "Gold will continue to trade as a function of interest rate expectations and geopolitical risks." Oil prices [USN:L2N46B09G TEXT:"fell"] on Monday after surging to near six-month highs last week, amid hopes of easing hostilities between the United States and Iran, although ongoing attacks on [USN:L2N46A05D TEXT:"Saudi Arabia"] by Yemen's Houthis kept supply concerns in focus. [USN:S8N43E021 TEXT:"Qatari mediators"] were in Tehran on Sunday to help de-escalate regional tensions in coordination with the United States, an official briefed on the situation told Reuters. Markets await the Fed's policy meeting on October 27-28. The US Personal Consumption Expenditures data, a key gauge closely watched by the central bank as it targets a 2% inflation rate, is due the next day. Traders largely expect the central bank to leave rates unchanged this week, while expectations for a hike in December are at 77%, according to the CME's FedWatch Tool. Although gold is typically seen as an inflation hedge, higher interest rates tend to diminish non-yielding bullion's appeal to investors. Meanwhile, US business activity [USN:ZON00GOCU TEXT:"slowed modestly"] in October, though robust demand allowed companies to raise prices for goods and services, a sign that inflation could increase further and remain persistently high in the coming months. Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.6% to $54.19 per ounce, platinum dropped 0.2% to $1,548.30 and palladium gained 0.2% to $1,046.25.

item.title: South Korea's Lee says unlikely to join Pacific trade pact within his term
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Monday that the country would not be able to join the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) during his term.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Monday that the country would not be able to join the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) during his term. "We need to obtain permission from all 12 member countries" in the partnership if South Korea applies, Lee said at a meeting with farmers, fishermen and forestry workers. "The possibility that it will not be completed within my term is far higher." Lee's term runs until June 2030. Lee [USN:P8N44G02O TEXT:"instructed"] his ministers earlier this month to not pursue an application to join the trade group, citing significant impact on South Korean farmers. The CPTPP came into force in 2018, replacing the Trans-Pacific Partnership which fell apart after the US withdrew.

item.title: NHL roundup: Wild's Quinn Hughes makes winning return to Vancouver
item.description: Quinn Hughes scored a goal and had an assist while reaching the 500-point career mark in his return to Vancouver, and Kirill Kaprizov scored his league-leading 13th goal and also had an assist as the Minnesota Wild defeated the Canucks 4-2 on Sunday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Quinn Hughes scored a goal and had an assist while reaching the 500-point career mark in his return to Vancouver, and Kirill Kaprizov scored his league-leading 13th goal and also had an assist as the Minnesota Wild defeated the Canucks 4-2 on Sunday night. Hughes, playing his first game in Vancouver since he was sent to Minnesota in a blockbuster trade on Dec. 12, 2025, became the second-fastest American defenseman in NHL history to reach 500 career points. Brian Leetch accomplished the feat in 496 games while Hughes, who was booed each time he touched the puck, did it in 520 games. Maxim Shabanov scored a goal and had an assist and Bobby Brink also scored a goal for the Wild, who moved two points ahead of the Utah Mammoth into first place in the Central Division. Calvin Pickard, making just his second start of the season, finished with 15 saves for his first win with Minnesota. Max Sasson and Brock Boeser scored goals and Leevi Merilainen finished with 30 saves for the Canucks, who lost their 10th straight game (0-9-1). Canadiens 2, Jets 1 Jacob Fowler made 33 saves as Montreal edged Winnipeg in the Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic played outdoors at Princess Auto Stadium in Winnipeg. Lane Hutson and fellow defenseman Kaiden Guhle scored, and Cole Caufield had two assists for the Canadiens in the NHL's 46th outdoor game and 10th played in Canada. Isak Rosen scored a late goal and Stuart Skinner made 19 saves for the Jets, who have lost five in a row (0-3-2). Dawson Mercer made his Winnipeg debut after he was acquired from the New Jersey Devils as part of Friday's trade for goaltender Connor Hellebuyck and the forward had two shots in 15:22. Panthers 3, Blackhawks 2 Lars Eller tallied the go-ahead goal with 2:23 remaining in the third period and Sandis Vilmanis and Matthew Tkachuk also scored to lift visiting Florida to a victory against Chicago. Eller netted his first goal of the season at 17:37 of the third period as the Panthers caught the Blackhawks in a line change. Eller took a long pass from Aaron Ekblad just inside the blue line, weaved down the right side and ripped a wrist shot from the circle past Chicago goaltender Spencer Knight. Goaltender Akira Schmid stopped 19 shots as Florida snapped a two-game losing streak. Ryan Greene and Roman Kantserov scored while Knight made 30 saves for the Blackhawks, who went 0-for-7 on the power play. Chicago fell to 2-4-0 on a seven-game homestand that is set to conclude with Tuesday's visit from the Los Angeles Kings. Stars 6, Islanders 3 Jason Robertson scored two goals for his fourth straight multi-point performance, fueling host Dallas to a victory over New York. Robertson scored in the first period and converted on a breakaway in the third to boost his point total to 13 (five goals, eight assists) in his last nine games. Wyatt Johnston and Tyler Seguin each collected a goal and an assist, Mikko Rantanen and Justin Hryckowian also tallied and Jake Oettinger made 17 saves to send the Stars to their fifth straight victory. Dallas spoiled the return of Islanders head coach Pete DeBoer, who served as the Stars' bench boss for three seasons (2022-25) -- taking that club to the Western Conference final in each campaign. New York's Matthew Schaefer, 19, scored a goal for the second time in as many games and boosted his career total to 25, moving him past Hall of Famer Bobby Orr for the second most by a teenage defenseman in NHL history. Predators 6, Avalanche 2 Ryan O'Reilly scored twice, including the game-winner, and added two assists as host Nashville beat Colorado to avoid a third straight loss and win for just the second time in seven outings (2-2-3). Steven Stamkos scored a pair and contributed a helper for the Predators, Filip Forsberg had a goal and added two assists, and Jack Drury also tallied while Roman Josi added three helpers. Justus Annunen made 19 saves for his first win of the season. Artturi Lehkonen and Devon Toews responded for the Avalanche, who have lost three of four and dropped to 2-4-0 on the road. Martin Necas registered two assists, and Scott Wedgewood stopped 29 shots. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rybakina finds Ningbo spark again ahead of WTA Finals title defence
item.description: A year after winning the Ningbo Open transformed Elena Rybakina's season, the world number one returned to the Chinese city and retained her title on Sunday, as her game clicked into gear before another tilt at the WTA Finals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A year after winning the Ningbo Open transformed Elena Rybakina's season, the world number one returned to the Chinese city and retained her title on Sunday, as her game clicked into gear before another tilt at the WTA Finals. Her 2025 success proved the springboard for a stellar run as she secured the last spot in the eight-player WTA Finals field the following week, before winning the season finale and carrying that momentum into the current campaign. The 27-year-old Kazakh went on to capture the Australian Open title in January before claiming her third Grand Slam crown at the US Open last month. Rybakina's 6-2 6-2 win over Leylah Fernandez in the [USN:L2N46B01T TEXT:"Ningbo final"] on Sunday came after she had suffered defeat in her first match as world number one in Beijing and an injury-enforced absence from Wuhan. "It's the first time I've defended a title, so it's a great achievement," Rybakina told the WTA website. "Ningbo is already a special place. Last year I started to play really well from this tournament. Hopefully it's going to give me motivation and good energy to continue this season and start the next one." After losing nine of her first 13 finals, Rybakina has now won 11 of her last 15. "I remember I was getting upset always losing in finals," she said after winning her fourth title of the year and 15th overall. "Now it's going my way, but I can't expect it all the time ... now it's experience clicking in important moments." Rybakina plays in the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo this week before heading to Indian Wells for the November 8-15 WTA Finals, where she went unbeaten last year to pocket over $5 million in prize money.

item.title: Six injured in Russian strikes on Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia, Chernihiv, officials say
item.description: A Russian strike on Ukraine's southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia injured four people overnight, regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said on Telegram on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Russian strike on Ukraine's southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia injured four people overnight, regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said on Telegram on Monday. Two more were injured in Russian strikes on the Chernihiv region, Ukraine's emergency service said on the messaging app. Also on Telegram, the Russian defence ministry said it hit a power station in Ukraine's second largest city of Kharkiv, a warehouse in the surrounding region and another power station in the Khmelnitskiy region. In addition, it targeted port infrastructure in Chornomorsk and a cargo vessel en route to Odesa used for military purposes, the ministry said. The United States has pressed Ukraine to suspend strikes on Russian oil refineries, which it argues added to high energy prices, a sensitive issue for the Trump administration amid its war on Iran as midterm elections approach next month. In an interview aired on Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy [USN:L2N46B05O TEXT:"said"] that in order for Kyiv to halt the strikes, Moscow must stop hitting power infrastructure. Alternatively the United States should allow the use of Starshield over Russia to detect missile launch sites, or supply Ukraine with Patriot missiles, he added.

L'Arabie saoudite sera représentée par le ministre de la Défense, Khalid ben Salmane, et le Pakistan par le chef de l'armée, Asim Munir, ont précisé les sources. Le chef des services de renseignement turcs, Ibrahim Kalin, se joindra également à la réunion, a précisé l'une des sources. Le secrétaire adjoint de la plus haute instance de sécurité iranienne, Ali Bagheri Kani, a déclaré à la télévision publique saoudienne que Khalid ben Salmane, Asim Munir et Ibrahim Kalin se rendraient à Téhéran pour des consultations au sujet de la sécurité régionale avec le Conseil national suprême de la sécurité. item.title: Yasuo Fukuda, Japan's first second-generation prime minister, dies at 90, Nikkei reports
item.description: Former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda, who used his brief period in office to seek closer ties with Asian neighbours, particularly China, has died at the age of 90, the Nikkei business daily reported on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda, who used his brief period in office to seek closer ties with Asian neighbours, particularly China, has died at the age of 90, the Nikkei business daily reported on Monday. The Japanese politician, the first son of a prime minister to become premier himself, died on Thursday from heart failure, the Nikkei said. Becoming prime minister on the sudden resignation of Shinzo Abe in 2007, Fukuda lasted less than a year — a tenure even shorter than his father Takeo's two-year stint. A graduate in economics from Tokyo's prestigious Waseda University, Fukuda spent nearly two decades working his way up the ranks of an oil company — including a two-year posting in the United States — before resigning to become a political secretary when his father became premier in 1976. Elected to Japan's more powerful lower house of parliament in 1990, Fukuda was chief cabinet secretary from 2000 to 2004, resigning as one of several cabinet ministers to admit not paying into the pension system. Known for his testy manner, the bespectacled Fukuda drew criticism in 2003 for off-the-record comments in which he suggested women who dressed provocatively were asking to be raped. When Fukuda succeeded Abe he joked he might have drawn the short straw in assuming office given the divided parliament and opposition parties' ability to delay legislation. Frustrated with the stalled legislative process, Fukuda resigned in 2008, the second of six prime ministers to quit after only around a year in office. Known as a diplomatic dove, Fukuda made several visits to China after leaving office in an effort to improve often fraught relations. Fukuda leaves a son, Tatsuo, who is also a lawmaker and has been viewed as a potential future prime minister.

item.title: South Africa's Pick n Pay narrows first-half loss as turnaround gains traction
item.description: South African grocery retailer Pick n Pay said on Monday its turnaround gained further traction in the first half, with a narrower headline loss driven by improved gross margins and a strong contribution from value retailer Boxer .
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South African grocery retailer Pick n Pay (PIKJ.J) said on Monday its turnaround gained further traction in the first half, with a narrower headline loss driven by improved gross margins and a strong contribution from value retailer Boxer (BOXJ.J) . Headline loss for the 26-week period ended August 30 narrowed 31.9% to 299 million rand ($18 million), from 439 million rand a year earlier, while trading profit rose 58.1% to 490 million rand. South Africa's second-largest grocery retailer by southern Africa turnover is in the middle of a turnaround aimed at regaining customers and returning to profitability after years of market-share losses and underperforming stores. Its gross margin expanded 0.7 percentage points to 18.8%, supported by a better product mix and supply-chain improvements. Group turnover rose 2.4% to 60.5 billion rand, aided by Boxer's 6.3% growth, while the Pick n Pay business was broadly flat, reflecting strategic store closures over the past 12 months, the retailer said. While Boxer continued to anchor the group, the troubled Pick n Pay business reduced its trading loss by 16.9% to 516 million rand, with company-owned South African supermarkets recording like-for-like sales growth of 2.4%. ($1 = 16.5804 rand)

item.title: Down by the River Thames, a failure to build holds back Britain's growth
item.description: Near the marshes east of London, a £1 billion regeneration plan remains in limbo 17 years after it was first announced, an example of how rising UK building costs are adding to finance minister John Healey's growth challenge in this week's budget.
item.dc:creator: William Schomberg, Kate Holton, Suban Abdulla
item.content:encoded: Near the marshes east of London, a £1 billion regeneration plan remains in limbo 17 years after it was first announced, an example of how rising UK building costs are adding to finance minister John Healey's growth challenge in this week's budget. Local officials still have high hopes for the rebuilding of Purfleet-on-Thames, a popular riverside destination for day-trippers in the Victorian age and a hub of industry in the 20th century before most of the factories closed. But of about 3,000 planned new homes only 34 have been built after the original developers failed to persuade investors that the financial numbers made sense. For now, the area earmarked as a future town centre is still mostly a dusty industrial park with an overnight parking lot for truckers. Despite some progress in [USN:L8N4341LA TEXT:"streamlining Britain's complex planning system"], hopes for a quick pickup in [USN:L8N44M07R TEXT:"housebuilding"] and infrastructure - which could accelerate the broader economy - are being thwarted in part by the rising costs of construction. Interviews with more than 15 planning and policy experts, investors, business leaders and economists show how the accumulation of new policy demands is pushing up those costs. Combined with [USN:L6N45K0YA TEXT:"sluggish demand"] as interest rates climb, investors are wary, risking a further slowdown in housebuilding and leaving the government further from its targets. The new rules range from building safety - following the Grenfell Tower fire in 2017 which killed 72 people - to requirements to improve biodiversity and water quality and reduce carbon emissions. Gavin Barwell, a former housing minister, said governments had routinely failed to see how multiple policy demands, including worthy ones, can lead to "very significant" cumulative costs, on top of higher taxes, labour costs and inflation. "The problem could get worse, not better, if you don't address this," he told Reuters, of the need to build. Many property investors have reduced or halted their projects. Activity in the housebuilding sector has been shrinking for almost all of the last two years, according to a survey by S&P Global, a data firm. The Home Builders Federation (HBF) estimates 370,000 homes need planning permission every year to meet the government’s target of delivering [USN:L8N3XM0N6 TEXT:"1.5 million homes"] between 2024 and 2029, but approvals are currently running at just 58% of that level. Taylor Wimpey, a major homebuilder, has said rising costs - including from regulation - and affordability concerns mean it will not start new projects in London. The HBF said £76,000 had been added to the cost of building a home since 2020. Prosper UK, a pro-growth advocacy group headed by Barwell, says half of that is due to government decisions on regulation, policy and tax. SUPPORTERS ARGUE PURFLEET HAS HUGE POTENTIAL In Purfleet-on-Thames, officials are conducting due diligence before reviving the regeneration project with a new developer. The town is well located for commuters to London, only 30 minutes away by train, and for workers at international shipping ports nearby. But Thurrock Council documents show the project's previous developer struggled to raise debt and equity to meet high upfront costs for land adaptation and building infrastructure. A review by KPMG found the viability of a new, initial stage remains "highly constrained". It would require a lower-than-normal provision of affordable housing and £118 million of public funding, KPMG said, at a time when Healey's budget is under strain. Community representatives expect the regeneration to go ahead but say they have stopped updating local residents. "People have had their fill of broken promises," Trevor Batchelor, vice chair of the Purfleet-on-Thames Community Forum, said. UK ALSO STRUGGLES TO BUILD MAJOR INFRASTRUCTURE The problem is not limited to housebuilding. Around 10 miles further down the river from Purfleet, digging has finally begun on the £10 billion Lower Thames Crossing road tunnel first considered when Margaret Thatcher was prime minister in the 1980s. It is designed to unblock a choke point on Britain's haulage spine but has been held up by political wavering and a regulatory process slow even by UK standards. The planning application runs to more than 359,000 pages. Iain McNab, head of policy at the local Chambers of Commerce, said the uncertainty had hindered the area's businesses and given potential investors reasons to think twice. According to the Boston Consulting Group, the UK was the slowest among several countries it studied for infrastructure pre-construction work, of which planning is a big part. Chris Stratford, a consultant who worked on the Lower Thames Crossing, said failure by developers to work with local officials and environmental groups can cause delays. He said securing planning consent on a major infrastructure project could cost between £500 million and £1 billion. That is time and money that Britain can ill afford. The economy is on course to grow by 1.3% this year, according to the International Monetary Fund, among the fastest in the Group of Seven nations but less than half its average pace in the 15 years before the 2007-09 global financial crisis. The IMF expects UK growth to slow to 1.2% in 2027, leaving Healey caught between demands for more public spending in areas such as health, education and defence and a bond market that has pushed up the costs of borrowing worldwide. He is expected to announce few changes to tax and spending in his budget on Wednesday but has [USN:L8N4682B4 TEXT:"signalled plans"] to cut regulation and the cost of doing business. MORE HOUSEBUILDING COULD BOOST WIDER ECONOMY Industry experts say recent reforms should speed up the [USN:L5N3VU1A0 TEXT:"planning process"] as they make it harder for opponents to turn to the courts, remove some consultation requirements and give ministers more powers over decisions. Britain's budget forecasters say the changes could boost productivity and housing services, adding 0.2% to the economy's potential output by 2029, rising to 0.4% in the mid-2030s. But that growth will struggle to materialise if the industry cannot get building costs down. For Paul Johnson, chief economist at the 2030 Prosperity Alliance, which seeks to boost growth, housebuilding is the "one single change" that could make a meaningful difference to living standards. The lack of new housing pushes up prices which discourages people from moving for better jobs, encourages banks and investors to focus lending on property rather than businesses and infrastructure and eats into incomes. It also exacerbates homelessness which adds to financial pressures on local authorities. In Purfleet-on-Thames, Batchelor, the community representative, said he remained hopeful the regeneration would attract business to the area. "We've got plenty of people," he said. "We're just waiting for a town now."

item.title: Data centre's mea culpa is only least it could do
item.description: NextDC Chair Douglas Flynn is out and CEO Craig Scroggie loses his bonus. It's the bare minimum after poor planning wiped a third off earnings and halved the now-$2.9 bln firm's stock price. The next task is to convince investors the firm can still grow as borrowing costs spike.
item.dc:creator: Antony Currie
item.content:encoded: Trust Elon Musk to kick a rival data centre operator while it's down. On Sunday the CEO of SpaceX (SPCX.O) and Tesla (TSLA.O) [USN:L6N46B080 TEXT:"crowed"] that debt markets are essentially shut for any of them without "substantial revenue independent of AI". That's the bigger problem beleaguered Australian outfit NextDC (NXT.AX) faces now that it has done the bare minimum to try to soothe its shareholders after its stock price halved over the past few days. Community protests against expansion at a key Melbourne facility prompted months-long delays, forcing NextDC last week to slash its EBITDA forecast by more than a third and prompting the stock rout. So on Monday the now-$2.9 billion company said CEO Craig Scroggie would forgo both his short- and long-term bonuses for this financial year. On top of that, Chair Douglas Flynn is stepping down and the entire board is taking a 10% pay cut. There was a need for such speedy appeasement: NextDC's annual general meeting is in less than four weeks, where there was to be a vote, now withdrawn, on increasing board remuneration by 13%. Worse, at last year's gathering 72% of shareholders voted against the company's executive pay, in large part due to long-term incentives that could bag more than $100 million for Scroggie. If just 25% vote against this year's payout plan, Australian rules allow investors to vote on ousting the whole board. Sure, the company remains profitable and has, as Scroggie was keen to point out last week, $6.1 billion of liquidity - much of it in untapped credit lines. But data centre builders are in constant need for more debt, which finances up to 90% of construction. And getting hold of it was already tricky: after NextDC baulked at paying 8.5% on new borrowings earlier this year, it sold a [USN:L6N40R08B TEXT:"$700 million century bond"], to La Caisse, whose initial 7.5% rate rises above 9.2% in 2031 - and has to retroactively pay that amount from the get-go if it buys the debt back. That suddenly looks like a good deal: NextDC would have to pay 10.3% if it tried to borrow now, based on where some of its debt is trading, per LSEG. NextDC has halted work on projects without signed customer contracts and is mulling whether to sell undeveloped land. That, existing liquidity and the lack of any major bond issues maturing until 2031 give Scroggie time to try to show both his debt and equity investors that he has learned his lesson. But in an industry that has pinned its fortunes on hyper-fast growth, that's a hard job for a company that's either slowing or reversing quickly. Follow Antony Currie on Bluesky and LinkedIn . Craig Scroggie, CEO of beleaguered data centre builder and operator NextDC, is to forgo his bonus for the 2027 financial year, which runs to the end of June, the company said on October 26. Board directors will take a 10% cut in fees, rather than the 13.6% increase that shareholders were set to vote on at the company's annual meeting next month. Chair Douglas Flynn "has reaffirmed his intention to retire from the board once a new chairman is in place, after a short handover period," as was stated in the company release to the stock exchange. The company had not previously confirmed in public that he was leaving. The company is also now seeking a new independent director as well as a new chair. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Spain’s housing quandary stretches worldwide
item.description: Plunged into instability by a 750,000-home shortage, the Iberian nation is an extreme example of a problem spanning from Boston to Brisbane. Since 2008, construction spurred by suburban sprawl has become less profitable. Political inertia will leave supply tied to another bubble.
item.dc:creator: Jon Sindreu
item.content:encoded: An inhospitable truth is that without credit and asset bubbles, housing supply tends to be constrained. The problem common to Barcelona, Boston and Brisbane is that construction often just isn't profitable enough. Spain provides an extreme example. Between 2021 and 2025, the country built fewer than 400,000 dwellings as it absorbed 1.9 million migrants. The situation triggered a political crisis, with Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez calling a snap general election for next month. The Bank of Spain has urged a relaxation of planning permissions to address the 750,000-home shortfall. Between 2000 and 2006, the country expanded housing stock by 15%, despite its population growing only 10%, according to the EMF Hypostat statistical compilation. Closer analysis undercuts the widely held view that a bubble merely generated empty assets bid up by speculators. For one, the extra homes accommodated flexible family structures and ageing societies. Even when population growth outpaced that of dwellings at the peak of the building craze, there was a strong correlation between the two across advanced nations, OECD data shows, as well as in US, British and Spanish metropolitan areas. Tellingly, the number of second homes in Spain barely increased during this stretch. All of these relationships weakened or vanished after the global financial crisis. Where rising incomes once translated into more construction, they now mostly feed into prices . Spain illustrates the pitfalls of breaking more ground as a broad solution. Economic activity is increasingly concentrated in a handful of places, which attract immigrants. Even suburbs regarded as overbuilt ghost towns in 2008 have filled up. Meanwhile, municipalities such as Soria and Cuenca in the sparsely populated interior regions keep losing residents. Unlike in the 1990s and 2000s, big cities aren't quickly spreading outward anymore, according to a 2024 Nature paper based on satellite and scatterometer data. Many now grow upward. The change has been dubbed "the closing of the suburban frontier" by economists Edward Glaeser and Joseph Gyourko. Sun Belt sprawl in Dallas, Miami and Phoenix increasingly resembles more concentrated Boston and New York. The problem traces back to educated suburban dwellers pushing politicians to tighten land-use rules, as noted by sociologist Jorge Galindo, who runs Spanish think tank EsadeEcPol. Even so, a construction slowdown so consistent across richer countries reflects broader forces. Fast sprawl just isn't as economically viable anymore. In Spain, the construction industry generated a 4% return on equity in 2024, compared with 10% before the financial crisis, BBVA analysts estimated . Blame the credit crunch that hit Spain particularly hard: mortgage volume halved to 30% of GDP while construction loans tumbled to 10% from 40%. Local banks that once financed all sorts of land redevelopment now only step in near the end of a project and demand pre-sales of 80% to 90%, according to consultancy Tinsa. Without leverage, return-on-equity targets become harder to reach, especially because materials and labour inflation have pushed costs up 50% relative to 2008. It therefore makes sense that homes beyond the wealthy suburbs are the ones going un-built. As travel from city centres stretches beyond an hour, demand relies on lower-income buyers currently unable to climb the property ladder. Red tape contributes to project delays, but so do workforce and funding shortages. It turns out that bubbly conditions were essential. Between 2002 and 2005, Spanish homes increased more than 15% in value annually, practically guaranteeing solid returns. Over the past decade, however, average price growth has been 4%, which is why the country only builds two dwellings per 1,000 people a year, compared to 6.6 in Australia, for example. Home prices Down Under kept rising after 2008, hitting new highs during the pandemic. These cycles do self-correct: Melbourne, which recorded strong price and construction growth after 2013, is experiencing fast home deflation. In Brisbane, however, where sprawl slowed down more, prices are now surging. Around the planet in Austin, local authorities engineered a deregulation-led supply surge after 2017, but the effect is already fading and rents are rising again. Spain's central bank grasps these dynamics and is pushing big cities to permit more dwellings per square foot. In Madrid, Barcelona and Málaga, mature neighborhoods are 2 times to 2.5 times denser than planned developments. Revised zoning laws could clear the way for some 1.2 million extra homes in the country's top six metro areas, officials estimate. But profitability constraints make such forecasts highly optimistic. Building skyward raises costs per square meter, even on empty plots. At some height, money spent on stronger structures, lifts and parking will offset savings from less land. There's a strong relationship between Spanish municipalities that were denser in 2011 and those experiencing less housing growth relative to population, a Breakingviews analysis suggests. Much low-hanging fruit was probably culled before 2008. Indeed, a decade after New York City's efforts to relax "up-zoning" rules, only 9% of newly permitted floor space was built, economist Vincent Rollet found. Few areas are expensive enough to generate the required returns for very tall buildings, but sufficiently low density to manage the costs. Although former industrial sites in Manhattan's Hudson Yards fit the bill, plans for Sunnyside Yard in Queens have stalled for years. One proposed solution: the public sector supporting construction by extending loans with lower repayment priority to contractors. Deliberately boosting private-sector profit margins, however, will be a hard sell for left-wing governments, including Spain's under Sánchez. Instead, he is touting rent control and strong tenant [USN:L6N45O0I7 TEXT:"protections"], echoing New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani. An alternative is for governments to reclaim a role as big builders, perhaps using the AI data-centre boom to [USN:L6N44O0PB TEXT:"create"] new accessible suburbs. They also could use taxpayer money to [USN:L6N41P0WZ TEXT:"buy"] enough homes in key urban areas and make them available to suitable longtime residents. A version of this works in Vienna. Otherwise, it might fall to another debt-powered bubble for the cyclical construction industry to meet housing demand. As Spain itself shows, that cure is far worse than the disease. item.title: Quinn Hughes hits milestone in Vancouver return as Wild best Canucks
item.description: Quinn Hughes scored a goal and had an assist while reaching the 500-point career mark in his return to Vancouver, and Kirill Kaprizov scored his league-leading 13th goal and also had an assist as the Minnesota Wild defeated the Canucks 4-2 on Sunday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Quinn Hughes scored a goal and had an assist while reaching the 500-point career mark in his return to Vancouver, and Kirill Kaprizov scored his league-leading 13th goal and also had an assist as the Minnesota Wild defeated the Canucks 4-2 on Sunday night. Hughes, playing his first game in Vancouver since he was sent to Minnesota in a blockbuster trade on Dec. 12, 2025, became the second-fastest American defenseman in NHL history to reach 500 career points. Brian Leetch accomplished the feat in 496 games while Hughes, who was booed each time he touched the puck, did it in 520 games. Maxim Shabanov scored a goal and had an assist and Bobby Brink also scored a goal for Minnesota, which moved two points ahead of the Utah Mammoth into first place in the Central Division with the win. Calvin Pickard, making just his second start of the season, finished with 15 saves for his first win with the Wild. Max Sasson and Brock Boeser scored goals and Leevi Merilainen finished with 30 saves for Vancouver, which lost its 10th straight game (0-9-1). Minnesota, playing the second game of a back-to-back that began with a 5-1 victory at Seattle on Saturday night, took a 1-0 lead at the 18:33 mark of the first period on a power-play goal by Shabanov, who scooped in a cross-crease pass from Kaprizov inside the right post for his third goal. Brink extended the lead to 2-0 early in the second period when he took a pass from Michael McCarron at the top of the right circle and broke in, deking Merilainen and tucking a backhand shot inside the right post. Hughes then picked up his milestone 500th career point on the power play, slapping a shot inside a wide-open right side of the goal on a rebound of a Joel Eriksson Ek shot. Hughes picked up career point No. 501 early in the third period when he found Kaprizov breaking down the middle of the ice between a pair of Canuck defenders. Kaprizov finished his rush with a backhand shot around Merilainen's left pad to make it 4-0. Sasson broke up the shutout at the 6:24 mark of the third period with a breakaway score off a long stretch pass by Filip Hronek. Boeser cut the lead to 4-2 with 3:07 left when he snapped in a shot from the high slot for his third goal. --Field Level Media

item.title: India to evacuate thousands as Cyclone Arnab nears eastern coast
item.description: Two states along India's eastern coast were preparing to evacuate thousands of people ahead of Cyclone Arnab, which is expected to make landfall on Wednesday, as one of them said it would close schools in some districts for two days.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Two states along India's eastern coast were preparing to evacuate thousands of people ahead of Cyclone Arnab, which is expected to make landfall on Wednesday, as one of them said it would close schools in some districts for two days. Arnab, which formed over the Bay of Bengal before intensifying into a cyclonic storm, is expected to make landfall in Andhra Pradesh state by Wednesday morning, with gusts of as much as 140 kph (87 mph), India's weather office said. The cyclone will probably intensify further, it added. The weather system is expected to bring heavy to extremely heavy rainfall to Andhra Pradesh's northern and central coastal districts, and southern regions of neighbouring Odisha. Andhra Pradesh has called for boats at sea to return ashore and ordered speedy restoration of power in case of disruptions. A senior Andhra Pradesh disaster management official told Reuters on Monday the state government had identified 570,000 people as vulnerable and evacuations would start on Monday evening. Odisha's government announced the closure of schools and colleges in five districts for Tuesday and Wednesday, and said it was preparing to move residents of low-lying areas to cyclone shelters. The Bay of Bengal is one of the world's major regions for tropical cyclones.
