item.title: Jio IPO rings home on promise of possibility
item.description: The telecom company's $3.2 bln deal drew strong demand despite global jitters, underscoring the Ambani clan's allure. Investors get their digital ambitions at a dumb pipe valuation multiple. It cushions risks from Jio’s 2020 backers, who paid for the dream and still need an exit.
item.dc:creator: Ujjaini Dutta
item.content:encoded: Jio Platform’s (JIOP.NS) successful share sale underscores an enduring belief in the Ambanis' ability to generate shareholder value. Their telecom company has pulled off India’s largest IPO despite AI jitters roiling global tech stocks. But the $3.2 billion issuance was also priced to do well. Investors are getting the family's digital ambitions at a "dumb-pipe" valuation multiple. That cushions risks from Jio’s 2020 backers who paid up for that dream and still need an exit. Institutional investors were the most emphatic, with subscriptions hitting 71 times the shares offered to them. Foreign institutional buyers accounted for 28% of the overall bids. Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, BlackRock (BLK.N) , Fidelity and others popped up in the anchor book. Retail investors were offered twice as many shares as institutions, and were more circumspect, but their portion was still nearly three times oversubscribed. They all stand to benefit if the Ambanis can deliver on their vision of Jio as a technology platform rather than just a telecom operator with some 524 million mobile subscribers. Akash Ambani, Jio's managing director, insists the difference between the 10-year-old venture he leads within Reliance Industries (RELI.NS) and its older telecom rival, Bharti Airtel (BRTI.NS) , is that the upstart merely uses connectivity as its distribution layer and has proprietary tech that can be licensed internationally. There may be something to that: revenue from digital services including gaming, cloud computing, Internet of Things and cloud PC accounts for just 12% of Jio's top line but that business grew 36% year-on-year at the end of March 2026, more than twice as fast as overall revenue. For now, investors are getting those dreams for free. At the $109 billion implied IPO market value, Jio commands a multiple of 31 times its earnings for 2027, per Visible Alpha estimates, a negligible difference to Airtel's 30 times. Investors also had to weigh the Ambanis' digital dreams against risks including the potential disruption from satellite-based connectivity: Elon Musk's Starlink has been waiting since 2022 to operate commercially in India and, if granted access, would be a direct competitor. There’s also a potential overhang as global investors that bought into Jio six years ago may seek an exit once a six-month lock-up period expires. Financial investors led by KKR (KKR.N) and Silver Lake own about 15% of the company. For their shares, they paid 23 times Jio’s annualised EBITDA, against its current valuation multiple of 12 times. Jio's latest buyers have less to lose. Follow Ujjaini Dutta on LinkedIn and X . Jio Platforms, the telecom unit of India's Reliance Industries, on October 24 set the offer price for its IPO at 1119 rupees per share, at the top end of the marketed range. It values the company's issuance at $3.18 billion and its equity at $109 billion. Jio drew bids for 4.4 billion shares, about 22 times the 197 million shares on offer after three days of bidding, exchange data showed. Qualified institutional buyers bid for nearly 71 times the shares reserved for them, while foreign institutional investors accounted for 28% of the total bids received. Non-institutional investors subscribed 14 times their share, while retail investors bid for about 3 times their allotted portion. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: China's domestic car sales seen rising 2% in 2027 after 2026 slump
item.description: China's domestic passenger vehicle market is set to stage a modest recovery in 2027 after a steeper-than-expected downturn this year, a senior industry executive said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's domestic passenger vehicle market is set to stage a modest recovery in 2027 after a steeper-than-expected downturn this year, a senior industry executive said on Monday. Domestic car sales are set to fall to 18.5 million vehicles in 2026, versus 23.7 million in 2025, before rebounding by a median 2% in 2027, said Cui Dongshu, secretary-general of the China Passenger Car Association. Behind the recovery will be the fading of short-term headwind, easing cost pressure and improved product offering, though competition is likely to become increasingly polarised, Cui said.

item.title: NBA roundup: Luka Doncic explodes for 52 to lead Lakers past Jazz
item.description: Luka Doncic scored 52 points and added 10 assists and eight rebounds to lead the Los Angeles Lakers to a 132-123 victory over the Utah Jazz on Sunday in Salt Lake City.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Luka Doncic scored 52 points and added 10 assists and eight rebounds to lead the Los Angeles Lakers to a 132-123 victory over the Utah Jazz on Sunday in Salt Lake City. Doncic made 8 of 18 3-point attempts as part of 17-of-30 shooting performance as the Lakers improved to 3-0. It marked the 10th time he scored 50 or more points in a regular-season game. Austin Reaves added 29 points for Los Angeles. Doncic and Reaves combined for 21 of 24 from the free-throw line. Walker Kessler tallied only two points and seven rebounds in his first game back in Utah after being sent by the Jazz to Los Angeles in a trade over the summer. Lauri Markkanen scored 28 points to lead Utah, which blew an 18-point second-quarter lead. Keyonte George tallied 24 points, 10 assists and nine rebounds for the Jazz. Jaren Jackson Jr. added 20 points while Ace Bailey chipped in 17 points and 12 rebounds. Thunder 108, Clippers 101 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 34 points to lead Oklahoma City to a home win over Los Angeles. Darius Garland led the Clippers with 16 points and 11 assists. With just more than a minute remaining, Thunder star Jalen Williams went down hard with a left leg injury on a foul by Derrick Jones Jr. Williams started to try to get up after the fall but teammate Chet Holmgren motioned for him to remain down. Williams was eventually carted off on a stretcher, offering a thumbs up to the crowd as they chanted his nickname. Williams was the third rotation player injured in the game for the Thunder. Cason Wallace left the game less than halfway through the first quarter with left shoulder soreness after a collision coming off a screen. At the end of the first, Jaylin Williams exited with right wrist soreness. Pacers 136, Nets 109 Tyrese Haliburton scored 20 of his 24 points after halftime as Indiana took control late in the first half and dominated the third quarter en route to a 136-109 victory over Brooklyn on Sunday night in New York. Haliburton made 8 of 13 shots and hit 4 of 7 3-point tries in his best game since returning from a torn right Achilles tendon that robbed him of the 2025-26 season. Pascal Siakam added 21 points, seven rebounds and six assists for the Pacers. Reserve Obi Toppin contributed 16 points. Andrew Nembhard and Kelly Oubre Jr. finished with 14 points. Nolan Traore took advantage of extended minutes and led the Nets with 17 points. Josh Minott added 15 and Moritz Wagner chipped in 13 for Brooklyn, which lost its third straight game to begin the season. Magic 111, Knicks 102 Franz Wagner scored 21 of his 23 points in the fourth quarter for visiting Orlando, which overcame a 10-point deficit in the final nine-plus minutes to beat defending NBA champion New York. Wagner (13 rebounds, nine assists) came within one assist of a triple-double for the undermanned Magic, who improved to 1-2 despite the absence of Paolo Banchero, who is expected to miss at least a month with an ankle injury sustained in Orlando's 115-93 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves on Friday. Desmond Bane scored 22 points and hit the 3-pointer that gave the Magic the lead for good with 4:53 left. The Knicks fell to 0-3 -- the first time a reigning champ has opened 0-3 since the Dallas Mavericks in 2011-12. Karl-Anthony Towns (22 points, 14 rebounds) posted a double-double for New York while Jalen Brunson scored a game-high 28 points. OG Anunoby scored 22, and Josh Hart added 13 points. Timberwolves 117, Raptors 94 Anthony Edwards scored 26 points on 10-for-18 shooting, and Minnesota pulled away for a win over Toronto in Minneapolis to remain unbeaten on the season. LaMelo Ball finished with 15 points and eight assists for the Timberwolves. Terrence Shannon Jr. also scored 15 points off the bench, and Jaden McDaniels recorded 14 points on 6-for-10 shooting. Ja'Kobe Walter scored 22 points on 7-for-12 shooting to lead the Raptors, who sustained their first loss after starting the season with back-to-back wins. RJ Barrett added 20 points, and Immanuel Quickley scored 19. Scottie Barnes was 0-for-12, including 0-for-5 from distance, in 28 minutes. Raptors star forward Kawhi Leonard was scratched before the game because of swelling in his left knee. Pistons 106, 76ers 93 Cade Cunningham notched 26 points, eight rebounds and eight assists as visiting Detroit downed previously unbeaten Philadelphia. The Pistons improved to 3-0 despite playing without two starters, as center Jalen Duren (hamstring) and guard Ausar Thompson (ankle) sat out the contest. That created more opportunities for Duncan Robinson (21 points), Daniss Jenkins (18 points) and John Collins (16 points, 11 rebounds). Tyrese Maxey scored 18 of his 29 points in the fourth quarter for the 76ers, who played without center Joel Embiid (foot) and guard VJ Edgecombe (abdomen). LeBron James chipped in with 18 points, while Jaylen Brown had 16 on 5-of-20 shooting for Philadelphia, which never led while falling to 3-1 on the young season. Grizzlies 123, Kings 112 Isaiah Stewart and Ty Jerome converted three-point plays to bookend a late 11-0 flurry and Memphis remained undefeated with a road victory over the winless Sacramento Kings. Jerome finished with 31 points while Cameron Boozer (16 points, 11 rebounds) and Cedric Coward (15 points, 11 rebounds) each recorded a double-double for the Grizzlies, who elected to rest star center Zach Edey on the first night of a road back-to-back set. Sacramento's Zach LaVine was the game's leading scorer with 37 points. Rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. had 22 to go with a game-high seven assists, while center Domantas Sabonis, fighting foul trouble much of the night, put up a 15-point, 15-rebound double-double for the Kings. --Field Level Media

item.title: Fiji light up World Cup despite defeat as heavyweights march on
item.description: Fiji breathed life into a Rugby League World Cup blighted by lopsided contests by going toe to toe with Australia on Sunday, though the defending champions survived to book their place in the semi-finals.
item.dc:creator: Ian Ransom
item.content:encoded: Fiji breathed life into a Rugby League World Cup blighted by lopsided contests by going toe to toe with Australia on Sunday, though the defending champions survived to book their place in the semi-finals. In a tournament rapidly turning into a procession for the established powers, Fiji threatened one of the great World Cup upsets in front of 41,000 fans at Brisbane's Lang Park after leading 16-12 early in the second half. That was before Kangaroos captain James Tedesco turned the tide and Tom "Turbo" Trbojevic completed a hat-trick as the favourites emerged with a 36-22 victory. Fiji winger Semi Valemei also crossed three times while playmaker Kurt Donoghoe was named player of the match after repeatedly exposing the Kangaroos' defence. Defeat notwithstanding, Fiji's performance was a major confidence boost before they meet New Zealand on the Gold Coast on Saturday with a semi-final berth on the line. "It was just outstanding tonight," said Fiji coach Mick Potter. "They showed courage, they showed they can play footy. "Even with the short turnaround, we'll be ready for (New Zealand)." New Zealand bounced back from their opening loss against Australia with an 82-16 demolition of Cook Islands in Christchurch, where Jamayne Isaako scored three tries in a record 38-point haul, the biggest by a Kiwi in a test. Unheralded Cook Islands back Esom Ioka improved his chances of earning a National Rugby League (NRL) contract with a hat-trick, including two long-range efforts from intercepts. ENGLAND REBOUND England also ran riot, thrashing France 82-0 in Perth to revive their semi-final hopes after an opening defeat by Tonga. Herbie Farnworth and Dom Young scored hat-tricks as England piled on 14 tries. "I'm really pleased with how we responded to the (Tonga) result, really," England coach Brian McDermott said. "The scoreline (30-12) wasn't good last week but I thought we played really well." England must now beat Papua New Guinea convincingly on Friday and will cheer for a Tonga win by a healthy margin over Samoa to remain in the hunt for the semis. Samoa, runners-up in England four years ago, underlined their quality by crushing Papua New Guinea 64-6 in Port Moresby, with prop Spencer Leniu igniting a devastating second-half onslaught three weeks after a match-turning performance off the bench for the Sydney Roosters in the NRL Grand Final. The hosts' heavy loss underlined a need for more investment at international level despite a sell-out crowd at the National Football Stadium and the coming entry of the PNG Chiefs into the NRL. Chiefs' marquee recruit Jarome Luai was given a hero's welcome by local fans despite captaining Samoa to victory, leaving the field in his underwear after throwing every item of his playing kit into the crowd. Tonga notched up another big win as they shut out Michael Cheika-coached Lebanon 36-0, setting up the Pacific showdown with unbeaten Samoa in Sydney on Sunday. Cheika said Lebanon's second defeat was an improvement on their 42-18 loss to PNG but underscored the massive gap between the game's top nations and the rest. "We tried to get a warmup match but we weren't allowed," he said of the only Asian nation represented at the 10-team tournament. "It's not easy for us. We haven't played a game since the World Cup of last time."

item.title: Indonesia strengthens measures against stock manipulation after market rout triggered by MSCI
item.description: Indonesia on Monday introduced more measures to address stock market manipulation, including adding independent parties to a committee determining stocks with concentrated ownership structures, after MSCI said the country could be demoted due to concerns about opaque trading.
item.dc:creator: Stefanno Sulaiman
item.content:encoded: Indonesia on Monday introduced more measures to address stock market manipulation, including adding independent parties to a committee determining stocks with concentrated ownership structures, after MSCI said the country could be demoted due to concerns about opaque trading. The measures came after MSCI announced earlier this month that it could demote Indonesia's stock exchange to [USN:L6N46208E TEXT:""standalone" market status"], saying not enough had been done to [USN:L4N46509U TEXT:"arrest coordinated trading practices"] in its stock market. That was more severe than the global index provider's January warning that it could downgrade the country to "frontier" status. At present, MSCI still classifies Indonesia as an "emerging" market. The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) plans to expand the membership of a committee that comes up with a list of stocks with high shareholder concentration to include independent parties like Indonesian academics and F. Chapman Taylor as a representative of foreign investors, chief Jeffrey Hendrik said at a press conference. Previously, the committee members were officials from capital market authorities. Taylor is a former partner with investment company the Capital Group and is currently an adviser to Indonesia's sovereign wealth fund, Danantara. "We encourage the IDX to strengthen the mechanism and methodology of trading supervision, including its capacity to identify patterns of irregular transactions, detect coordinated trading and strengthen the mechanism to respond to such events," said Hasan Fawzi, the financial regulator's capital market supervisor. Last week, the IDX said it would [USN:L1N46804O TEXT:"exclude stocks"] with high shareholding concentrations from its main Jakarta index (.JKSE) starting on November 2. The current list includes 80 companies. The MSCI downgrade warning spurred Indonesia's deepest-ever two-day stock selloff on October 16 and 19, sending the main index to its lowest point since 2020. It has since rebounded. At 0320 GMT on Monday, the index was down around 0.6%. The rupiah weakened 0.4% to its weakest point since July. POSSIBLE COORDINATED TRADING TRIGGERS INVESTIGATION The exchange also plans to launch investigations when it detects possible coordinated trading to manipulate share prices and freeze suspicious investor accounts, Hendrik said. The new measure, to take effect in November, is more proactive than the IDX's previous response. The IDX previously warned public investors of unusual market activities when a stock price moved sharply and requested an explanation from the company. The process could also lead to a temporary freeze in share trading. A policy that allows share buybacks without requiring approval from a general shareholders meeting has also been extended until June 2027, Hasan said, adding that any buyback must consider rules about the minimum free float, or shares available to trade in the market. Hasan said Indonesia has been communicating with MSCI and other global index providers like FTSE Russell to reiterate its regulators' commitment to market reforms. The market showed resilience following MSCI's (MSCI.N) recent announcement, Hasan said, describing local investors as "mature" and "wise" for buying stocks in companies with good fundamentals. President Prabowo Subianto told his cabinet last week that MSCI was trying to "intimidate" Indonesia, but said the country would not be afraid, striking a combative tone in his first public reaction to the [USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"downgrade "][USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"warning"]. Since MSCI's January warning, Indonesia has launched a series of reforms including releasing more details on investor accounts and ownership data, increasing the minimum free-float level and unveiling [USN:L1N4670MN TEXT:"record fines"] against parties involved in market manipulation.

item.title: India's Shriram Finance hits 11-month low as growth outlook cut, credit costs weigh
item.description: Shares of India's Shriram Finance fell to an 11-month low on Monday after the non-bank lender lowered its annual loan growth forecast and warned of higher credit costs, overshadowing a better-than-expected second-quarter profit.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shares of India's Shriram Finance (SHMF.NS) fell to an 11-month low on Monday after the non-bank lender [USN:L4N4690PL TEXT:"lowered"] its annual loan growth forecast and warned of higher credit costs, overshadowing a better-than-expected second-quarter profit. Shares fell as much as 6.13% to 810.20 rupees, extending losses from Friday, and were on track for an eighth consecutive session of declines. The company cut its assets under management growth forecast for fiscal 2027 to 15%-17% from 18%, citing weak monsoon conditions and geopolitical uncertainty, and flagged pressure on borrowers in drought-hit regions. Jefferies said credit costs could remain elevated for another one to two quarters as stress rises in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana. The brokerage maintained its "buy" rating but cut its target price to 1,145 rupees from 1,210 rupees. Higher slippages and write-offs reflected drought-like conditions in several states, Motilal Oswal said, adding that the lender's overall asset quality remained broadly stable. JM Financial said rising early-stage delinquencies and drought-related stress among rural borrowers remained key concerns for Shriram Finance. The brokerage maintained its "buy" rating but cut its target price to 1,025 rupees from 1,175 rupees, citing deteriorating asset quality indicators. Shriram Finance reported a nearly 60% jump in second-quarter profit to 36.77 billion rupees ($387.30 million) on Friday, beating analysts' estimate of 35.46 billion rupees, according to LSEG-compiled data. ($1 = 94.9400 Indian rupees)

item.title: Investors expect Brazilian stocks, currency to fall after Lula reelected
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won reelection on Sunday, defeating right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and setting up a test for financial markets, with investors expecting recent bets on a change of government to unwind in a volatile week ahead.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Campos, Marcela Ayres
item.content:encoded: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva [USN:L6N4681ER TEXT:"won reelection on Sunday"], defeating right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and setting up a test for financial markets, with investors expecting recent bets on a change of government to unwind in a volatile week ahead. November futures for the Brazilian real were down 10% in Asian hours while a Tokyo-listed Brazilian stock exchange-traded fund, the Nomura NF Ibovespa Link ETF (1325.T) , plunged 15%. Markets had moved sharply in anticipation of a right-wing shift since Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former President Jair Bolsonaro, unexpectedly finished first in the opening round three weeks ago. Stocks (.BVSP) closed on Friday almost 7% above their level going into the first round, while the real currency was nearly 5% stronger against the US dollar. Interest-rate futures had indicated expectations that tighter public finances would allow borrowing costs to decline. "We expect a sharp market reaction on Monday, with aggressive repricing, a selloff in assets and interest rate futures likely to hit their upper limit shortly after the open," said Luis Felipe Vital, head of macro strategy at Warren Investimentos. Over the next four years, Lula must slow the growth of Brazil’s debt while protecting social programs and investment. For investors, the question is whether his gradual approach to fixing public finances can bring borrowing costs down. Without confidence that he can deliver, lenders could demand higher interest rates, adding to the government’s debt and making credit more expensive for businesses and households. "Investors want a clear and credible commitment to fiscal discipline," said Alejo Czerwonko, chief investment officer for emerging markets at UBS Global Wealth Management. "We expect the rally that followed the first round to be largely priced out, and sentiment to stay weak until a clear fiscal plan emerges." Czerwonko said investors are looking for a halt to the spending that accompanied the campaign and a believable path to stabilize public debt. "It also means a working relationship with an opposition-leaning Congress, because no fiscal plan passes without it," he said. Lula’s team aims to produce a budget surplus before interest payments of about 1.3% of gross domestic product by 2030. That would leave money to cover part of the interest bill, reducing the need for fresh borrowing. But public debt already exceeds 82% of GDP, while pensions and other legally required spending limit where savings can come from. "Lula's policies have talked about spending cuts, but he's not gone into the details of how that is going to look like," said Divya Singaravelu, head of research at Meridian 1305 Capital. She said the choice of the next finance minister would be an early signal to markets, adding: "We want to see what the 2027 budget and spending cap looks like." Whoever takes the job will need to explain how campaign commitments fit within those fiscal limits. "The key point is that, even if pessimism prevails in the near term, investors will need to watch how the government's economic agenda advances over the medium term," said Gustavo Sung, chief economist at Suno Research. "The main thing to watch now is how the government organizes itself for 2027."

item.title: How purchases of sanctioned Iranian jet fuel were disguised by Myanmar
item.description: In December 2025, the US-sanctioned tanker Reef arrived in Myanmar waters with some 113,000 barrels of fuel backed by sham paperwork.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: In December 2025, the US-sanctioned tanker Reef arrived in Myanmar waters with some 113,000 barrels of fuel backed by sham paperwork. Myanmar-based energy broker Dynamic Wave ordered the shipment, agreeing in a sales contract inked with Thailand’s Tawan-Oil Trading to supposedly take delivery of a similar amount of South African diesel. But the $15.8 million agreement, which Reuters viewed, was a charade: there was no such trade between South Africa and Myanmar in 2025, according to data from the United Nations and Vortexa, a shipping and energy data provider. In reality, Reef carried jet fuel from Iran to Myanmar, according to records of fuel shipments to Myanmar, as well as satellite images and analysis by SynMax Intelligence, which tracked the tanker’s journey from the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas to Southeast Asia. The deception was needed because the US in 2023 imposed targeted sanctions on Myanmar’s jet-fuel industry. The US [USN:L1N35V1MA TEXT:"did so citing the deadly bombing campaign"] waged by the Southeast Asian country’s military on civilian targets as part of an effort to crush a rebel-led insurgency. All purchasers of Iranian oil and fuel are also exposed to sweeping American sanctions. Details of how Myanmar disguised purchases of Iranian jet fuel, as well as the entities involved in the transactions, are reported here for the first time. Myanmar’s military junta was involved in the ruse. Days before Reef arrived, Myanmar’s foreign exchange regulator told the client of Dynamic Wave that it would issue import documentation that labeled the delivery as diesel “instead of jet fuel,” according to a copy of the agency’s November 30 letter seen by Reuters. The document, which was provided to Reuters by the activist group Justice for Myanmar, did not explain the purpose of the mislabeling. The letter from the regulator also authorized Dynamic Wave and its client, National Energy Prime Aviation Services Company, to pay Tawan for the shipment. Neither Dynamic Wave nor its client, which is part-owned by Myanmar’s military-backed government, responded to questions about the fuel shipment. Spokespeople for Myanmar’s military-backed government and foreign exchange regulator, as well as the Iranian foreign ministry, also did not return requests for comment. Tehran was the Myanmar military’s primary supplier of jet fuel between October 2024 and December 2025, with much of the trade carried out by the tankers Reef — since renamed Maris — and Noble, a Reuters report revealed in January. The scheme uncovered by Reuters underscores both the reach and limits of Washington’s power. The lengths taken to disguise the trade suggest US sanctions are biting. But Iranian jet fuel has continued to flow, earning Tehran valuable foreign currency and providing Myanmar with the means to conduct both commercial aviation and air raids. The US Treasury did not respond to questions about jet-fuel shipments between Iran and Myanmar. JET FUEL, AIRSTRIKES AND CIVILIAN CASUALTIES Myanmar’s generals seized power in 2021 from the democratically elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi. The coup sparked a civil war, during which the military has killed thousands — including many civilians — in aerial assaults, the United Nations said in August. Myanmar’s foreign ministry said in response to the UN allegations that the military “exercises maximum restraint to avoid civilian harm.” Justice for Myanmar, which also shared the fuel sales contract with Reuters, published a report on Monday concluding that Myanmar’s junta was importing jet fuel mislabeled as diesel. The organization, which supports further sanctions on Myanmar's jet fuel imports, said it obtained the documents from a junta-run server that was briefly publicly accessible. Reuters found a dead link to one of the documents on the DuckDuckGo search engine, indicating it had once been hosted on that server. Delivery dates and fuel quantities in the documents also match Iranian jet fuel shipment records that were separately reviewed by the news agency. THAI BANK CONNECTION The sales contract for Dynamic Wave's fuel shipment stipulated that the payment be transferred into Tawan’s account at Siam Commercial Bank (SCB), Thailand’s oldest bank. Tawan was identified by UN experts in a 2024 report as a jet-fuel supplier to Myanmar’s military. The firm has not commented on those allegations. SCB was described as a major facilitator of Myanmar military procurement in that report. The bank said after the report’s release that it adheres to anti-money-laundering laws and that its Myanmar-related transactions were legitimate and not connected to the arms trade. Reuters could not determine whether SCB was aware of the nature of Tawan’s business. Thai regulators in 2024 ordered banks to closely scrutinize transactions involving Myanmar in order to comply with sanctions and anti-money-laundering laws. SCB did not respond to repeated requests for comment about its commercial relationship with Tawan. Tawan and the Bank of Thailand, which supervises the kingdom's financial industry, also did not respond to questions. The December shipment was not the first time jet fuel arrived in Myanmar disguised as diesel. Dynamic Wave in May 2025 agreed to buy from Tawan 202,000 barrels of what a second contract, also obtained from the junta server, described as South African diesel. The agreement stipulated that the diesel should arrive at Yangon within a month and that Dynamic Wave would pay $26 million into Tawan’s SCB account. The invoice for that contract contained discrepancies suggesting the tanker actually contained jet fuel. The density of the fuel listed in the document matched the specifications for jet fuel rather than diesel sold in Southeast Asia, according to Joshua Heyne, a jet-fuel expert at Washington State University, and data from Platts, the energy-industry information provider. In addition, the price of the fuel was more than 50% higher than a global diesel benchmark. Noble called at Yangon on June 17 carrying just under 200,000 barrels of jet fuel earmarked for Dynamic Wave, shipment records show. Like Reef's December shipment, Noble’s cargo was loaded at Iran’s Bandar Abbas according to SynMax’s analysis of satellite imagery. As it made its way to Myanmar’s commercial capital, Noble transmitted location signals that made it appear as though its destination was the port of Chittagong in Bangladesh, according to SynMax. The manager of the Reef and Noble tankers did not respond to questions sent via its listed website. Shipments of jet fuel between Iran and Myanmar have continued this year, Reuters [USN:L6N45U0Y7 TEXT:"reported in October"], citing SynMax analysis and satellite imagery.

item.title: Raiders to consider starting No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza
item.description: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak will consider whether No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza can be part of the solution as losses mount for Las Vegas since starting the season 3-0.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak will consider whether No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza can be part of the solution as losses mount for Las Vegas since starting the season 3-0. The Raiders were plagued by familiar issues as they lost a fourth consecutive game Sunday, 35-21 to the Los Angeles Rams. "I think at this point, we're thinking about everything," Kubiak said. "How to fix our problems, how to fix our issues in the red zone, in the third quarter. Personnel, scheme, we've got to talk about all of it." Kirk Cousins completed 26 of 44 passes for 295 yards and two touchdowns Sunday and his performance wasn't entirely detrimental to the Raiders. Las Vegas was 3-of-14 on third down and scored a touchdown on one of five trips to the red zone. "It's really the same every day that it was in March or April," Cousins said when asked about ceding the position to Mendoza. "Nothing changes in the sense that, if I'm not the best option, then I don't want to be out there either. The first OTA, if that had become apparent, I would have been the first one to say, ‘Yeah, you can't play me.' "So nothing changes. The organization will do what they feel is best. I feel that Fernando's done a great job and has a bright future ahead, and I'm going to try to go out there and play as well as I possibly can, help us win, and give him a great example to learn from until he does go out there eventually." Mendoza has completed 6 of 8 passes for 48 yards, all in mop up duty at New England on Oct. 11. Cousins leads the NFL with 16 touchdown passes and is 12th in the league with a 97.4 passer rating. Drafted first overall in April, Mendoza was the Heisman Trophy winner and led Indiana to the national championship in 2025. But he's been QB2 most of his stint in Las Vegas. Kubiak and general manager John Spytek made it clear Cousins, 38, would begin the 2026 season as the Raiders' starter. Not executing in the red zone was the main issue that left Kubiak miffed on Sunday. "It comes down to we have to make plays down there when we have our one-on-one opportunities," Kubiak said. "Got to make the throws, got to make the catches. Didn't happen." --Field Level Media

item.title: Gap apparel supplier Gokaldas eyes doubling Europe exports share to cut US reliance
item.description: Indian apparel supplier Gokaldas Exports expects Europe to nearly double its share of exports as it benefits from a proposed trade deal, while diversifying beyond the US, a top executive told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Praveen Paramasivam
item.content:encoded: Indian apparel supplier Gokaldas Exports (GOKL.NS) expects Europe to nearly double its share of exports as it benefits from a proposed trade deal, while diversifying beyond the US, a top executive told Reuters. Domestic garment exporters are looking beyond the United States as uncertainty over tariffs persists, while anticipating stronger demand from Europe as India secures better trade access. "Europe accounts for around 15% of our exports. Over the next three to five years, we expect Europe's share to increase to approximately 25%-30%," said Sivaramakrishnan Ganapathi, Gokaldas' vice-chairman and managing director. The European Union is expected to sign [USN:L8N42P0VF TEXT:"a landmark trade deal"] with India by the end of 2026, cutting tariffs on imports. Gokaldas is "actively holding discussions with major European retailers in preparation for duty-free trade," Ganapathi said without naming them, adding it is boosting capacity in India instead of moving production elsewhere. The exporter, whose top customers include brands such as Gap, Carhartt, and JCPenney, is investing 1.25 billion rupees ($13.2 million) in fiscal 2027 to expand overall capacity and upgrade facilities. Gokaldas, which counts Pearl Global Industries (PGIL.NS) and KPR Mill (KPRM.NS) among its peers, expects the US share of exports to moderate from 69%, seeking to cut exposure to tariff shocks and policy uncertainty. It did not say by how much the share would fall. "The India–EU trade agreement could provide a medium-term opportunity to improve competitiveness, subject to implementation, product coverage and origin requirements," said Equirus Securities analyst Ronak Shah. US apparel imports from across the globe fell 7% to $49.08 billion in January-August, government data showed. But Gokaldas' US spring and summer orders for 2027 were stronger than the 2026 holiday season, when its shipments from India rose 3%-4% from a year earlier, Ganapathi said. He added that holiday sales would provide an early indication of demand for next year. ($1 = 94.9400 Indian rupees)

item.title: Grizzlies stay unblemished with victory at winless Kings
item.description: Isaiah Stewart and Ty Jerome converted three-point plays to bookend a late 11-0 flurry and the Memphis Grizzlies remained undefeated with a 123-112 road victory over the winless Sacramento Kings on Sunday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Isaiah Stewart and Ty Jerome converted three-point plays to bookend a late 11-0 flurry and the Memphis Grizzlies remained undefeated with a 123-112 road victory over the winless Sacramento Kings on Sunday night. Jerome finished with 31 points while Cameron Boozer (16 points, 11 rebounds) and Cedric Coward (15 points, 11 rebounds) each recorded a double-double for the Grizzlies, who elected to rest star center Zach Edey on the first night of a road back-to-back set. Memphis (3-0) plays at Utah on Monday night. After blowing a 14-point lead and finding themselves in a 106-all tie with 5:41 remaining, the Grizzlies seized control again by scoring the game's next 11 points. Stewart got the spurt rolling by turning a 5-footer into three points with a foul shot. Coward made it a five-point game when he tipped in a Boozer miss on Memphis' next possession. Jerome then scored six straight points, three on a 27-footer and three on an 8-footer on which he was fouled and sank the resulting free throw. Down 117-106 with 3:57 to play, the Kings got no closer than seven the rest of the way. Jerome, who made all 14 of his free-throw attempts, also found time for a team-high six assists. Jaylen Wells chipped in with 16 points, while Stewart and Cam Spencer added 13 apiece. Sacramento's Zach LaVine was the game's leading scorer with 37 points. Rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. had 22 to go with a game-high seven assists, while center Domantas Sabonis, fighting foul trouble much of the night, put up a 15-point, 15-rebound double-double. Precious Achiuwa (12 points, 10 rebounds) also had a double-double for the Kings, who have lost all three of their games on the young season. Seeking to open 3-0 for the first time since 2017, the Grizzlies used an 11-0 run early in the second quarter to take a lead that eventually grew to double digits before halftime and 83-69 in the fifth minute of the third quarter. But the Kings eventually drew even at 106-all on a three-point play by Sabonis with 5:41 remaining, setting the stage for the Grizzlies' late surge. --Field Level Media

item.title: India's Infosys falls after revenue growth view cut flags AI, competitive pressures
item.description: Shares of India's Infosys fell 2.7% on Monday after the software exporter sharply cut its fiscal 2027 revenue growth forecast, underscoring challenges from AI-driven pricing pressure, tougher competition and sluggish demand in key markets.
item.dc:creator: Mridula Kumar, Sai B
item.content:encoded: Shares of India's Infosys (INFY.NS) fell 2.7% on Monday after the software exporter sharply cut its fiscal 2027 revenue growth forecast, underscoring challenges from AI-driven pricing pressure, tougher competition and sluggish demand in key markets. The firm was the last of the top 5 to report [USN:L6N45T0UF TEXT:"earnings"] for the Indian IT sector. Earlier this month, peers Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS) and HCLTech (HCLT.NS) met revenue estimates with modest margin performance, but investors cheered the uptick in AI revenue. The company cut its fiscal 2027 revenue growth [USN:L6N4680ZX TEXT:"forecast"] to 1%-2% from 1.5%-3%, while most analysts had expected it to trim only the upper end of the range to 2.5%. "Peers are better placed than Infosys at this point, and the share movement is just reflecting that. Infosys has been underperforming from Q4FY26 results," LKP Securities analyst Anshul Jethi said. AI competition and clients expanding their global capability centres or offshore tech hubs directly, rather than engaging Infosys for IT services, are also hurting the company, he added. Systematix analysts called it a "disappointing quarter", highlighting pricing pressure from heightened competition and client productivity demands on account of AI, and subdued tech spending among retail and high-tech clients. Brokerage Motilal Oswal said weaker volumes, smaller-than-expected price increases, a shift toward offshore delivery and Infosys' decision to exit a large European manufacturing contract had weighed on growth. TD Cowen said macroeconomic uncertainty, AI-led productivity demands, and heightened competition have hurt pricing and volumes, while seasonal weakness and client ramp-downs could weigh on second-half growth. Analysts rate the stock "Buy" on average, with a median price target of 1,180 rupees, according to data compiled by LSEG. Shares were last trading 1.5% lower at 1,136 rupees as of 10:53 a.m. IST. The Nifty IT (.NIFTYIT) index was down 0.2% while the benchmark Nifty 50 (.NSEI) index was up 0.16%.

item.title: Houthis say they attacked Saudi oil pumping stations, Riyadh airport as fighting intensifies
item.description: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's East-West crude oil pumping stations and Riyadh airport, as rising hostilities choke oil supplies and threaten to erupt into a larger conflict.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they had attacked Saudi Arabia's East-West crude oil pumping stations and Riyadh airport, as rising hostilities choke oil supplies and threaten to erupt into a larger conflict. The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said earlier it had destroyed two ballistic missile launchers in the capital Sanaa, including one used to fire a missile towards Riyadh that the coalition said it had intercepted. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation of the Houthi attacks. The Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports, ports and oil installations, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in the wider war. The Houthis also said they had struck Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, which [USN:L2N46A05D TEXT:"resumed operations at two terminals"] on Sunday after an attack claimed by the group [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"earlier this month"] killed 13 people, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. Top officials from the Mecca Pact countries Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are set to meet Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday to discuss regional coordination, two people with knowledge of the matter said. The planned talks would be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the three-nation bloc since Saudi Arabia came under escalating attacks from Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis. STRIKES INSIDE YEMEN Saudi Arabia [USN:L6N453173 TEXT:"temporarily shut down"] its 1,200-km (746-mile) East-West pipeline in September as a precaution after a drone attack that Riyadh and Baghdad said originated in Iraq. The pipeline has served as a key route for Middle East oil exports while the Strait of Hormuz has been largely shut by the war. The Houthis also said on Saturday they had targeted the East-West pipeline, crude oil pumping stations, an Aramco facility in Yanbu and the Rabigh refinery. There was no Saudi confirmation of those claims. The Saudi coalition said on Monday it had also carried out a military operation against Houthi targets in Yemen, destroying five tunnels used to store ballistic missiles, four ballistic missile launchers and a missile storage facility. The operation also targeted Houthi supply lines, fighters and military equipment along front lines inside Yemen, coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said, pledging continued "deterrent operational measures" to protect civilians. Saudi Arabia has intensified its strikes on the Houthis since the group captured strategic areas along Yemen's Red Sea coast last month, advancing towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key global shipping route for Gulf oil producers on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz. The latest fighting has effectively ended a UN-brokered truce that had largely held since 2022. Saudi Arabia led a coalition into Yemen's civil war in 2015 to back the internationally recognised government, a year after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa.

item.title: The week in Asian football
item.description: Talking points from the week in Asian football:
item.dc:creator: Michael Church
item.content:encoded: Talking points from the week in Asian football: SEOUL CROWNED CHAMPIONS FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 2016 FC Seoul's 1-1 draw with Gangwon FC on Saturday secured the club a first league title in a decade as nearest rivals Ulsan HD were held 2-2 by Pohang Steelers. Moon Seon-min put hosts Seoul ahead in the 58th minute before Kang Joon-hyuck levelled six minutes. Seoul, who claimed their seventh league title, are 16 points clear of Ulsan with five matches left. CHINESE TITLE RACE GOES TO THE WIRE AS CHENGDU LOSE The Chinese Super League title race will go down to the final week of the campaign after leaders Chengdu Rongcheng lost 1-0 to second-placed Dalian Yingbo on Saturday. Chengdu have needed a point from their previous three matches to claim their first title but have lost them all. They will get another chance to claim the point they need when they face Shandong Taishan on November 8. Chengdu's Felipe Silva missed a penalty before Mamadou Traore scored the winner for Dalian, who face Tianjin Tiger in their final game. AL-HILAL RETURN TO TOP SPOT IN SAUDI PRO LEAGUE Al-Hilal won 3-2 against Al-Qadsiah on Friday to replace Brendan Rodgers' side at the top of the Saudi Pro League, while champions Al-Nassr moved up to second. Second-half goals from Ruben Neves and Sergej Milinkovic-Savic secured the win that took Al-Hilal two points clear of Al-Qadsiah, who have played one game more. Al-Nassr defeated hosts Al-Faisaly 3-1 to move ahead of Al-Qadsiah on goal difference. MACHIDA STAY TOP DESPITE DRAW WITH VISSEL KOBE FC Machida Zelvia were held 0-0 by Vissel Kobe in Japan on Saturday but stayed top on goal difference ahead of FC Tokyo, who thrashed Mito Hollyhock 6-0. Machida and Tokyo are on 27 points, one point ahead of Sanfrecce Hiroshima, who won 4-0 against Shimizu S-Pulse. WELLINGTON PHOENIX CONTINUE PERFECT START Wellington Phoenix beat Central Coast Mariners 2-0 on Sunday to pick up their second straight victory to start the new A-League season, with two goals in two second-half minutes from Rafael Duran and Corban Piper. Defending champions Auckland FC lost 5-2 to Western Sydney Wanderers.

item.title: China's yuan climbs to fresh 4-year high ahead of key policy meetings
item.description: China's yuan climbed to a fresh four-year high against the dollar on Monday, extending its longest winning streak since May, as softer oil prices and US Treasury yields weighed on the greenback, ahead of key policy meetings at home and overseas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's yuan climbed to a fresh four-year high against the dollar on Monday, extending its longest winning streak since May, as softer [USN:L2N46B09G TEXT:"oil prices"] and US Treasury yields weighed on the greenback, ahead of key policy meetings at home and overseas. Investors were cautious ahead of major central bank meetings due later this week, with the US Federal Reserve, Bank of Japan and European Central Bank widely expected to keep rates unchanged while maintaining a hawkish tone. Attention will also turn to China's [USN:L6N46C04K TEXT:"fifth plenum"] for fresh policy clues. Prior to market opening, the People's Bank of China set the midpoint rate at 6.7162 per dollar, its strongest since February 2, 2023. The spot yuan is allowed to trade a maximum of 2% either side of the fixed midpoint each day. Monday's midpoint was 471 pips weaker than a Reuters estimate of 6.6691 — its largest weak-side deviation since September 23. The central bank has been gradually strengthening its daily yuan official guidance this year, but at levels weaker than market expectations, suggesting it is seeking to manage the pace of appreciation, traders and analysts said. "The PBOC continues to resist a faster pace of appreciation via weaker than-market-expected fixings," analysts at Barclays said in a note. "We think the PBOC's reaction function points to a stronger floor against disorderly weakness, while the fixing should continue to constrain the pace of gains as the trade-weighted currency strengthens." In the spot market, the onshore yuan hit a high of 6.6682 per dollar at one point, the strongest level since June 2022, before last trading at 6.6691 as of 0252 GMT. If it retains the gains at the late-night close, the onshore spot yuan would have booked an eighth straight session of rises, the longest winning streak since May. Its offshore counterpart last fetched 6.6688 per dollar, up about 0.01% in Asian trade. "We continue to think that a gradual but sustained currency appreciation is underway but consensus forecasts and forward markets underestimate how far this process can run given the deep undervaluation starting point," Goldman Sachs analysts said in a note. "Ultimately, currency appreciation alone will not address China's economic challenges ... that needs both currency appreciation and support for domestic demand, two instruments to hit two targets," they said, maintaining their 12-month target for the yuan at 6.40 per dollar.
