item.title: Pachuca gana de visita a líder América en el torneo mexicano de fútbol
item.description: Pachuca regresó a la senda del triunfo tras vencer el domingo 2-1 de visita al líder América en la decimocuarta jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pachuca regresó a la senda del triunfo tras vencer el domingo 2-1 de visita al líder América en la decimocuarta jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano. Los "Tuzos" de Pachuca, que no ganaban desde el 11 de septiembre en la octava jornada, vencieron a las "Águilas" con goles de Alan Bautista y del neerlandés Oussama Idrissi. En el partido disputado en el estadio Azteca de la Ciudad de México, Pachuca se adelantó a los 12 minutos por conducto de Bautista, quien definió con un disparo raso desde fuera del área. América empató en el inicio de la segunda parte cuando Henry Martín remató con el pecho en el área chica un centro de Erick Sánchez en una jugada donde los elementos del equipo local hilaron varios pases a los 46 minutos. Pachuca logró la victoria a los 74 minutos con un potente disparo de Idrissi desde fuera del área. En los minutos restantes, América presionó en busca del empate que estuvo cerca de conseguir, pero las atinadas intervenciones del portero Carlos Moreno lo evitaron. A pesar de la derrota, América se mantiene como líder del torneo con 27 puntos, mientras que Pachuca se ubicó en la decimotercera posición con 16 unidades. “Venimos aquí con la cara en alto, con el pecho erguido, contra el súper líder en su casa y, a mi parecer, jugamos mejor partido. Pero no quiere decir que echemos las campanas al vuelo y nos relajemos, al contrario, es la catapulta más importante para cerrar dignamente el torneo, no nos queda más que salir a luchar, competir y jugar lo mejor que podamos", dijo en conferencia de prensa el director técnico de Pachuca, Benjamín Mora. "Tenemos que ser muy consistentes para sumar la mayor cantidad de puntos que podamos", agregó. En los otros partidos disputados el domingo, el actual campeón Cruz Azul venció 3-1 de visita a Querétaro con goles de Andrés Montaño, del argentino Nicolás Ibáñez y del nigeriano Christian Ebere. Para los "Gallos Blancos" de Querétaro anotó el argentino Mateo Coronel. Atlas venció 4-3 a Puebla con tantos de los argentinos Florián Monzón y Kevin Zenón, y doblete de José Martín. Para Puebla anotaron el venezolano Luifer Hernández, el defensa Paulo Ramírez en su propia portería y Omar Moreno. Por su parte, Tijuana goleó 4-1 a Santos Laguna con tantos del argentino Francisco González, del uruguayo José Ignacio Rivero en dos ocasiones y del ecuatoriano Adonis Preciado. Para los "Guerreros" de Santos anotó Esteban Lozano. El sábado, Guadalajara ganó 1-0 de visita a Monterrey, Pumas UNAM y Tigres UANL empataron 1-1, mismo marcador que se registró en el partido entre León y Toluca. El viernes, Atlético de San Luis ganó de visita al Atlante por 1-0. Por su parte, Necaxa y Bravos de Ciudad Juárez empataron 1-1.

item.title: Seahawks knock Chiefs from unbeaten ranks in decisive fashion
item.description: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown and Emanuel Wilson rushed for 100 yards and a score as the host Seattle Seahawks defeated Kansas City 20-3 on Sunday night, handing the Chiefs their first loss of the season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown and Emanuel Wilson rushed for 100 yards and a score as the host Seattle Seahawks defeated Kansas City 20-3 on Sunday night, handing the Chiefs their first loss of the season. Wilson had 24 carries, including a 21-yard touchdown run around the left end with 3:47 remaining to clinch the victory for the defending Super Bowl champions. NFL rushing leader Kenneth Walker III, who was the MVP of the Seahawks' 29-13 Super Bowl victory against New England before signing with Kansas City as a free agent in the offseason, was limited to 36 yards on 14 carries on Sunday night. Patrick Mahomes was 19-of-33 passing for 165 yards with an interception for the Chiefs (5-1), who had just 213 yards of total offense to the Seahawks' 410. Tight end Travis Kelce had four receptions for 44 yards. Sam Darnold completed 20 of 28 passes for 257 yards with one touchdown and one interception for the Seahawks (4-3). Darnold hit Smith-Njigba on a 28-yard scoring strike down the left sideline with 1:44 left in the first half, giving the Seahawks a 10-0 lead. Smith-Njigba was originally ruled out of bounds inside the 1-yard line, but a video review determined the ball had crossed the goal line. The drive started after safety Ty Okada intercepted a Mahomes pass. The Chiefs went three-and-out on the ensuing possession, giving the ball back to Seattle with 1:16 remaining. The Seahawks reached the Kansas City 2 before Chiefs cornerback Nohl Williams intercepted a pass in the back of the end zone and returned it to Seattle's 44. Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker was short on a 58-yard attempt on the final play of the half, leaving the score at 10-0. Jason Myers kicked a pair of field goals for the Seahawks, including a 25-yarder with 8:22 remaining in the second quarter to open the scoring. The Seahawks took the second-half kickoff and Myers made a 35-yarder to increase the lead to 13-0. The Chiefs' lone score came on Butker's 50-yard field goal with 1:42 left in the third quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jordan arrests three suspects in deadly church attack, state media says
item.description: Jordanian security forces arrested three armed suspects after a shootout on Monday in connection with an attack on a church in the US-allied country that killed nine people, state television reported.
item.dc:creator: Yomna Ehab
item.content:encoded: Jordanian security forces arrested three armed suspects after a shootout on Monday in connection with an attack on a church in the US-allied country that killed nine people, state television reported. Friday's attack during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hamoud in Karak governorate, about 120 km (75 miles) southwest of the capital Amman, also wounded 40 others. [USN:L6N46B02Q TEXT:"Witnesses "]said the shooting lasted several minutes. Jordan's Public Security Directorate said the suspects were located while hiding in an abandoned house in Karak. They refused to surrender and attacked security forces, who returned fire and arrested all three after wounding them, the directorate said in a statement published on state media. No security personnel were injured, and a number of firearms and ammunition were found in the suspects' possession. Jordanian authorities have said the violence was carried out by "extremist terrorists". There has been no claim of responsibility. "Terrorism has no place among us," the directorate said, adding that the suspects had met their "just fate". King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against Islamist militant groups, has ordered security forces to respond with an "iron fist" to the rare attack on the Christian minority. Such violence is highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable state in the Middle East, though authorities say they have foiled several Islamist militant plots over the years. The Public Security Directorate did not name the suspects or publicly identify possible affiliations with any Islamist militant groups. Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said authorities were reviewing the circumstances that led young people towards extremism and would hold accountable anyone found to have participated in the attack.

item.title: Bank of Japan's hawkish pause to leave scope for December hike
item.description: The Bank of Japan will likely declare victory in a nearly 14-year battle to hit its 2% inflation target at its policy meeting on Friday and emphasise the risks prices could overshoot, signaling the chance of a rate hike as soon as December.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Japan will likely declare victory in a nearly 14-year battle to hit its 2% inflation target at its policy meeting on Friday and emphasise the risks prices could overshoot, signaling the chance of a rate hike as soon as December. Such hawkish language may reinforce expectations the [USN:L4N4650G0 TEXT:"BOJ"], [USN:L6N46606V TEXT:"US Federal Reserve"] and [USN:L6N45U0QU TEXT:"European Central Bank"] will all raise rates by year-end, as brisk AI demand and the Iran war-induced energy shock worsen global inflationary pressures. Still, the BOJ is likely to avoid dropping explicit hints on the timing and pace of future rate rises as it balances the need to forestall risks of an inflation overshoot without disrupting jittery markets with a premature hike, analysts say. "With rises in prices and wages moderate, the BOJ will keep raising rates gradually without rushing," said a person familiar with its thinking, a view echoed by two more people. At the two-day policy meeting ending on Friday, the BOJ is set to maintain its policy rate at 1.25% by a majority vote, forgoing a back-to-back hike to spend more time scrutinising the effect of past rate hikes on lending conditions. In a quarterly report due after the meeting, the BOJ is likely to slightly revise up next fiscal year's price forecast and signal that underlying inflation has roughly achieved its 2% target, [USN:L4N45S011 TEXT:"people familiar with the matter have told Reuters"]. With wage gains becoming embedded and inflation expectations hovering around 2%, the central bank will likely stress that it will now focus on anchoring inflation around its target by raising rates toward levels deemed neutral to the economy. While Governor Kazuo Ueda has already signaled such a shift in policy focus upon raising rates in September, the pivot would mark another symbolic departure from the BOJ's prolonged efforts to fire up inflation through ultra-loose monetary policy. "It's a historical moment for the BOJ, though it faces a more challenging task now that it needs to step not just on the accelerator but the brakes," said Naomi Muguruma, chief bond strategist at Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities. "The BOJ will probably scrutinise upcoming data and market moves in deciding whether to raise rates in December, or hold until January," she said. Analysts [USN:L4N4650G0 TEXT:"polled by Reuters"] expect the BOJ to raise rates to 1.5% in December and stick to a quarterly pace of rate hikes. FUNDING STILL LOOSE Under former governor Haruhiko Kuroda, the BOJ deployed a massive stimulus in 2013 to pull Japan out of deflation and fire up inflation to its 2% inflation target. Even after ending its mix of unorthodox easing steps in 2024, the central bank has trodden cautiously in raising rates on the view underlying inflation - or price moves excluding one-off factors and driven by domestic demand - remained below target. With stubbornly high energy costs and rising import prices from a weak yen adding to inflationary pressures, the BOJ raised rates in September after delivering a hike in June - a shorter interval than the roughly twice-a-year hikes in 2024 and 2025. The BOJ's policy rate, at 1.25%, is now within the range of 1.1% to 2.5% its staff estimated as Japan's neutral rate, or the level that neither cools nor overheats the economy - drawing market attention to how far it could eventually hike rates. With growth in bank lending still strong, the central bank is likely to stress on Friday that financial conditions remain loose - signalling scope for further rate hikes before its policy rate reaches levels close to neutral, the people said. The BOJ's meeting follows that of the Fed, which is seen skipping a hike at its two-day meeting concluding on Wednesday. The ECB is also set to keep rates unchanged at 2.5% on Thursday.

item.title: Officials from Mecca pact countries to meet Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday
item.description: Top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are to meet Iran's leaders in Tehran on Monday in their first high-level contact since the kingdom became a pressure point in the wider Iran conflict.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Mills, Ariba Shahid
item.content:encoded: Top officials from Mecca Pact countries Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are to meet Iran's leaders in Tehran on Monday in their first high-level contact since the kingdom became a pressure point in the wider Iran conflict. Saudi Arabia will be represented by Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan by army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Turkey by intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, Saudi and Iranian officials said. The talks come as attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have spiralled over recent weeks and rhetoric between Washington and Tehran has grown more heated. Both countries have also drawn up plans to restart the wider war, possibly after the US midterm elections on November 3. Monday's planned talks would be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the three-nation bloc since Saudi Arabia was drawn deeper into the conflict. Under [USN:L6N4440I6 TEXT:"the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement"] signed in August, an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all. Qatari mediators met Iranian officials in Tehran on Sunday in a push to de-escalate regional tensions, Reuters reported. Qatar has, for months, played a key mediating role between Tehran and Washington. A senior Iranian official said the meeting was initiated by Pakistan, during Munir's visit to Tehran [USN:S8N455017 TEXT:"last week"], as he met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other senior officials. During the visit, Iranian officials told him there would be no talks with Washington until Tehran's demands were met, according to Iranian media. Earlier mediation efforts involving both Pakistan and Qatar helped produce an interim peace agreement in June, but the deal quickly unravelled as fighting between Iran and the United States resumed weeks later. The deputy secretary of Iran's top security body, Ali Baqeri-Kani, told state TV that Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid, Pakistan's Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin would visit Tehran for consultations with Iran’s Supreme National Security Council on regional security. Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said the meeting is part of ongoing efforts by the Mecca Pact countries to de-escalate the current crisis, promote diplomatic solutions, and support mediation efforts led by Qatar and Pakistan."The visit also underscores the pivotal role of the Mecca Pact states in fostering regional security and stability, and their commitment to working with all nations in the region toward achieving this goal," Krimly posted on X. Pakistan's military media wing and Turkey's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment. TENSIONS RISING Saudi Arabia intercepted another wave of missiles and drones on Sunday as fighting with the Houthis continued unabated. Ministers from the Mecca Pact countries held an emergency meeting in Riyadh earlier this month and agreed to ensure the "rapid deployment" of military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia. The Houthi attacks have become an increasingly destabilising element in the US-Israeli offensive against Iran , turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in the wider war. Tensions between Washington and Tehran have sharpened in recent days. President Donald Trump said on Friday the US may carry out another military operation against Iran and Iran's leaders have said that a renewed US military campaign would be met with a stronger response than before. Iranian security officials have told Reuters that Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if the United States and Israel attack again. A US intelligence memo this week warned that Iranian plots against American personnel had reached "advanced stages". The war, now nearly eight months old, has weighed on President Donald Trump's approval ratings ahead of the midterms. The Mecca agreement's first article says the parties shall use "all necessary means" to eliminate threats to one another's territorial integrity, sovereignty or internationally recognised borders, according to a text seen by Reuters. Efforts by Turkey’s parliament to ratify the agreement began last week and are still underway, while Pakistan approved the pact last week.

item.title: Rupee weakens on importers' dollar payments, modest buildup in long dollar positions
item.description: The Indian rupee came under pressure after opening largely unchanged on Monday, with dollar purchases by importers and a modest buildup in long dollar interbank positions adding to the drag from high oil prices.
item.dc:creator: Nimesh Vora
item.content:encoded: The Indian rupee came under pressure after opening largely unchanged on Monday, with dollar purchases by importers and a modest buildup in long dollar interbank positions adding to the drag from high oil prices. The rupee weakened through the morning, slipping 0.18% to 95.1150 per dollar by 11:10 a.m. IST. The absence of central bank dollar sales, which had helped support the rupee in recent sessions, added to the currency's woes on Monday. The weakness highlights the unit's struggle to withstand persistent external headwinds without regular support from the Reserve Bank of India. Brent crude rose more than 6% last week to a six-month high amid concerns over supply disruptions following attacks on Saudi Arabia. Prices remained near $115 a barrel in Asia trading. High oil prices widen India's import bill, add to inflationary pressures and weigh on economic growth. They can encourage companies to increase currency hedges and make foreign investors more cautious about Indian assets. The rupee had found support in recent weeks from the Reserve Bank of India's interventions, which helped it recover from levels near 96.70 per dollar, and from Jio Platforms IPO-linked inflows. In the absence of this support, the currency remains more exposed to dollar demand. Another factor could come into play this week, with the Federal Reserve's policy decision adding to the rupee's list of external risks. A rate pause is widely expected, leaving markets focused on guidance on the rate outlook and whether further tightening remains on the table this year. FALLING FX RESERVES India's foreign exchange reserves fell for a sixth consecutive week through October 16, declining by $5 billion to $721 billion. Reserves are down more than $64 billion from their all-time high in the first week of September. Bankers have attributed part of the decline to the RBI's spot dollar sales to support the rupee, alongside sell/buy swaps used to manage rupee liquidity.

item.title: Israel markets see upside in Netanyahu defeat after three-year rally
item.description: Some investors see further upside if Netanyahu is defeated, potentially easing regional tensions.
item.dc:creator: Steven Scheer, Marc Jones
item.content:encoded: Israel's markets have soared despite three years of war and political turmoil, but some investors see further upside if the opposition defeats Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Tuesday’s election, potentially easing regional tensions and political risk. Opinion polls point to a tight contest , with neither Netanyahu's ruling Likud bloc nor an opposition alliance centred on former military chief [USN:L6N46303T TEXT:"Gadi Eisenkot"] expected to secure the 61 seats in the 120-seat Knesset needed to govern. That raises the prospect of lengthy coalition negotiations or even another election. Since the October 7 Hamas attacks in 2023, the Tel Aviv stock market (.TASE) has soared 130%, far outpacing Wall Street's 80% gain, while the shekel has climbed 25% , one of the world's strongest currency performances. Analysts attribute some of that strength to Israel's tech sector and the global AI boom, while defence spending, which has nearly doubled to around 8% of GDP, has also provided a boost. With both Netanyahu and Eisenkot vowing to maintain pressure on Hamas and Iran, markets are focused on their broader policy differences. JPMorgan estimates the shekel could swing as much as 3% depending on the result. An opposition victory that improves relations with Western allies and halts a judicial overhaul that sparked mass protests in 2023 could strengthen the currency, JPMorgan said, while another Netanyahu-led government could weaken it. Billionaire investor [USN:L5N46B045 TEXT:"Bill Ackman"], while stopping short of backing a candidate, said a government without far-right ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich would signal that Israel was "turning a new page," potentially helping rebuild its international credibility and expand the Abraham Accords with its neighbours. IBI Investment House also expects an opposition victory to lift the markets. "From a capital markets perspective, this would likely be reflected in a decline in Israel's risk premium, appreciation pressure on the shekel, and a positive reaction in the local market," IBI's Chief Economist Rafi Gozlan said. "The most significant issue is what the result will mean for the region," said Equity Bank's chief economic adviser Charlie Robertson. "If Netanyahu is reelected it might increase the chances of further escalation with Iran, whereas a defeat might be seen as lessening the tensions." But the prospect of gains under an opposition government does not mean investors expect Israeli assets to suffer if Netanyahu remains in power. Stocks and bonds have proved remarkably resilient through years of war and political upheaval, and some investors remain confident in the economy regardless of the election outcome. Union Investment's Sergey Dergachev has been buying Israeli bonds ahead of the election, betting the economy and companies he favours will remain fundamentally strong. "We are very constructive on Israeli credits going into the election," Dergachev said, adding that bonds were less prone to major swings and the region's intertwined conflicts should eventually ease. RISKS REMAIN Despite the rally, foreign investors remain cautious. Copley Fund Research data show the share of global funds holding Israeli equities is at a record low, having fallen sharply since 2023. TS Lombard's Christopher Granville cited central bank estimates that the war had cost the economy more than $55 billion by last year, equivalent to 8.6% in cumulative lost GDP growth. Israel's fiscal position is another focus. Public debt has risen to nearly 70% of GDP, around 10 percentage points higher than in 2022, while the budget deficit is expected to remain around 4.5% of GDP, versus less than 2% before the conflict. Central bank head Amir Yaron stressed last week the need to "preserve adequate fiscal policy space" given the Iran war. FUNDAMENTAL STRENGTHS Like stocks, Israeli government bonds have rallied, returning about 30% over the last two years, more than double the main emerging market indexes. The main risk for investors is an inconclusive result that prolongs political uncertainty, delaying budgets, reforms and investment, some investors believe. That uncertainty can produce sharp short-term swings. Tel Aviv Stock Exchange research covering the last 10 elections found volatility in leading share indexes rose by as much as 45% in the weeks after voting compared with a typical week. But initial losses were typically recovered within a month, with the indexes posting an average gain of about 1.7%. Over a longer horizon, the TA-125 returned an average 16.4% in the year following elections, compared with a long-term annual average of 11.5%, the research found. Political deadlock often weighed on stocks before voting, but the effects typically faded within months, said Nissan Avraham, an analyst at the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange's research unit. That record supports the view that elections matter less for Israeli companies than many investors assume. Lior Yochpaz, chief investment officer at insurance company Menora Mivtachim, said businesses have continued to thrive despite years of political upheaval, judicial overhaul proposals and regional conflict, helped by a relatively business-friendly environment. For some investors, however, the more attractive election trade lies outside Israel. TT International's Jean-Charles Sambor said an opposition victory or weakened Netanyahu government could ease regional tensions and benefit Lebanese bonds. "The best way to play it for us is through other Middle East countries, and for us Lebanon is a good proxy," Sambor said.

item.title: IEA's Birol does not expect energy markets to return to pre-war levels in 2027
item.description: The head of the International Energy Agency said on Monday that he does not expect energy markets in 2027 to return to where they were before the Iran war, which began in late February.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The head of the International Energy Agency said on Monday that he does not expect energy markets in 2027 to return to where they were before the Iran war, which began in late February. The conflict sharply tightened a market that had been projected to be in surplus this year, significantly disrupting global energy flows and pushing up oil benchmarks and refined product prices. "I am afraid I don't see any credible pathway that the markets will go next year, where we were before this war has started," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol told the Singapore International Energy Week conference. "So therefore, we all need to get prepared, taking the energy security as a number one priority in our government, business world, but without forgetting what is the next chapter for the countries and for companies that are all here today," he said. More Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia sent Brent crude futures as high as $117 a barrel on Friday, the highest level in nearly six months. The contract eased on Monday but was still trading about 59% above its pre-war level. "Oil prices are flirting with $120 a barrel and the prices for products are even much higher," Birol told a press conference. He declined to give a forecast for oil prices, but added: "I can tell you that the current price of oil is, for some countries, for example in Europe, maybe not so high and affordable. But in many parts of the world, having almost $120 oil prices is having a major impact on trade deficits." WINTER CONCERNS Birol also raised concern about winter demand for some fuels, especially diesel, which is used in parts of the West for heating. "I am worried on top of that for refined products because we are entering...winter season. Some parts of the world, where typically diesel demand goes high and several refineries are going through maintenance period." "In Europe, we are facing a tough winter because European countries have decided to cut gas imports from Russia and with the additional problem now rising from the Iran war, namely Qatar and the Emirates not being able to export gas as they were before, will put significant pressure on gas markets." Birol expects a "strong comeback" for the nuclear sector as a result of the current crisis. The IEA's recent survey showed that 90 gigawatts of nuclear power plants are under construction and this is the highest in the last four decades, he added.

item.title: Week 7 injury roundup: Vikings’ Aaron Jones aggravates knee injury
item.description: Minnesota running back Aaron Jones aggravated a left knee injury that he suffered earlier this season during the undefeated Vikings' 16-10 home win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Minnesota running back Aaron Jones aggravated a left knee injury that he suffered earlier this season during the undefeated Vikings' 16-10 home win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Jones was seen heading straight for the blue medical tent following a hit at the end of a 17-yard run. Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said after the game that Jones had the knee evaluated, and Pro Football Talk reported that the running back would undergo an MRI on Monday. Jones sprained his left MCL in Week 2 against the Chicago Bears but has not missed a game. He finished with eight carries for 26 yards. The Vikings did get back Jordan Mason (thumb) at running back for the first time since Week 1. He led the team with 68 yards on 15 carries. --Carolina Panthers veteran right tackle Taylor Moton was carted off the field with a fractured left fibula during their 43-13 home loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Panthers coach Dave Canales acknowledged that Moton would be "out for a while" after the contest. It was just Moton's second game since returning from a serious blood clot issue. He was hurt when teammate Rasheed Walker, the left tackle, fell across the back of his legs in the opening minute of the third quarter. Moton held his left leg and punched the turf while waiting for trainers to come on the field. "It was the fibula. There is a fracture there," Canales told reporters. "We'll have to get the full run-up to be able to give you the extent of the whole thing. "But it was just sick for ‘T-Mo.' Working his way back, getting out there. Just kinda an end-of-the-play thing, guys just rolled up on him unexpectedly at that moment." --Denver Broncos receiver Jaylen Waddle exited his team's 30-16 road victory over the Arizona Cardinals with a chest injury. The injury occurred on a reverse with under five minutes remaining. Waddle fumbled the pitch from quarterback Bo Nix and dove to recover the ball as Arizona's Josh Sweat landed on top of him. The receiver left for the locker room and didn't return. Waddle (four catches, 48 yards on Sunday) was dealing with a chest injury during the week and was limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday. He was a full participant on Friday and received no injury designation. Broncos head coach Sean Payton criticized his own play call per the reverse in which Waddle was injured. "Why didn't anybody ask me about the dumb reverse call?" Payton said during his postgame press conference. "... It was awful. I'm sorry." --The New York Giants came out of their 27-21 overtime win over the host Houston Texans with multiple injury concerns in the backfield. Tyrone Tracy Jr. left in the first half with a hamstring injury, while Cam Skattebo also revealed he felt something in his hamstring after his 42-yard dash in overtime set up Devin Singletary's 30-yard touchdown run to walk it off. Skattebo had a career-high 124 yards as the Giants racked up 188 on the ground to support quarterback J.J. McCarthy in his first start for the team. The Giants get a chance to rest and recover with a bye in Week 8. For the Texans, running back Woody Marks briefly left with an apparent left knee injury but returned to the game. Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said wide receiver Jaylin Noel had a turf toe injury, and Noel was seen wearing a boot. --The banged-up Green Bay Packers' offensive line received two more blows as centers Sean Rhyan (ankle) and Jacob Monk (quad) made early exits. Both players left the game in the first quarter of an eventual 20-17 road loss to the Detroit Lions. John Williams served as Green Bay's center the rest of the game. Afterward, Packers coach Matt LaFleur said he wouldn't expect either Rhyan or Monk to be available on a quick turnaround for their next game Thursday against the Panthers. The Packers already had lost tackle Zach Bako-Bewele (torn patellar tendon in his right knee) for the season, with starting guard Aaron Banks in and out of the lineup with multiple injuries. Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (ankle) did not return after being hurt in the fourth quarter. --In Paris, New Orleans Saints safety Justin Reid sustained a concussion and running back CJ Donaldson hurt his shoulder during a 16-10 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. --Seattle wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) exited early in the second half and did not return in the Seahawks' 20-3 home win over the Kansas City Chiefs. Starting left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) left in the fourth quarter, while running back Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring) also went out early. Shaheed caught two passes on three targets for 1 yard. Jones had five carries for 8 yards. --Field Level Media

item.title: Canadiens earn narrow victory vs. Jets in Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic
item.description: Jacob Fowler made 33 saves for the Montreal Canadiens in a 2-1 win against the Winnipeg Jets in the Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic at Princess Auto Stadium in Winnipeg on Sunday evening.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jacob Fowler made 33 saves for the Montreal Canadiens in a 2-1 win against the Winnipeg Jets in the Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic at Princess Auto Stadium in Winnipeg on Sunday evening. Lane Hutson and fellow defenseman Kaiden Guhle scored, and Cole Caufield had two assists for Montreal in the NHL's 46th outdoor game and 10th played in Canada. Isak Rosen scored a late goal and Stuart Skinner made 19 saves for the Jets, who have lost five in a row (0-3-2). After a scoreless first period, Hutson gave the Canadiens a 1-0 lead at 7:19 of the second. Caufield received a pass outside of the left circle, brought it along the blue line and then above the right circle, where he passed it to Noah Dobson cutting through the same circle. Dobson got to the bottom of the circle and made a centering pass between two Montreal defenders to Hutson, who was cutting to the far post a step ahead of Jets forward Alex Iafallo, giving him room to redirect the puck into the net before Skinner could slide over. Montreal extended its lead to 2-0 at 11:04 of the second. Juraj Slafkovsky took a shot off a rush that was deflected wide. The puck came off the end boards to Caufield, who passed it back to Guhle at the left point. He flicked a one-timer that sailed through traffic and hit the net. Winnipeg prevented Fowler's second shutout of the season when Rosen scored with a one-timer on the shortside from the bottom of the right circle to cut it to 2-1 at 15:24 of the third period. The Jets went on a power play with 1:32 left and soon after pulled Skinner for a 6-on-4, but couldn't tie it. Montreal forward Alex Newhook had the best scoring chance of the first period on a short-handed breakaway, but was turned away by Skinner at 17:15. Dawson Mercer made his Jets debut after he was acquired from the New Jersey Devils as part of Friday's trade for goaltender Connor Hellebuyck and the forward had two shots in 15:22. --Field Level Media

item.title: Indian shares fall as oil concerns persist
item.description: Indian shares declined on Monday as sentiment remained subdued over elevated crude oil prices and their impact on inflation, with investors focused on the US Federal Reserve's policy decision later this week.
item.dc:creator: Bharath Rajeswaran, Vivek M
item.content:encoded: Indian shares declined on Monday as sentiment remained subdued over elevated crude oil prices and their impact on inflation, with investors focused on the US Federal Reserve's policy decision later this week. The benchmark Nifty 50 (.NSEI) fell 0.5% to 22,485.65, and the Sensex (.BSESN) shed 0.46% to 72,783.15, as of 9:47 a.m. IST (0417 GMT). Twelve of the 16 major sectors logged losses. The broader small-caps (.NIFSMCP100) and mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100) lost 0.7% and 0.4%, respectively. IT stocks (.NIFTYIT) shed 1.1%. Infosys (INFY.NS) lost 2% after it cut its annual revenue growth forecast as weakness in its key North American market outweighed its higher-than-expected revenue. Brent crude futures traded around $114.5 a barrel, easing from a near six-month high of $117 after the Indian market close on Friday, though ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Houthis kept supply concerns in focus. "Concerns over supply disruptions due to escalating Mideast tensions pushed crude oil prices higher," said G Chokkalingam, founder and head of research at Equinomic Research. "Domestic equities are likely to remain highly volatile, with a short-term downward bias and unless the Mideast conflict is resolved meaningfully, higher energy costs could reignite global inflation, restrain economic growth and darken the outlook for stock markets worldwide," he said. Investor caution was further reinforced by expectations that the US Federal Reserve will hold interest rates steady this week before resuming its tightening cycle with a December increase. Higher US rates typically draw capital toward the dollar and Treasuries, reducing the appeal of emerging-market equities including India. Among stocks, Shriram Finance (SHMF.NS) lost 5% after cutting its annual loan-growth forecast and flagging higher credit costs, eclipsing stronger-than-expected quarterly profit. Kotak Mahindra Bank (KTKM.NS) gained 2.3% after second-quarter profit beat on robust loan demand and lower bad-loan provisions. Dr Reddy's Laboratories (REDY.NS) gained 3% after posting higher-than-expected September quarter profit, as domestic demand cushioned weakness in its crucial US market.
