item.title: Anthony Edwards, Timberwolves cruise past Raptors
item.description: Anthony Edwards scored 26 points on 10-for-18 shooting, and the Minnesota Timberwolves pulled away for a 117-94 win over the Toronto Raptors on Sunday evening in Minneapolis.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Anthony Edwards scored 26 points on 10-for-18 shooting, and the Minnesota Timberwolves pulled away for a 117-94 win over the Toronto Raptors on Sunday evening in Minneapolis. LaMelo Ball finished with 15 points and eight assists for Minnesota, which won its third game in a row to start the season. Terrence Shannon Jr. also scored 15 points off the bench, and Jaden McDaniels recorded 14 points on 6-for-10 shooting. Ja'Kobe Walter scored 22 points on 7-for-12 shooting to lead Toronto, which sustained its first loss after starting the season with back-to-back wins. RJ Barrett added 20 points, and Immanuel Quickley scored 19. Scottie Barnes was 0-for-12, including 0-for-5 from distance, in 28 minutes. Raptors star forward Kawhi Leonard was scratched before the game because of swelling in his left knee. The 35-year-old Leonard is averaging 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals through two games in his return to Toronto. Toronto trailed by 21-plus points throughout the fourth quarter. Minnesota outscored Toronto 35-15 in the third quarter to grab a 90-62 advantage. The Timberwolves opened the second half with a 22-6 run to grab a 77-53 edge midway through the third quarter. Ball started the run with a layup, and McDaniels added a three-point play less than a minute later. Second-year big man Joan Beringer provided the scoring at the end of the run for Minnesota. He made an alley-oop dunk off a lob from Ball with 6:21 to go in the third quarter and then drained a pair of free throws to make it a 24-point lead with 5:46 left. The Timberwolves jumped to an 11-point lead at the end of the first quarter. Shannon converted a three-point play with 22 seconds remaining to secure the double-digit lead. Minnesota opened the second quarter on a 6-0 run to increase its lead to 17 points as McDaniels and Shannon buried back-to-back 3-pointers. The Raptors finished the first half on a 10-4 run to cut the deficit to eight points. Quickley hit a 3-pointer and Collin Murray-Boyles made a free throw to cap the first-half scoring. --Field Level Media

item.title: China's Xi opens Communist Party plenum, aims for firm governance measures
item.description: China's Communist Party began a four-day meeting of its highest-ranking members on Monday targeting concrete measures for "full and rigorous party self-governance", as President Xi Jinping seeks to reinforce his authority and enforce ideological uniformity.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's Communist Party began a four-day meeting of its highest-ranking members on Monday targeting concrete measures for "full and rigorous party self-governance", as President Xi Jinping seeks to [USN:L6N46909C TEXT:"reinforce"] his authority and enforce ideological uniformity. Xi briefed the party's Central Committee on a draft document that state news agency Xinhua said addressed the challenges the party faced, including growing its governing capacity, as well as guarding against complacency and combating corruption, the president's signature campaign. The implementation of major decisions and plans of the Central Committee, the largest of its top decision-making bodies, must not be empty rhetoric, the commentary wrote. "It is essential to both refine institutional rules and regulations to close loopholes and strengthen safeguards, and ensure their effective implementation," it said. The Central Committee will convene in the [USN:L6N4690N6 TEXT:"closed-door meeting"] from Monday to Thursday - the fifth since the current cohort was formed in 2022 and therefore known as the fifth plenum. Analysts say this could be the last major party gathering before its 2027 leadership reshuffle, when Xi is expected to hold on to the top job for a fourth term. ROOTING OUT CORRUPTION FOR MARKET PREDICTABILITY Xi has overseen a vast anti-corruption campaign in recent years which has led to the purge of hundreds of senior officials and top generals, even the president's [USN:L4N3YQ02T TEXT:"one-time allies"]. While critics argue the purges - particularly those targeting the highest ranks of the armed forces - are destabilising and undermine combat readiness, the party has portrayed the campaign as both necessary and regenerative, saying the military must undergo a phoenix-like rebirth and "bathe in flames and be forged anew." The Xinhua commentary propped up the anti-corruption drive as a demonstration of "sustained and systemic" self-governance to "ensure officials dare not, cannot and do not want to commit corruption". "For global investors and policymakers, this signals greater predictability," it said, arguing that China was also creating a more transparent environment for international cooperation as merit and the rule of law prevail over connections and bribery.

item.title: Currency markets subdued ahead of busy central bank week
item.description: Major currencies traded in tight ranges on Monday at the start of a busy week of central bank decisions and corporate earnings, while a pullback in oil prices and Treasury yields weighed on the dollar.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxing Li
item.content:encoded: Major currencies traded in tight ranges on Monday at the start of a busy week of central bank decisions and corporate earnings, while a pullback in oil prices and Treasury yields weighed on the dollar. Oil prices [USN:L2N46B09G TEXT:"eased"], with Brent crude futures down nearly 2% at $114.50 a barrel after surging to a six-month high last week, following a Reuters [USN:S8N43E021 TEXT:"report"] that Qatari mediators were in Tehran on Sunday as part of an effort to de-escalate regional tensions in coordination with the US. Meanwhile, US Treasuries largely held onto gains from a recent safe-haven rally, as a [USN:L6N468196 TEXT:"tech-led selloff"] over concerns about AI spurred a rotation out of risk assets even as elevated oil prices kept inflation worries alive. Yields on US 10-year notes were last down to 4.967% while those on 30-year notes were at 5.299%, hovering near one-month lows. "For the time being, it seems to point to the US bond market being in the driving seat for broader dollar performance," said Ray Attrill, head of FX strategy at National Australia Bank. "The market is sort of responding to the fall we've seen in Treasury yields and the fact that yield differentials between the US and other kind of G10 majors are compressing. I think that's taken a little bit of the heat out of the US dollar." The euro rose 0.15% against the greenback to $1.1218, amid relief that France was spared a Moody's [USN:L1N469154 TEXT:"downgrade"] despite social unrest. Sterling strengthened 0.1% to $1.3379. The dollar index , which measures the US currency against a basket of peers, was little changed at 101.65. The Australian dollar was flat at $0.7031 and New Zealand's kiwi traded 0.05% stronger at $0.5701 . The Japanese yen was steady at 156.92 per dollar. [USN:L6N46919T TEXT:"Corporate earnings"] reports from hyperscalers Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Amazon (AMZN.O) will also test the fragile AI-led market rally and broader risk appetite. CENTRAL BANK DECISIONS IN FOCUS Five major central banks will announce closely watched policy decisions later in the week. The US [USN:L6N46606V TEXT:"Federal Reserve"], the [USN:L6N45U0QU TEXT:"European Central Bank"] and the [USN:L3N46C02N TEXT:"Bank of Japan"] are all expected to hold rates steady despite inflation pressures, while leaving room for December hikes. [USN:L4N4690C8 TEXT:"New Zealand"] and [USN:L6N46911N TEXT:"Canada"]'s central banks are expected to raise rates this week. "Forward guidance could matter more than the decisions themselves," said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone, in a note. "The decisions themselves may be largely discounted. The real issue that could move the dial in short-term rates ... is how policymakers shape expectations for subsequent meetings and whether markets need to reprice the forward rates curve." Investors will also be paying attention to a packed US economic calendar — including the October consumer confidence (USCONC=ECI) report, the PCE price index (USPCEM=ECI) and jobless claims (USJOB=ECI) — which could provide additional clues on the outlook for Fed policy. Elsewhere, spot gold was slightly higher, trading at $4,014 per ounce. In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin was down 0.3% at $80,134.29, while ether was 0.9% lower at $2,323.34.

item.title: Thunder star Jalen Williams injures leg in win over Clippers
item.description: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 34 points to lead Oklahoma City to a 108-101 home win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Sunday that was marred by a gruesome leg injury to Thunder star Jalen Williams.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 34 points to lead Oklahoma City to a 108-101 home win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Sunday that was marred by a gruesome leg injury to Thunder star Jalen Williams. With 1:14 remaining in the fourth quarter, Williams went up for a dunk and landed hard and awkwardly on his left leg on what was ruled a flagrant 1 foul by Kris Dunn after video review. Williams started to try to get up after the fall, but teammate Chet Holmgren motioned for him to remain down. Williams was eventually carted off on a stretcher, offering a thumbs-up to the crowd as they chanted his nickname "J-Dub." Williams, 25, was limited to just 33 regular-season games last season and missed much of Oklahoma City's run to the Western Conference Finals. The shooting guard/forward was the third rotation player injured in the game for the team. The Thunder did not announce a diagnosis on Williams' injury, with head coach Mark Daigneault saying the team will be updated Monday. "I just feel bad for him," Gilgeous-Alexander told reporters after the game. "It's obviously going to be tough without a player like that. But he's not gone forever. He'll be back better than ever, and we know it. We've just got to hold the fort down until he comes back." Cason Wallace left the game less than halfway through the first quarter with left shoulder soreness after a collision coming off a screen. At the end of the first, Jaylin Williams exited with right wrist soreness. After Jalen Williams left the game, Gilgeous-Alexander hit a pair of free throws in his place to extend the lead to six and then hit another free throw on the next possession to virtually put the game away. Oklahoma City has won three consecutive games to start the season. A game after Gilgeous-Alexander's NBA-record streak of scoring 20 or more points came to an end, the back-to-back NBA Most Valuable Player didn't have a problem reaching that mark with a 16-point third quarter. Gilgeous-Alexander finished 13-of-26 from the floor and 7-of-8 from the free-throw line. Darius Garland led the Clippers with 16 points and 11 assists. The Clippers went up 64-57 on Garland's 3-pointer midway through the third quarter. Oklahoma City's bench then fueled a 20-10 run to put the Thunder back in front. Alex Caruso had five points, two assists and a steal in the stretch including hitting a game-tying 3-pointer. Nine of Oklahoma City's points during the stretch came off turnovers. Ajay Mitchell scored 18 points off the bench in the win while Isaiah Hartenstein had 12 points and 12 rebounds. The Thunder scored 38 points off 26 Clippers turnovers. The game was the first of a back-to-back for Oklahoma City. --Field Level Media

item.title: Lula crée la surprise et remporte l'élection présidentielle au Brésil
item.description: Le président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva a remporté dimanche un nouveau mandat à la tête du Brésil, a annoncé le tribunal électoral national, un résultat surprenant alors que les sondages donnaient son adversaire, le sénateur de droite Flavio Bolsonaro, en tête.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes, Pedro Fonseca
item.content:encoded: Le président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva a remporté dimanche un nouveau mandat à la tête du Brésil, a annoncé le tribunal électoral national, un résultat surprenant alors que les sondages donnaient son adversaire, le sénateur de droite Flavio Bolsonaro, en tête. Lula, figure de la gauche qui a déjà occupé par trois fois les fonctions de président, s'est imposé face au fils de l'ancien président d'extrême-droite Jair Bolsonaro lors du deuxième tour du scrutin. Flavio Bolsonaro, qui était arrivé en tête au premier tour, a déclaré qu'il demanderait l'annulation du résultat en raison d'une décision rendue dimanche par la Cour suprême du Brésil de prolonger de deux heures la durée du vote. L'ampleur de la défaite de Flavio Bolsonaro face à Lula et le fait que sa campagne ait également demandé de prolonger la durée du vote en raison des pluies dans le sud du pays rendent toute annulation peu probable, ont estimé les analystes. UN PARCOURS INATTENDU VERS LA VICTOIRE Les sondeurs estiment que le taux de participation, plus élevé qu'attendu, a joué en faveur de Lula. "Les gens devaient choisir aujourd'hui entre le changement, avec une certaine appréhension, et rester en terrain connu, ce qui garantit certains droits", a dit Leonardo Barreto, du cabinet de conseil Think Policy, pour qui les électeurs ont préféré Lula, qui leur est familier, à Flavio Bolsonaro, qui représentait la nouveauté. Durant la campagne, Lula s'est notamment appuyé sur son bilan, alors que le chômage, l'illettrisme et la déforestation ont atteint des plus bas inédit durant son troisième mandat. Il avait prévenu que son adversaire réduirait les allocations, reviendrait sur les avancées sociales et offrirait la souveraineté du Brésil au président américain Donald Trump. Durant la campagne, Lula a accusé l'administration Trump d'ingérence électorale et dénoncé des actes d'intimidation de la part de Washington. Samedi, Reuters a révélé l'existence d'une campagne menée par le département d'Etat américain pour aider les Bolsonaro à revenir au pouvoir. LE ROI DU "COME-BACK" Cette victoire marque un nouveau "come-back" pour Lula, 80 ans. "C'est un homme d'Etat. Un géant", a déclaré à Reuters l'élue de gauche Erika Hilton, qui était aux côtés de Lula lors du dépouillement. Lula devient le premier candidat depuis le retour du Brésil à la démocratie dans les années 1980 à remporter une élection présidentielle après être arrivé en deuxième position au premier tour. Le président sortant avait fait campagne en s'appuyant sur le savant mélange de pragmatisme et de populisme qui a marqué sa carrière politique pendant un demi-siècle, promettant de mettre en oeuvre une série de réformes visant à améliorer les conditions de vie des travailleurs et des Brésiliens défavorisés. En fin de campagne, il a pris divers engagements comme la gratuité des transports publics le week-end à l'échelle nationale – mesure qui doit encore être officiellement soumise au Parlement – ou une augmentation de 15% de son programme phare d'aide sociale - dont la mise en oeuvre est déjà en cours. Lula a également défendu un amendement constitutionnel qui a donné lieu à la plus grande réforme du droit du travail que le Brésil ait connue depuis des décennies, et qui a été adopté avec un large soutien au sein du Congrès. Figure de proue du Parti des travailleurs (PT), Lula s'est retrouvé en 2016 au coeur d'une enquête tentaculaire pour des soupçons de corruption. Il avait alors passé 580 jours en prison avant que sa condamnation ne soit annulée pour des vices de procédure. Cette peine l'a toutefois empêché de se présenter à l'élection présidentielle de 2018 remportée par Jair Bolsonaro. UN MANDAT QUI S'AVÈRE DIFFICILE Le quatrième mandat de Lula pourrait toutefois être le plus difficile, alors que le Brésil a élu le Congrès le plus conservateur depuis le retour à la démocratie. Le parti de Flavio Bolsonaro, le Parti libéral (PL), et ses alliés pourraient contrôler plus de 280 sièges de la chambre basse du Parlement, et jusqu'à 50 sièges au Sénat, assez pour bénéficier de majorités confortables dans les deux chambres. "Il risque d'avoir des difficultés dès le début de son mandat", a déclaré Oliver Stuenkel, professeur de relations internationales à la Fondation Getulio Vargas de São Paulo. VENTS CONTRAIRES ÉCONOMIQUES Lula sera également confronté à une économie qui, selon les prévisions de son gouvernement, devrait croître de seulement 2,3% l'année prochaine, ce qui alimente les inquiétudes liées aux taux d'intérêt élevés et à la dette publique, qui a dépassé les 82% du produit intérieur brut, un plus haut depuis la pandémie de COVID-19. Les détracteurs du président imputent cette situation aux dépenses, alors que ce sont les intérêts qui ont principalement contribué à l'augmentation de la dette publique. Goldman Sachs a déclaré s'attendre à ce que Lula ne parvienne, tout au plus, qu'à des progrès modestes pour maîtriser les dépenses au cours d'un quatrième mandat, car il reste attaché à un modèle de croissance piloté par l'Etat. La hausse fulgurante de l'endettement des ménages inquiète également les économistes. Pour tenter de remédier à ce problème, Lula a mis en place une interdiction provisoire des paris en ligne et a dévoilé un nouveau programme d'allègement de la dette pendant la campagne.

item.title: Japanese companies compensate users as cyberattacks buffet economy
item.description: Japanese companies are moving to pay compensation to users following waves of cyberattacks that have disrupted internet services and raised concerns about economic stability.
item.dc:creator: Kentaro Okasaka, Sam Nussey
item.content:encoded: Japanese companies are moving to pay compensation to users following waves of cyberattacks that have disrupted internet services and raised concerns about economic stability. GMO Internet Group (9449.T) , a leading provider of online financial services, said customers would be compensated for losses stemming from unauthorised access following a cyberattack on its foreign exchange trading service, and all customers would receive 5,000 yen ($32) as a gesture of goodwill, CEO Masatoshi Kumagai said in a blog post on Sunday. "The internet itself is now starting to break down," said Kumagai, whose sprawling group includes internet infrastructure and cryptocurrency trading. Japan said on Friday it would set up a team to [USN:L1N469098 TEXT:"simulate cyberattacks"] using AI to identify weaknesses in technology systems as organisations scrambled to curtail risks from flaws in the [USN:L6N467127 TEXT:"PHP programming language"] that underpins much of the internet. More broadly, Japanese companies are being roiled by attacks with experts saying AI is helping automate tasks from scanning for software vulnerabilities to crafting phishing campaigns, making cybercrime faster, cheaper and harder to detect. "The internet is increasingly being transformed into a tool that malicious actors use to threaten and rob people," said Kumagai. Shares of GMO, which had a market value of $2.6 billion as of Friday's close, slumped almost 16% to a four-month low against a 0.2% rise in Tokyo's benchmark index (.TOPX) . Government and company websites in Japan, Europe and elsewhere [USN:L6N46813V TEXT:"went offline"] last week after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language prompted millions of hacking attempts. CALL ON JAPAN TO STEP UP CYBERDEFENCE Kumagai has urged the Japanese government to apply cyberdefence measures in response to the cyberattack, after the introduction of a cyberdefence system this month. The system could involve steps such as attacking hostile servers to neutralise threats. "Now is the time for the public and private sectors to work together to protect Japan," wrote Kumagai. GMO said it received a demand for money from a party believed to be behind the attack, along with a threat to disclose company and customer information if it did not comply. GMO said it would not comply with the demand and would respond to the incident in coordination with police and other authorities. It did not mention any connection to PHP flaws. The company, which will provide a free alternative service to its customers for six months, said it could not currently calculate the impact on earnings from the goodwill payments and compensation for losses. White-hat hackers working for the company had identified security issues but the depth and speed of the response were insufficient, Kumagai wrote. CUSTOMER DATA PROTECTION WEAKNESSES The scale of recent cyberattacks has exposed weaknesses in Japanese companies' ability to protect their wealth of customer data and raised the prospect of surging costs to beef up defences. "Companies already have standard security measures in place, so if they want to strengthen them further, there is a possibility that the additional cost burden could be quite substantial," said Shoichi Arisawa, an analyst at IwaiCosmo Securities. There have been 723 cybersecurity incidents in the year to October 20, according to data from TrendAI, exceeding the annual totals in 2025 and 2024. "Reports may reflect both the threats organizations face and greater visibility into incidents that would previously have gone undetected, been underinvestigated, or remained undisclosed," said Satoshi Nagano, president of cybersecurity firm ESET Japan. Park24 (4666.T) , which operates the Times car-sharing service, said on Friday it would make 3,000-yen payments to customers following a personal data breach last month. The company said it would no longer retain identity document images after completing registration verification and expects to book an extraordinary loss of 5.5 billion yen due to responses to the attack and compensation payments. ($1 = 156.8100 yen)

item.title: Saudi Arabia to store oil in Singapore to bolster Asia supply security
item.description: Saudi Arabia plans to store crude oil at Singapore's Jurong Rock Caverns from the second half of 2027 to strengthen supply security in the region, energy ministers from both countries said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Florence Tan, Jeslyn Lerh
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia plans to store crude oil at Singapore's Jurong Rock Caverns from the second half of 2027 to strengthen supply security in the region, energy ministers from both countries said on Monday. The move comes after the US-Israeli war with Iran severely disrupted energy supplies to Asia shipped through the Strait of Hormuz, prompting countries to draw down inventories and raising concerns about stockpile levels globally. Asia imported two-thirds of its oil supplies from the Middle East before the war. "Saudi Arabia and Singapore are announcing our joint intent to establish an arrangement for Saudi crude oil to be stored at the Jurong Rock Caverns from the second half of 2027," Tan See Leng, minister for energy, trade and industry, told the Singapore International Energy Week conference. "This arrangement enhances the resilience of the Saudi crude oil supply chain in Southeast Asia, as well as contributes to Singapore's energy security and resilience in the event of supply disruptions." Tan said Saudi Aramco will sign a memorandum of understanding with the Energy Market Authority and JTC Corp on Monday and aimed to conclude negotiations in a few months' time. "Bringing supply closer to key Asian markets would strengthen the flexibility of our supply network and support Singapore's security of supply and preparedness," Saudi Arabia's Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman Al-Saud said in a video recording at the conference. Located at a depth of 150 metres (492 feet) below the ground, the rock caverns at Jurong Island can store up to 1.47 million cubic metres, or roughly 9 million barrels of liquid hydrocarbons such as crude oil and condensate. Saudi Aramco currently stores crude in Japan and South Korea where local governments have priority to buy the supplies in the tanks in the event of an unexpected shortage. The crude storage capacity in Okinawa was expanded to 8.2 million barrels in September 2017 in an agreement with Japan Oil, Gas and Metals National Corp (JOGMEC), Aramco Japan said on its website. In 2023, [USN:L4N3BU0GY TEXT:"Aramco inked a deal"] with Korea National Oil Corp to store 5.3 million barrels of oil in South Korea's reserve facilities in the port of Ulsan for five years. Elsewhere, [USN:L1N45S03O TEXT:"Japan is in talks"] with Asian countries to boost crude reserves across the region, part of the Partnership in Wide Energy and Resources Resilience Asia (POWERR Asia) initiative proposed earlier this year by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi backed by $10 billion in financial support. While China, Japan and South Korea have built large oil stockpiles, most other Asian countries have less of a buffer in the event of supply shocks.

item.title: Japan's Nikkei falls for a 3rd day as tech sector weighs, energy shares rise
item.description: Japan's Nikkei share gauge lost ground for a third straight session on Monday as chip-related shares continued their decline, while energy-linked shares gained on higher oil prices.
item.dc:creator: Rocky Swift
item.content:encoded: Japan's Nikkei share gauge lost ground for a third straight session on Monday as chip-related shares continued their decline, while energy-linked shares gained on higher oil prices. The benchmark Nikkei 225 (.N225) slid 0.80% to close at 62,189.65, its lowest closing level since July 30. The broader Topix (.TOPX) edged up 0.18% to 3,972.98. US share gauges ended lower on Friday, but the S&P 500 energy sector rose 2.5% to a [USN:L6N46917T TEXT:"record"]. Oil prices [USN:L2N46B09G TEXT:"slid"] from a six-month high on Monday after reports that Qatari mediators visited Tehran to seek de-escalation in coordination with the United States, following intensified Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia that had stoked supply concerns. "The Nikkei Stock Average is showing signs of short-term technical undervaluation," Monex Securities senior analyst Satoshi Saito said in a note. "Stocks may see phases of short-term rebound, but with several concerns in the background, the recovery may remain sluggish for now." The market was also impacted by the latest in a wave of cyberattacks that have disrupted internet services and leaked customer information. GMO Internet Group (9449.T) said customers would be [USN:L2N46C02R TEXT:"compensated"] for losses stemming from unauthorised access following an attack on its foreign exchange trading service. Its shares plunged 15.65%, the sharpest decline since March 2011. Breadth was largely positive on the Nikkei, but the heavy weighting of tech shares dragged it lower. The gauge had 149 gainers and just 73 decliners. The largest losers were online retailer Mercari (4385.T) , down 6.21%, followed by Screen Holdings (7735.T) , 4.34% lower, and Kokusai Electric (6525.T) , which lost 4.29%. The biggest winners were energy explorer Inpex (1605.T) , up 4.90%, followed by internet security firm Trend Micro (4704.T) , 4.20% higher, and Mitsubishi Corp (8058.T) , which gained 4.14%.

item.title: Stocks trade warily in Asia, Brent off six-month top
item.description: Stock markets traded cautiously on Monday as oil eased from six-month highs ahead of a week packed with central bank meetings and corporate earnings that will further test investor confidence in the AI boom.
item.dc:creator: Wayne Cole
item.content:encoded: Stock markets traded cautiously on Monday as oil eased from six-month highs ahead of a week packed with central bank meetings and corporate earnings that will further test investor confidence in the AI boom. Brent oil slipped 1.9% to $114.48 following reports that [USN:S8N43E021 TEXT:"Qatari mediators"] were in Tehran on Sunday as part of an effort to de-escalate regional tensions in coordination with the US. Brent futures jumped 6.2% last week to their highest weekly close since mid-2022 as Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns about energy supplies. US crude futures fell 2.2% to $101.01 a barrel. The Houthi group in Yemen said on Monday it had attacked Saudi Arabia's [USN:L2N46C045 TEXT:"East-West crude oil"] pumping stations and Riyadh airport, but there was no immediate confirmation from Riyadh. Japan's Nikkei (.N225) dipped 0.2% after losing 4.0% last week, while South Korea's main index (.KS11) fell 0.5%, having shed almost 20% so far this month. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares excluding Japan (.MIAPJ0000PUS) was flat. Chinese blue chips (.CSI300) lost 0.5%, as China's ruling [USN:L6N46C04K TEXT:"Communist Party"] began its fifth plenum in Beijing. The market has now fallen for 11 weeks straight amid concerns about domestic demand - even as exports remain strong. The inflationary pulse from oil is likely to alarm all the central banks that are meeting this week, with hikes seen as just a matter of time even if some hold for now. "The main message from global central banks grappling with this year's macroeconomic surprises is that a relatively shallow rate-hike cycle is underway," said Bruce Kasman, global head of economics at JPMorgan. "G3 central banks are likely to remain on hold, but [USN:L6N46911N TEXT:"Canada"] should start its tightening cycle and first moves are expected from the UK and Sweden next month." [USN:L4N4690C8 TEXT:"New Zealand's"] central bank is widely expected to raise rates on Wednesday. Markets assume the US [USN:L6N46606V TEXT:"Federal Reserve"] will stand pat, but they imply an 80% chance that it will pull the trigger in December. Much the same is priced in for the [USN:L4N4650KC TEXT:"Bank of Japan"] and the [USN:L6N45U0QU TEXT:"European Central Bank"]. , , A key reading on US core inflation should show cost pressures remained elevated at 3.1% in September, while the economy is forecast to have grown at a brisk 3.2% annualised pace thanks in part to furious spending on data centres. "The Fed is set to skip raising rates at its October meeting but is likely to deliver a second hike in December," analysts at Goldman Sachs said in a note. "The most important risk is that oil futures are above our forecasts, largely reflecting concerns about potential further conflict with Iran," they added. "The more extreme and long-lasting the energy shock becomes, the more Fed participants will worry that inflationary pressures could broaden." HYPERSCALERS TO TEST AI HYPE On Wall Street, S&P 500 futures edged up 0.2%, while Nasdaq futures added 0.1%. In Europe, EUROSTOXX 50 futures firmed 0.3%, DAX futures gained 0.3% and FTSE futures gained 0.4%. Earnings [USN:L6N46919T TEXT:"highlights"] will include the hyperscalers Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Amazon (AMZN.O) , among one-third of S&P 500 companies reporting. Results from Intel (INTC.O) and Sandisk (SNDK.O) also could influence the AI trade. The analyst consensus on Microsoft is for $90.6 billion in revenue and an adjusted EPS of $4.73, with Amazon at $202 billion in revenue and EPS around $1.97. Alphabet revenue is seen at $128 billion with EPS of $3.00. In Asia, SK Hynix (000660.KS) and Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) both report this week. [USN:L2N46C01C TEXT:"SK Hynix"] also said it will unveil shareholder return measures on Wednesday, responding to a report that it is considering a special dividend of about 16 trillion won ($12 billion). Equity valuations have been tested by higher bond yields, though Treasuries did manage a rally last week before running into renewed selling on Friday. Yields on 10-year Treasuries were at 4.97%, well off a peak of 5.36% hit early in the month. In currency markets, the Japanese yen retained its safe-haven appeal at 156.90 per dollar , having gained around 0.8% last week. The euro added 0.1% to $1.1220 after France dodged a [USN:L1N469154 TEXT:"credit downgrade"] last week. Sterling held at $1.3346 with Britain's new finance minister, [USN:L1N46206Z TEXT:"John Healey"], set to deliver his first budget on Wednesday against a backdrop of rising global borrowing costs and high energy prices due to the US-Israeli war on Iran. The Brazilian real had yet to trade in Asia as Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva [USN:L2N46B01X TEXT:"won"] an unprecedented fourth term on Sunday, according to the country's electoral court. Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro refused to concede and said he would seek the annulment of the runoff election. An ETF of Brazilian stocks traded in Tokyo (1325.T) shed 15%, reversing gains made when Bolsonaro led in the first round of voting. In commodity markets, non-interest-bearing gold was 0.4% firmer at $4,012 an ounce , having fallen more than 4% last week.

item.title: Trump says Canada tariff deal coming 'soon' at Michigan border rally
item.description: President Donald Trump at a Sunday political rally predicted a trade dispute with Canada would be resolved "soon," without providing specifics.
item.dc:creator: Valerie Volcovici
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump at a Sunday political rally predicted a trade dispute with Canada would be resolved "soon," without providing specifics. At an event in Port Huron, Michigan, to boost Republican candidates ahead of the November 3 midterms, Trump and other speakers reiterated his oft-expressed position that higher tariffs on Canadian goods are needed because Canada "has been ripping off" the US in trade. "I had to do it," Trump told the Michigan crowd. "We'll have that settled pretty soon. They're willing to give us anything at this moment." The office of Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Trump won in Michigan's border region that includes Port Huron in the 2024 presidential election with more than 66% of the vote, but the local economy has felt the impacts of the US-Canada tariff standoff, including the Detroit-based US auto industry. Republican Congressman Mike Rogers, who is running in a tight race against Democratic rival Abdul El-Sayed, has tried to distance himself from the president's tariff policy on the auto sector. Rogers on Sunday hailed Trump's tariffs for securing manufacturing investments for Michigan by Chevrolet and Detroit Diesel, but said "the automobile portion of these Canadian tariffs worries me a little bit." "There's some good and there's some things we have to work on," he told "Meet the Press."

item.title: Oil drops from near six-month highs on hopes Iran war hostilities to ease
item.description: Oil prices fell on Monday after surging last week to near six-month highs, amid hopes of easing hostilities between the United States and Iran, although persistent attacks on key producer Saudi Arabia kept investors wary.
item.dc:creator: Mohi Narayan, Colleen Howe
item.content:encoded: Oil prices fell on Monday after surging last week to near six-month highs, amid hopes of easing hostilities between the United States and Iran, although persistent attacks on key producer Saudi Arabia kept investors wary. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down $2.23, or 2.16%, at $101.04 per barrel by 0426 GMT. Brent crude futures were down $2.21, or 1.89%, at $114.51. On Friday, prices [USN:L1N46903W TEXT:"settled"] nearly $3 higher after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked energy supply concerns. Brent finished the week up 6% and WTI ended 2.3% higher. On Sunday, Qatari [USN:S8N43E021 TEXT:"mediators"] traveled to Tehran as part of an effort to de-escalate regional tensions in coordination with the United States, an official briefed on the situation said. "Concerns over renewed military hostilities in the Middle East, which drove much of last week’s crude rally, have eased this morning, but the reprieve may prove temporary," said Vandana Hari, founder of oil market analysis provider Vanda Insights. Hari said US President Donald Trump has not dispelled market expectations that strikes on Iran could still follow after the November 3 midterm elections. "We therefore expect volatility to remain elevated, with risks still skewed to the upside," she added. Despite the mediation talks, attacks continued over the weekend with the Iran-backed Houthis saying they struck an airport and oil facilities in Saudi Arabia on Saturday. Saudi Arabia said on Sunday it had intercepted more missiles and drones. The effects of the US-Israeli war on Iran that began on February 28 continue to reverberate as companies adjust to the disruptions of [USN:L1N4690RP TEXT:"commercial shipping"] through the key Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb Strait caused by the conflict. On Monday, the energy ministers from Saudi Arabia and Singapore said state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco will start [USN:L2N46C022 TEXT:"storing"] crude oil in Singapore from the second half of 2027, to shore up the resilience of Aramco's supply chain in the region. "While supply risks surrounding the Strait of Hormuz remain firmly entrenched, the current pullback appears more reflective of position adjustments and risk management rather than any meaningful improvement in the underlying supply situation," said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insight at Phillip Nova. The [USN:P8N3RS06K TEXT:"head"] of the International Energy Agency, Fatih Birol, reinforced the concerns about the supply situation, saying on Monday at an industry event in Singapore that he does not expect energy markets in 2027 to return to where they were before the Iran war.

item.title: Belgrade in rapture as Serbian students topple Vucic in historic election
item.description: It was the culmination of a two-year protest movement that called for Vucic to step down.
item.dc:creator: Edward Mcallister, Kirsten Donovan, Aleksandar Vasovic
item.content:encoded: Trams and traffic halted by crowds. Tens of thousands of people choking the city's main boulevards; the air thick with smoke; a man on a car waving a flare. Familiar-sounding scenes after a month of sometimes violent protests across European cities as students take to the streets calling for better education standards and better prospects. Except, on Sunday night in Serbia's capital Belgrade, students were not protesting but celebrating an election victory after long-time ruler Aleksandar Vucic [USN:L6N46B017 TEXT:"conceded defeat"] to a student-backed list of candidates in parliamentary elections. It was the culmination of a two-year, [USN:L8N4650K6 TEXT:"peaceful protest movement"] that called for Vucic to step down and an end to what they said is rampant corruption in the Balkan country - a charge Vucic denies. The students' win marks a profound political shift in the country of some 6 million people and shows what power younger generation have when they are able to harness widespread discontent. "That is the best thing that happened in my life. We will now breathe freely," said Milica, a law student. Vucic had ruled as prime minister or president since 2014, and oversaw a period of strong economic growth, but he faced growing opposition from student-led protests after the collapse of a railway station awning killed 16 people in November 2024. Tomorrow, the disparate group of 250 student-backed candidates will have to turn towards ruling, but Sunday evening was a time to party. At their headquarters, the unknown candidates, many of them lawyers, professors, actors or farmers, hugged and cheered in near disbelief at what they had achieved. "The people have won! The people defeated a dictator! The people will lead Serbia!" said Nebojsa Cosic while waving a flag on the street.

item.title: Real Madrid defeat Barcelona at Camp Nou to halve gap to LaLiga leaders
item.description: Kylian Mbappe's 11th goal in 10 LaLiga matches secured victory for Jose Mourinho in his return to El Clasico 13 years after his first spell at Real Madrid ended.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: Real Madrid became the first side to beat Barcelona in LaLiga this season, defeating the league leaders 2-1 at Camp Nou with a brace from Kylian Mbappe. Mbappe's 11th goal in 10 LaLiga matches secured victory for Jose Mourinho in his return to El Clasico 13 years after his first spell at Real Madrid ended. Real halved the gap to league leaders Barcelona to three points. "It was the most difficult match, against the highest quality opponent, one that had only won in the league," Mourinho told reporters. "For us, it's the victory with the most impressive performance." Both sides created a series of half-chances early on, but Real's forays forward came with far more resolve. Barca manager Hansi Flick's frustration on the touchline served as evidence that Mourinho's [USN:L6N46B0AT TEXT:"game plan"] was functioning better than his own. In the 41st minute, Yan Diomande crossed from the left and Gerard Martin's soft clearance hit the onrushing Mbappe, bouncing off him and into the net. Barcelona had the chance to level before the break after a fortunate ricochet, but Lamine Yamal couldn't convert from close range. It was a set piece that undid Real in the 61st minute, with Pedri's reverse pass finding Raphinha in space in the box and the Brazilian finishing into the corner. Real's swift movement of the ball in their own half continued to expose the Barcelona backline in the early stages of the second half. However, following the goal, the visitors found it increasingly hard to escape Barcelona's pressing. Barcelona's attacks were now finishing with last-ditch blocks from the Real defence, even if Mourinho's side continued to carry a threat going forward. That defensive conviction was rewarded with three minutes remaining. A loose touch from Barcelona substitute Gabriel Jesus set Real on the counter-attack, and substitute Eduardo Camavinga had enough pace to get in behind the defence, before squaring the ball for Mbappe to tap into the empty net. "It's two defeats and we're not happy," Flick told reporters. "We're disappointed. We lacked freshness." The defeat ended Barcelona's nine-match winning start to the league campaign and came days after a 4-2 [USN:L6N4661CR TEXT:"Champions League defeat"] by Paris St Germain. Flick pointed to a demanding run of travel as a factor behind his side's drop in energy levels. "These past few weeks haven't been easy. You only see the matches, but being on a plane for three hours to Seville, returning to the hotel, then going to Paris; it's a lot," he said. "I don't want to talk about this when we lose. It's better when we win, and I won't accept excuses." Barcelona remain top of the standings with 27 points from 10 games, one ahead of Atletico Madrid in second place. Third-place Real Madrid are on 24 points. Earlier Athletic Club beat Getafe 4-0 and Real Sociedad won 2-1 against Levante. Real Betis remain fourth after drawing 0-0 with Celta Vigo.

item.title: Lars Eller scores first goal with Panthers in narrow win over Blackhawks
item.description: Lars Eller tallied the go-ahead goal with 2:23 remaining in the third period and Sandis Vilmanis and Matthew Tkachuk also scored to lift the visiting Florida Panthers to a 3-2 victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Lars Eller tallied the go-ahead goal with 2:23 remaining in the third period and Sandis Vilmanis and Matthew Tkachuk also scored to lift the visiting Florida Panthers to a 3-2 victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Sunday. Panthers goaltender Akira Schmid stopped 19 shots as Florida snapped a two-game losing streak. Schmid turned aside Cole Smith on a breakaway with 5:45 to keep the game tied at 2. Eller netted his first goal of the season at 17:37 of the third period as the Panthers caught the Blackhawks in a line change. Eller took a long pass from Aaron Ekblad just inside the blue line, weaved down the right side and ripped a wrist shot from the circle past Chicago goaltender Spencer Knight. For the 37-old-year Eller, it was also his first goal as a member of the Florida Panthers. He started his NHL career with the St. Louis Blues in the 2009-10 season and has played for the Montreal Canadiens (2010-16), Washington Capitals (2016-23, 2024-25), Colorado Avalanche (2023), Pittsburgh Penguins (2023-25) and Ottawa Senators (2025-26). Special-teams struggles hurt the Blackhawks, who went 0-for-7 on the power play while also failing to capitalize on other chances at even strength. Knight made 30 saves. Chicago managed just six shots in the first period, but one of the club's early attempts provided a 1-0 lead. Ryan Greene tracked a puck that bounced at the top of the crease and into the air and batted it past Schmid and into the net. Andrew Mangiapane earned the primary assist in his return to the lineup; the forward had been out since sustaining a lower-body injury in the club's season opener on Sept. 29. Florida tied the game just over four minutes later, as Vilmanis backhanded a loose puck past Knight after the backstop made a save on Sam Reinhart. The Panthers took a 2-1 lead on Matthew Tkachuk's power-play goal at 14:21 of the first. Tkachuk deflected Seth Jones' shot from the point just five seconds into the man advantage. Chicago netted the equalizer at 11:15 of the second period when Roman Kantserov took a Patrick Kane feed from behind the net and scored on a wrist shot from the right circle. Florida limited Chicago to one shot on goal during a four-minute power-play early in the second period after Carter Verhaeghe was whistled for a high-sticking double minor against the Blackhawks' Wyatt Kaiser. Verhaeghe sent a wrist shot off the crossbar on a breakaway moments after springing from the penalty box. The Blackhawks fell to 2-4-0 on a seven-game homestand that is set to conclude with Tuesday's visit from the Los Angeles Kings. --Field Level Media

item.title: North Korea-South Korea tensions high as letters lodged with UN, howitzer spotted
item.description: Tensions between North Korea and South Korea are running high this week after Pyongyang sent a letter to the UN Security Council, repeating accusations that Seoul fabricated a September landmine incident, and after a North Korean howitzer was spotted close to the border.
item.dc:creator: Hongji Kim, Kyu-Seok Shim, Joyce Lee
item.content:encoded: Tensions between North Korea and South Korea are running high this week after Pyongyang sent a letter to the UN Security Council, repeating accusations that Seoul fabricated a September landmine incident, and after a North Korean howitzer was spotted close to the border. A Reuters witness at an observatory in South Korea overlooking the heavily armed border on Monday confirmed the presence of a North Korean artillery piece positioned in clear view near the frontier. South Korea's Yonhap news agency on Sunday identified the weapon as a self-propelled 122-mm howitzer, saying its deployment near the border marked a rare public display of such artillery. Reuters also observed three North Korean armored vehicles with their gun barrels pointed south, as well as about 20 to 30 North Korean soldiers carrying out fencing work inside the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ). "It is highly unusual (for North Korea) to expose its self-propelled artillery so conspicuously,” said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University in Seoul. "By deliberately displaying it, North Korea is signalling through action, not words, that it intends to enforce its border policy through force rather than dialogue or negotiation." It is also warning South Korea to exercise caution about escalating border friction, with the intention to prevent an accidental clash, he added. North Korean state media KCNA reported that in the letter sent on Sunday, the country's UN representative said Seoul was using the landmine incident to depict Pyongyang's border construction as a military incursion. North Korea warned in the letter that violations of its sovereignty could trigger self-defence measures and that South Korea would be "wholly accountable for all the ensuing consequences." PHOTOS ALSO SHOW NORTH KOREAN DRILLS The letter is a response to a South Korean letter to the Security Council last week, which said a September 21 blast in the DMZ was planted by North Korean troops and constituted a violation of the Korean War Armistice Agreement. The UN Command, which oversees the DMZ, has said a North Korean mine across the line violated the armistice. Pyongyang has denied responsibility. A spokesperson for South Korea's Unification Ministry said on Monday that the North Korean letter appears to repeat North Korea's existing position and seeks to justify its so-called border line marking work. The ministry had no separate comment on the placement of the howitzer. Seoul has [USN:L1N46905T TEXT:"proposed"] dialogue with North Korea to defuse border tensions. North Korea's letter also repeated accusations that South Korea had opened fire on North Korean personnel, calling that a violation of the UN Charter, which bars the threat or use of force against another state's territorial integrity. Seoul has said its military issues warning broadcasts and fires warning shots to send North Korean soldiers back across the line when they cross the military demarcation line (MDL), which bisects the DMZ. North Korean troops have been building tactical roads and fences and laying mines near the MDL in recent years. The Yonhap report cited photographs taken from an observatory in the South Korean border city of Gimpo that appeared to show the howitzer as well as North Korean troops conducting drills on the coast of Kaepung county, about 1.5 km (1 mile) from the observatory. In 2015, there was a similar incident in which South Korean troops were injured by North Korean mines. Then, Seoul resumed anti-North Korea loudspeaker broadcasts across the DMZ, triggering a military standoff. After North Korea expressed regret, the standoff ended with a high-level inter-Korean agreement.

item.title: NFL roundup: Falcons harass 49ers into first loss of 2026
item.description: Michael Penix Jr. threw for three touchdowns and the Atlanta Falcons' defense forced four turnovers as they claimed a 29-20 victory on Sunday afternoon to hand the visiting San Francisco 49ers their first loss.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Michael Penix Jr. threw for three touchdowns and the Atlanta Falcons' defense forced four turnovers as they claimed a 29-20 victory on Sunday afternoon to hand the visiting San Francisco 49ers their first loss. Penix completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards while rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels picked off a pass and recovered a fumble in the fourth quarter for the Falcons (3-4), who won their first home game of the season. Nick Folk added three field goals. Brock Purdy hit 27 of 40 passes for 288 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions for the 49ers (6-1). Christian McCaffrey rushed for 39 yards and one touchdown while catching six passes for 61 yards. The 49ers built a 14-3 lead on Kaelon Black's 30-yard touchdown run on the first play of the second quarter, but the Falcons responded with 23 unanswered points as Penix completed touchdown strikes to Nick Muse, Kyle Pitts Sr. and Drake London. Seahawks 20, Chiefs 3 Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown and Emanuel Wilson rushed for 100 yards and a score as host Seattle defeated Kansas City, handing the Chiefs their first loss of the season. Wilson had 24 carries, including a 21-yard touchdown run around the left end with 3:47 remaining to clinch the victory for the defending Super Bowl champions. Sam Darnold completed 20 of 28 passes for 257 yards with one touchdown and one interception for the Seahawks (4-3). NFL rushing leader Kenneth Walker III, who was the MVP of the Seahawks' 29-13 Super Bowl victory against New England before signing with Kansas City as a free agent in the offseason, was limited to 36 yards on 14 carries in his return to Seattle. Patrick Mahomes was 19-of-33 passing for 165 yards with an interception for the Chiefs (5-1), who had just 213 yards of total offense to the Seahawks' 410. Giants 27, Titans 21 (OT) Devin Singletary ran for a 30-yard touchdown to defeat his former team and propel New York to the walkoff victory over host Houston. J.J. McCarthy completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards to win his debut start for the Giants (4-2-1) and his fifth consecutive start overall. Cam Skattebo had 17 carries for 124 yards, including a 42-yard run the play before Singletary's game-winner, and Malik Nabers caught seven passes for 111 yards. C.J. Stroud completed 17 of 28 passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns for the Texans (2-5), who dropped to 0-4 at home. Woody Marks had 19 carries for 66 yards and tight end Dalton Schultz had five catches for 45 yards. Stroud's 3-yard touchdown pass to Xavier Hutchinson with 52 seconds left forced overtime. Steelers 16, Saints 10 Aaron Rodgers broke a tie with Peyton Manning on the all-time touchdown passes list, Jaylen Warren rushed for 101 yards and Pittsburgh defeated New Orleans in the first NFL game played in Paris. The Steelers (5-2) won their third straight game after shutting out the Saints (2-5) in the second half in Stade de France in Saint-Denis, just north of Paris. Rodgers broke a tie with Manning for third place on the all-time list when he completed his 540th career touchdown pass to Darnell Washington in the second quarter. Tyler Shough passed for 278 yards with a touchdown and an interception for the Saints, who rushed for just 18 yards -- 130 fewer than Pittsburgh. Browns 27, Titans 24 Cleveland kicker Andre Szmyt made up for an earlier miss by nailing the game-winner from 32 yards on the final play of a victory over Tennessee in Nashville. After Tennessee tied it 24-24 with 58 seconds remaining on Tony Pollard's third touchdown of the day, Deshaun Watson hit Harold Fannin Jr. for 36 yards with 28 seconds left. Szmyt, who missed from 43 yards in the fourth quarter, booted the winner to keep the Browns (5-2) atop the AFC North. Watson eclipsed 300 yards for the first time with the Browns as he completed 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards and an interception. He also rushed for a score. For the Titans (1-6), Pollard carried 25 times for 129 yards. Dolphins 28, Jets 25 Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes to rookie Caleb Douglas and ran for another to help Miami pick up its first win, beating New York in East Rutherford, N.J. Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards without an interception and rushed for 37 yards on eight attempts to help give head coach Jeff Hafley his first NFL victory. Ollie Gordon II ran for 103 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries as the Dolphins (1-5) rushed for 156 yards overall. The Jets (2-5) lost for the fifth time in six games and lost their eighth consecutive game against an AFC East opponent. Geno Smith completed 23 of 30 passes for 287 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. Smith's third touchdown pass was a 12-yarder to Mason Taylor, who caught five passes for 62 yards and two touchdowns. Buccaneers 43, Panthers 13 Bucky Irving rushed for 106 yards and two touchdowns, Calijah Kancey returned a fumble 32 yards for a touchdown and Tampa Bay blasted mistake-prone Carolina in Charlotte. Baker Mayfield was back at quarterback for the Buccaneers (2-5) after missing three games with a dislocated right thumb and had an easy return while completing 7 of 11 passes for 64 yards and one touchdown. The Panthers (3-3) committed four turnovers and missed an extra-point kick. Bryce Young was 14-of-27 passing for 163 yards with two interceptions and a touchdown, while losing a fumble. Vikings 16, Colts 10 Kyler Murray passed for 150 yards and a touchdown, and safety Harrison Smith made an interception in the final minutes to preserve a Minnesota victory over Indianapolis in Minneapolis. T.J. Hockenson had the go-ahead touchdown catch for the Vikings (6-0) early in the fourth quarter. Jordan Mason had a team-high 68 rushing yards, and Justin Jefferson caught four passes for 44 yards on seven targets. Will Reichard made three of four field goal attempts. Jonathan Taylor rushed for 95 yards and a touchdown to lead the Colts (2-5). Daniel Jones completed 13 of 22 yards for 108 yards and an interception. Indianapolis fell despite converting 9-of-16 third- and fourth-down chances. Bengals 35, Ravens 13 Joe Burrow threw four second-half touchdown passes and Cincinnati scored 35 unanswered points to record a victory over host Baltimore. Burrow completed 16 of 18 passes for 249 yards while leading five touchdown drives in the half as the Bengals (4-2) overcame a 13-0 halftime deficit. Tee Higgins caught six passes for 148 yards and a touchdown. Ja'Marr Chase, Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample also caught touchdown passes and Samaje Perine rushed for a score. Lamar Jackson (ankle) missed his third straight game for the Ravens (4-3). Tyler "Snoop" Huntley completed 23 of 34 passes for a career-high 298 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Zay Flowers had eight catches for 137 yards and one score for Baltimore, which blew a double-digit lead for the second straight week. Broncos 30, Cardinals 16 Bo Nix threw a touchdown pass and ran 62 yards for another, J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey also scored TDs, and Denver topped Arizona in Glendale, Ariz. Nix finished 15-for-29 passing for 222 yards and also rushed for 73 yards for the Broncos (5-2), who have won three in a row and won three of four games against NFC West opponents. Jacoby Brissett finished 27-for-48 passing for 272 yards and a touchdown pass to Trey McBride, who had 10 receptions for 111 yards for the Cardinals. Arizona (2-5) has lost 10 straight home games dating back to Sept. 14, 2025. Rams 35, Raiders 21 Matthew Stafford threw for three touchdowns and visiting Los Angeles built a 28-3 second-quarter lead on its way to victory against slumping Las Vegas. Stafford completed 23 of 29 passes for 195 yards and an interception as the Rams (3-4) snapped a two-game losing streak. Kyren Williams (16 rushes, 99 yards) and Blake Corum (17 attempts, 93 yards) each scored a touchdown and contributed to Los Angeles' 386 yards of offense. Kirk Cousins hit 26 of 44 throws for 295 yards and two touchdowns, but it wasn't enough as the Raiders (3-4) dropped their fourth straight game. Las Vegas managed just 48 yards on 17 carries and abandoned the run for most of the second half. Lions 20, Packers 17 Jake Bates kicked a 22-yard field goal as time expired to give host Detroit a victory over Green Bay and snap the Packers' three-game winning streak. The Lions' Jared Goff passed for 303 yards and two touchdowns, both to Jameson Williams. Amon-Ra St. Brown caught nine passes for 153 yards and Williams hauled in five for 91 yards. Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 116 yards on 29 carries for Detroit (4-2). Jordan Love passed for 274 yards, two touchdowns and one interception for Green Bay (4-3). Running back Josh Jacobs, activated off the NFL commissioner's exempt list, rushed for 36 yards and caught five passes for 55 yards and a touchdown in his season debut. --Field Level Media --Field Level Media

item.title: Antonelli wins US Grand Prix but must wait for title
item.description: Kimi Antonelli stands on the brink of becoming Formula One's youngest ever champion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kimi Antonelli delivered a dominant US Grand Prix victory for Mercedes on Sunday to stand on the brink of becoming Formula One's youngest ever champion with four rounds to spare in Mexico next weekend. The 20-year-old Italian did all he could to put the championship out of reach of his rivals in Texas but Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Mercedes teammate George Russell did just enough to delay the inevitable with fourth and eighth respectively. Antonelli now needs to score only two points -- a ninth place -- in Mexico City to be sure of the title even if Russell wins. "It was the result we needed and the whole team deserve it so much," he said of his first win since Spain last month. "I know we're very close. We try to finish on a high and hopefully we can clinch it very soon". LECLERC SECOND AND VERSTAPPEN THIRD Ferrari's Charles Leclerc finished second, 13.078 seconds behind, in Sunday's race at Austin's Circuit of the Americas with Red Bull's Max Verstappen third and helped by a late virtual safety car that slowed a chasing Hamilton who finished one second down the road. The win from pole position on a one-stop strategy was Antonelli's ninth in of the season and he now leads Russell by 123 points, and Hamilton by 124 with a maximum 125 remaining to be won and that reducing to 100 after Mexico. "The main headline is that for me (it is) the best race he's delivered so far," said Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff. "The race of a champion who isn't the champion yet, but exceptional". McLaren's reigning champion Lando Norris finished fifth on a one stop strategy after being passed by both Verstappen and Leclerc on lap 47 of 56 with his tyres struggling. Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was sixth, and ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri. Liam Lawson was ninth for Racing Bulls and Pierre Gasly took the final point for Alpine. Antonelli made a flying getaway and was 2.3 seconds clear at the end of the opening lap while the Ferrari pair took the fight to slow-starting Verstappen for second place. Leclerc went ahead, before being passed again by the Red Bull, and nearly made contact with Hamilton after the uphill scramble off the grid. The virtual safety car was briefly deployed on lap two to allow marshals to clear debris and Russell, who had started sixth, had to serve a five second penalty at his sole stop after stewards ruled he had gained an advantage on Piastri on the opening lap at Turn 13. Russell was then unable to find a way past the McLaren. "Six good laps, 50 bad laps," he said of his race. "I want to understand why the pace was so bad on the first stint. The penalty was a bit ridiculous as well, but that's the least of my worries after such a bad weekend. "For me, as long as we're in the constructors' (lead), that's the main thing. Obviously I'd like to finish best of the rest, but P2, P3, P5 is not champion, so it doesn't mean anything." Haas's Ollie Bearman also collected a 10 second penalty for causing a collision with Gasly and retired at the half-distance.
